The 2003-02-10 bout, KSZ vs Topex, dates the actual turnover in its own retrospective prose: "He had beaten Jeff Garvin on Whatever for it just a few days before, going the entire fifteen minutes and winning it back with a 450 Splash just seconds before the time limit expired." "Whatever" bookings in the window: Whatever 6 (2003-01-17) is already accounted for above (action-tv-001's defence); Whatever 7 (2003-02-07) is one of the fed's own 16 honest-absence shows (marked "Not located") -- so the match this quote describes almost certainly IS Whatever 7, but no card text survives to confirm the date to the day. Filed at won_precision 'circa' on the next reign (action-tv-003) rather than resolved here. No defence text survives for this reign.

lost.source: The fed's write-up of Courage 16; the fed's own belt page lists the change.

reigns.note: ICU hit Aaron Ward with Critical Condition and pinned him to become the first Television Champion of the televised era. Defences on record. breakOUT 2002, 10 November 2002: ICU kicked Ron Williams low, then climbed the ropes and pulled the chicken down from its peg to retain the Television Title in the Chicken on a Pole match. End Game 2002, 22 December 2002: ICU retained the Television Title by pinning ToK after ToK slid out of Critical Condition and ICU hit him with the Depression clothesline.

Apocalypse 2003, 16 February 2003: Scott Perry retained the Television Title over Alias when the referee, who had been knocked down during Osyrus and Ethan Winters' interference, recovered and counted the three.

reigns.title: acw-television
reigns.label: Alias

won.source: Courage, 16 March 2003: Alias knocks out Scott Perry with Anarchy's Lullaby and "Alias was now ACW's Television Champion" ("Winner: Alias"). The show falls seven days before Legends on 23 March 2003, and a later Courage names it "the March 16 2003 edition of Courage"; the fed's belt page dates the win 9 March 2003, a week early.

reigns.how: Won on the Courage of 16 March 2003, when the referee stopped the match with the champion caught in Anarchy's Lullaby.
reigns.note: Glory's own text: "The Television Title had been vacated since June 1st when Alias ended his reign as the champion." The fed's belt page dates the win 9 March 2003 and counts 84 days to that vacancy; the show carrying the win falls a week later, on 16 March, which makes the reign 77 days. On 1 June Alias hands the belt across SilverHAWK's desk; SilverHAWK does not become champion. Alias's own card (captured 3 November 2005) also counts the reign at 84 days ("undefeated; 84 day reign"), the belt page's count.

reigns.title: acw-television
reigns.label: Quinton May

won.source: Glory: "Winner and NEW ACW TELEVISION CHAMPION: Quinton May".

lost.source: The fed's own belt-history page vacates the title on 7 December 2003: the television deal fell through and ACW folded.

reigns.how: Won the battle royal for the vacant championship at Glory.
reigns.note: Defended against Drake Nefarian on Courage 33 (13 July 2003), "Ego" Greg Davis on Courage 34 (20 July), Vince Jacobs on Courage 36 (10 August), Vincent Pembridge at King of Ages (7 September, in a triple header that put the Scorpion Fighting Championship up too) and Elijah Arson on Courage 39 (21 September). The fed's belt page ends the reign on 7 December 2003, when ACW folded.

reigns.title: acw-television

won.source: Courage 44 (8 April 2004): a ladder match against Phil Atken for the vacant championship, the belt retrieved — "WINNER : Quinton May, new ACW Television Champion." The fed's belt page dates the reign from "08 04 2003", a slip for 2004 (182 days to 7 October 2004).

reigns.how: Won a ladder match against Phil Atken for the vacant championship.
reigns.note: First defence on Courage 45 (15 April 2004) over Bantam Diablo, the same night as his Scorpion Fighting defence; defended over Lancett on Courage 48 and against Fejona Min and Natalie Quinston at King of Ages 2004. Fejona Min took the belt from him on 7 October 2004.

reigns.how: Beat Quinton May in a match that put her Scorpion Fighting Championship on the line against his Television Championship.
reigns.note: breakOUT's own text says the two belts "had been unified. There simply weren't enough fighters in ACW to warrant the latter", and has her walk out carrying only the Television title.

won.source: breakOUT 2005: "Winner > Seymour Almasy" in the ACW Television Championship three-way (3317 u15 ¶755-765); the fed's own belt-history page: "BREAKOUT 2005 / 06 02 2005 / Seymour Almasy".

lost.source: Courage 79: Andy Sharp pins him with The Sharper Image, "Winner and NEW ACW Television Champion > Andy Sharp" (3328 u4 ¶136-154). The fed's own belt page dates the change "COURAGE 79 / 08 09 2005"; Argyle's booking record estimates the card at 4 August 2005. Both readings stand.

reigns.how: Submitted champion Fejona Min with an ankle lock in a three-way, after putting Kelly Flawless off the top rope to the floor. His first championship in ACW.
reigns.note: Defended against Kelly Flawless on Courage 70, against Violence Jack (a time-limit draw) and Sars on Courage 73, at End Game 2005 (where he kept it by pinning Max Danger, the last man in the five-way), against Aerith Heartilly on Courage 77 and against Rook Black on Courage 78. Andy Sharp pinned him for it on Courage 79; he did not move after the pin and was carried out.

reigns.title: acw-television

won.source: Courage 79: Andy Sharp pins the champion with The Sharper Image and wins the Television title ("Winner and NEW ACW Television Champion > Andy Sharp"). The fed's belt page dates the change 8 September 2005; the card itself carries no dateline.

reigns.how: The record does not hold the match he won it in.
reigns.note: Legends II retires the championship from the stage while he is holding it: "He was looking down at his now defunct TV title. He would be the last in a long storied list of champions."

Final score: Shame 2, Nightshade 3, Savage Warrior 2, Chaos 2 — the winning fall a rollup on Shame while Warrior was still recovering.

Triangles 2005, 11 November 2005: Mike Wade kept the Relentless Championship at the top of the pyramid when the clock ran out in the Pyramid Scramble; Chainz, who held a Sharpshooter on Alexa Kendericks through the buzzer, was named the new number one contender. Fresh!, 6 December 2005: Mike Wade hit Hate with the TFW onto a steel chair and pinned him to retain the Relentless Championship. Winter Warfare 2005, 23 December 2005: Mike Wade clubbed Chainz on the back of the head with his mouth over the cup and filled it with his blood to win the Cup Of Blood match and retain the Relentless Championship. Bloodlust 2006, 17 February 2006: Mike Wade hit Paddy O'Shea with the TFW off the top rope onto the ring steps, then dragged him into the ring and pinned him in a Loser Leaves Town match, retaining the Relentless Championship and ending O'Shea's AWC contract. Mike Wade laid the Relentless Championship in the centre of the ring, held up his Triangles briefcase and said he would use it on Jack Murphy for the Transatlantic title; there was no match.

Fresh!, 16 May 2006: Red Rock wrapped a chain around Anton Assault's neck and swung him down head first with the RDT, then pinned him to retain the Relentless Championship. Fresh!special: Day Of The Devil, 6 June 2006: Red Rock pinned Chainz with a roll-up out of a sunset flip counter to retain the Relentless Championship in the Double Dog-Collar match, and Chainz caned him afterwards. Divide And Conquer 2006 (pay-per-view), 23 June 2006: Red Rock hit Jack Murphy with a kendo stick, landed a body splash from the top of a ladder and pulled him into a pin by his knee pad to retain the Relentless Championship. Fresh!special: Live On Huntington Beach, 1 August 2006: Red Rock hit Aimz with a rolling spinning heel kick and the Elevated Inverted DDT, the RDT, after a barbed wire bat match and pinned her to retain the Relentless Championship.

Jack Murphy kicked Aimz off Adam Dick in the middle of a pin, then hit Dick with the Fall From Grace and pinned him to win the Transatlantic Championship at Bloodlust; Dick's crown is not part of the finish. The fed's own title history has no vacancy (Adam Dick from 17 January to 1 September 2006, with Pierce Lavelle's third reign from 1 August concurrent); the write-up has Dick throw the belt down on 4 July 2006 and the belt left vacant. Adam Dick lifted Jack Murphy and dropped him on his head with Murphy's own Fall From Grace and pinned him to win the Transatlantic Championship; James Brunt refused to announce it. Defences on record. Fresh!, 9 May 2006: Adam Dick faked an injury after falling out of the ring, kicked out of Darcy Crisis's pin and hit the Eaterplex '05 to pin him and retain the Transatlantic Championship. Divide And Conquer 2006 (pay-per-view), 23 June 2006: Adam Dick hit Mike Wade with the Finger Poke Of Doom and covered him, and the two Unfuckables embraced after the count; Pearl then sent Michael Ryan home and ordered the match run again with Jack Murphy as referee. Divide And Conquer 2006 (pay-per-view), 23 June 2006: Mike Wade kicked out of Adam Dick's Eaterplex '05, then Dick reversed Wade's roll-up into a pin, with Jack Murphy as referee, to keep the Transatlantic Championship. Adam Dick threw the Transatlantic belt on the ground in front of Pearl and kept the crown as his own; the belt was left vacant and there was no match.

reigns.title: ccw-classic-1996-international

The Explosion!! promo of 25 March 1997 (3m9r_eoKeP0J) still has Warden holding the gold. No surviving document records the night or the match.

reigns.how: Took the title from Bradley Warden; the night and the match are not recorded.

reigns.title: chz-heavyweight
reigns.label: Staz

won.source: The fed's own title history (CHZ WILD), /promotions/chz/archive/heavyweight-title-history.html.

reigns.how: Defeated Kris Snyder with the help of his old ally The Count.

lost.source: The fed's own title history, /promotions/chz/archive/heavyweight-title-history.html. Also: The fed's own news archive: "Staz was last mentioned in the CHZ when he fled the country with the World Title belt, leaving many people wondering what the heck was going on. This later resulted in the World title being vacant for 6 months" (promotions/chz/archive/news-archive-2002.html, 5 February 2002 item); The Count's own 12 December 2001 promo independently corroborates Staz's disappearance: "World Champion oneday, the next not even listed on the roster" (promotions/chz/archive/wild-2001-12-12.html).

reigns.note: Vacated by forfeiture rather than lost in a match — Staz left the promotion (and the country) with the title itself. The six-month vacancy the news archive describes runs into the Matt Helms reign below. The fed's own title history adds that Cellrock hunted Staz down and retrieved the belt, and that it stayed vacant for five months.

reigns.title: chz-heavyweight

won.source: The fed's own title history (CHZ PPV Caged Fury 2), /promotions/chz/archive/heavyweight-title-history.html. Also: The title was vacant on the fed's own 22 December 2001 champions snapshot (promotions/chz/archive/champions-2001.html); the fed's own news archive, 5 February 2002 item, reports Helms "crowned the World Champion at Caged Fury" after the six-month Staz vacancy, and a separate 8 February 2002 column recalls him having "ousted 3 others in a fight for his life" for it (promotions/chz/archive/news-archive-2002.html, news-2002.html). Caged Fury's own front-page posting dates it to 30 January 2002 ("Chazy2Cool Vs JT Fringe (Caged Fury Jan 30)", promotions/chz/archive/front-page-2002-02.html).

reigns.how: Beat Diablo in cage one, where the winner had to handcuff his opponent and leave the cage, then the three other finalists — Don Rossi, The Count and Chazzy 2 Cool — in the center cage.
reigns.note: Defended against Brent Brewer at No Luv on 27 February 2002 ("AND HELMS RETAINS HIS TITLE!!!!", /promotions/chz/archive/no-luv-2002-02-27.html) and was billed holding "his golden World Title" on the 20 February 2002 Wild (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-02-20.html); also billed champion on 22 March 2002 and into the unaired NBK Pride main event against Keyser Soze — no result for that match survives anywhere held.

reigns.how: Won the World title at Caged Fury 2; the held shows show him defending it only as a champion.

reigns.note: On 21 May 2003 Drayton MacPhereson's pin is counted by a second referee, and Keyser Soze rules that the count does not stand; the first referee raises Manback's hand.

The fed's own title history dates his win to 9 November 2001, over Don Rossi.

The 21 September 2001 Friday Night Wild stages Santos retaining against Gazz "TNT" Maybury that night; the 9 November 2001 Friday Night Wild stages Santos making Helms tap to the DragonSlayer to retain; and the 12 December 2001 Wild stages Helms winning the title from Brian Nash after Santos "RETIRED EARLY".

lost.source: The change is in no show: the 23 January 2002 Wednesday Night Wild introduces the Disciples of Thunder as "the reigning CHZ Tag Team Champions" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-01-23.html), while the Sons of Thunder appear that night with Simon but not as champions; the fed's 22 December 2001 champions snapshot still lists the Sons (/promotions/chz/archive/champions-2001.html).

reigns.note: The 9 November 2001 Friday Night Wild stages the win, a tables match over Hell's Fury, and names the Sons of Thunder James and John, managed by Simon (/promotions/chz/archive/fnw-2001-11-09.html); the 14 November 2001 house show and the fed's 22 December 2001 champions snapshot call the reigning champions Son's / Sons of Thunder. By the 23 January 2002 Wednesday Night Wild the reigning CHZ Tag Team Champions are the Disciples of Thunder, Atlas and Mountain ("STILL CHZ TAG TEAM CHAMPIONS…..DOT!!", /promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2002-01-23.html); no show records the change, so this reign ends at an unrecorded change before 23 January 2002 and the Disciples' reign opens at the first show that bills them champions. Sources disagree: the fed's own title history (/promotions/chz/archive/tag-team-title-history.html) gives the Disciples of Thunder (2) one reign from 9 November 2001 to 1 March 2002, the night the show gives to the Sons.

won.source: Genocide's own Women's title gauntlet: Syd Ashley pins Faith after the Air Canada.

reigns.how: Won the gauntlet match, the last to enter, from the champion Faith.
reigns.note: Ultimate Chaos bills her as the former Women's champion; the match in which she lost it is not in the surviving record.

reigns.title: cwf-chaotic-womens
reigns.label: Faith

won.source: Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007) bills Faith as the Women's champion, and Syd Ashley as the former champion; the night Faith regained it between those two broadcasts is not in the surviving record.

reigns.how: Champion again on the last broadcast.

reigns.title: cwf-chaotic-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Priest

won.source: Champion on both Genocide (22 October 2006) and Ultimate Chaos (3 April 2007). Ultimate Chaos says both that he has held it since winning it from the Suntan Superman 'last May' and that he has carried the belt 'since September'; Genocide says X-Factor took it from him at Bloodbath and he is champion again.

reigns.how: Kept the title against X-Factor at Genocide and against John Thomas at Ultimate Chaos.
reigns.note: The broadcasts give two starting points for this reign, May and September, with X-Factor's title win at Bloodbath between them; no date is filed.

reigns.title: cwf-continental-hardcore
reigns.label: Mike Maddness

won.source: No document records exactly when Mike Maddness won the CWF Hardcore Championship, but the corpus bounds it tightly: the fed's own served Friday Night Blitz broadcast (18 January 2002) has him winning only the #1 CONTENDERSHIP for the belt, beating Xtreme T through a trash can -- meaning he was not yet champion that night. The fed's own served "Babylon" results (25 January 2002) already bill him as champion, defending successfully against eXodus. The title changed hands, off-page and unrecorded, sometime in the seven days between the two shows; the Title Histories page's own "n/a" former-champion listing is consistent with the vacant belt simply being awarded to the newly-earned #1 contender rather than won in a documented match.

reigns.how: Earned the #1 contendership by beating Xtreme T through a trash can at Friday Night Blitz (18 January 2002); became champion off-page sometime in the following week, no document recording how. Successfully defended against eXodus at 'Babylon' (25 January 2002).
reigns.note: No linked event: the reign's own won date is unknown, and the linked Babylon show only captures a defense, not the winning of the title, so the ambiguity is left recorded rather than resolved.

end.source: The fed's own served "Babylon" results page: "Apocalypse defeats Dr. Doom & Kula" for the Television Championship, a triple-threat No Disqualification main event.

reigns.how: Won a No Disqualification title match; the belt's own founding reign in the held record.

won.source: PTC News, 2 December 2003 (promotions/ptc/archive/news-2003-12.html): "Can Saij continue his run of form that led to him winning the Chris Williams Memorial Cup?" — the tournament's own conclusion, recapped from a fourth promotion's vantage.

conflict.reading_a: PTC's own contemporary news of 2 December 2003 reports Saij winning the Cup that year — the only dated winner the surviving record confirms.
conflict.reading_b: Jay Phoenix's own PCW biography card (promotions/pcw/archive/jay-phoenix-bio.html) and PRIME biography card instead claim a Chris Williams Memorial Cup championship of his own, the PCW card dating it "2003" under a PWW heading. PRIME's ReVolution 197 (17 June 2009, an in-fiction interview question) and SCCW's own match-segment 20053 (8 March 2009, his entrance video) separately bill him a two-time Cup winner. None of the three claims names a specific staging, an opponent, or a result any other federation's record corroborates.

reigns.title: dwo-heavyweight
reigns.label: AJ Trinidad

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — the fed's own news item of 10 June 2002 reaches him already champion ("Our heavyweight champion, AJ Trinidad", /promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-news-2002-05-to-06.html).

reigns.how: Not recovered. The Champions page still had John Miro on 8 June 2002 and the newsdesk had Trinidad on 10 June; no document held covers the change.
reigns.note: Still champion on 22 August 2002, when Mike Pizaz beat him in a non-title match on his own debut, and still defending it against Jackson Rust at the fed's own Blackshock afterwards.

reigns.title: dwo-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jackson Rust

won.source: The fed's own Travesty main event of October 2002, in which he is announced as "your winner and STILL DWO WORLD CHAMPION" after retaining against Adam Stryker (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2002-10-main-event.html).

reigns.how: Not recovered — the record reaches him already champion and watches him retain in an anything-goes match against Adam Stryker.
reigns.note: Chryste's own dialogue that autumn calls him "our best at the time". The belt is vacant by December, when the fed runs a World Title tournament to fill it; nothing held records how his reign ended.

reigns.title: dwo-heavyweight
reigns.label: Adam Stryker

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — the fed's own post-pay-per-view Travesty segment of 4 October 2002 has him carrying the belt and calling himself "Current WORLD Champion" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-news-2002-09-to-10.html).

reigns.how: Not recovered. The fed's own October 2002 main-event commentary refers back to "Stryker's last and only World Title match against AJ Trinidad".
reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE. The same fortnight has Adam Stryker carrying the World Title in one served segment and Jackson Rust defending it against him in another. Both are recorded; neither is picked, and no document held dates a change between them.

reigns.title: dwo-heavyweight
reigns.label: Kaiowas

won.source: The fed's own Christmas Chaos report: the World Title Tourney came down to Kaiowas against Julius Corbin, "to determine the new DWO World Champion, to be crowned at the next Travesty" (/promotions/dwo/archive/dwo-news-2002-12-to-2003-01.html); the fed's own news of 25 January 2003 calls him "our current DWO Heavyweight Champion".

reigns.how: Won the final of the DWO World Title tournament against Julius Corbin, at the Travesty following Christmas Chaos. He had beaten The Event and then Vash to reach it.
reigns.note: The tournament ran through December 2002 to fill the belt after Lexis Bane's own shutdown of the fed. He was booked to defend it against Rainer inside the Crimson Steel Cage at Lord of the Asylum: Crimson Dance on 31 January 2003; no account of that match survives.

reigns.title: dwo-heavyweight
reigns.label: Donny Diamond

won.source: Primetime Central's own New Era results, which stage the DWO World Heavyweight Title match on the alliance's own supercard and record Kaiowas losing it (/promotions/ptc/archive/new-era-2003-results.html).

reigns.how: def. Kaiowas (c) in the DWO Asylum, on Primetime Central's own New Era interfed supercard. He won the PTC Global Championship later the same night.
reigns.note: The only DWO title change anywhere in the record that is dated to the day, and the receipt for it is another promotion's. The show is Primetime Central's own canonical row; this reign references it rather than duplicating it. RESOLVED FURTHER: the reign ended in-fiction by Donny Diamond's own kayfabe death, revealed on the fed's own Travesty of 10 July 2003 — Damian and Samantha claim to have killed him at an LOA event the week before, taking his own pentagram necklace as a trophy and relaunching the Disciples of Darkness in his place. No card carrying the killing itself is held; see dwo-loa-donny-diamond-death-2003-07 (collected: false).

end.source: The fed's own Travesty of 10 July 2003 has Damian and Samantha reveal they killed Donny Diamond at a Lord of the Asylum event "the week before" (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-07-10.html).

reigns.title: dwo-heavyweight
reigns.label: Kaiowas

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — the fed's own Travesty of 10 July 2003 has its commentary call him "the DWO World Champion" in the middle of the non-title match he loses to Kai Shinobi (/promotions/dwo/archive/travesty-2003-07-10.html).

reigns.how: Not recovered. The record has him lose the belt on 20 April 2003 and hold it again by 10 July, with nothing held in between.
reigns.note: A second reign, recorded because the fed's own commentary states it plainly; how and when he regained the title is not in anything held. Donny Diamond's own reign is now known to have ended in his own kayfabe death rather than a lost match — see that row's own note — which explains why the belt was open, though not how or when Kaiowas specifically regained it. SOURCES DISAGREE, RECORDED HONESTLY: by 25 September 2003 Callisto Bane calls Donny Diamond the reigning Heavyweight Champion, meaning the belt changed hands from Kaiowas a second time — undated, unwitnessed in anything held, and never reconciled anywhere held with Damian and Samantha's own claim five weeks earlier to have killed Donny Diamond (dwo-travesty-2003-07-10). Recorded as a new reign rather than picked apart or resolved by guess.

end.source: Relentless, 25 September 2003, has Callisto Bane call Donny Diamond the reigning Heavyweight Champion, booking Damian against him for the belt at the coming pay-per-view (/promotions/dwo/archive/relentless-2003-09-25.html).

reigns.title: dwo-heavyweight
reigns.label: Donny Diamond

won.source: Undated in the surviving record — Relentless, 25 September 2003, has Callisto Bane call him the reigning Heavyweight Champion and book Damian against him for the belt at the coming pay-per-view (/promotions/dwo/archive/relentless-2003-09-25.html).

reigns.how: Not recovered. Regained the title from Kaiowas (dwo-heavyweight-r007) at some point between 10 July and 25 September 2003, with nothing held documenting the change.
reigns.note: A second reign, recorded because the fed's own commentary states it plainly. It is never reconciled anywhere held with Damian and Samantha's own claim five weeks earlier (dwo-travesty-2003-07-10) to have killed Donny Diamond — the museum records what each document says and picks no side. He is billed to defend against Damian at the coming pay-per-view, Lord of the Asylum: Descent into Darkness (dwo-descent-into-darkness-2003-09, collected: false); no result for that show survives.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-dudleyville-hardcore-tag-team
reigns.label: The Dudley Boyz (Bubba Ray and D-Von)

won.source: Declared by the Dudleyz themselves on Blood, Sweat and Beers the night after Summer Assylum, July 2007: the old World Tag Team Championships, renamed the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, with no match; the diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists the belt as "Dudley Boyz: 28 July 2007 - 24 August 2007 (Dudley Boyz debut titles on Blood, Sweat & Beers)" (in-game dates).

lost.source: The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) gives this date; the belt is lost in the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship Match at Heatwave (Friday, week 4, August 2007).

reigns.how: The Dudley Boyz's only reign in this range: they say on Blood, Sweat and Beers that the belts are the old World Tag Team Championships from when they dominated the division and that these are now the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, with the second generation of Dudleyz at their side; they make the first defence on Revolution in August, beating the bWo with a 3D on Hollywood Nova after Chessman and Oz hit the bWo with the belts, beat Balls & Axl with a 3D on Axl on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and are challenged by the Hardcore Innovators for Heatwave and by Los Guerreros. In August 2007 they keep the belts over Los Guerreros, the Samoan Gangstas and the Briscoe Boys, with their relatives' help; the Hardcore Innovators cane them after the last of these and walk off with the belts, and at Heatwave Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer win the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship Match, putting D-Von through a table with a Double DDT: the reign ends there.
reigns.note: The belt is the Dudleyz's own, made and named by them on screen; no match is wrestled for it. The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists it and dates this reign 28 July 2007 (the Saturday show the night after Summer Assylum) to 24 August 2007, Heatwave (Friday, week 4, August 2007), where the Hardcore Innovators win the belts.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-dudleyville-hardcore-tag-team
reigns.label: The Hardcore Innovators (Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer)

won.source: Won from the Dudley Boyz in the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship Match at Heatwave (Friday, week 4, August 2007), PDF p.1279: "We have new champions! We have new champions!"; the diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists the belt as "Hardcore Innovators (Cactus Jack & Tommy Dreamer: 24 August 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates).

lost.source: The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) gives this date, and the text agrees: the belts are lost in the Three Way Dance at Guilty As Charged (PDF p.1545).

reigns.how: Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer beat the Dudley Boyz for the belts at Heatwave: the Innovators cane the second generation of Dudleyz on the outside, Cactus Jack's Double Arm DDT catches Bubba Ray as he rebounds, Dreamer rakes D-Von's eye, and the two put D-Von through a table with a Double DDT before Cactus covers (1...2...3). Joey Styles says the Dudleyville Hardcore Championship has become the ECW Hardcore Championship, the diary's later previews call the belts the (newly rechristened) ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship, and the Whole F**kin' Show attack the new champions after the match. In September, with Beulah McGillicutty at their side, the Innovators ask the World Tag Team Champions for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz to crown the Undisputed Tag Team Champions; they are still the holders when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 the Innovators lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest when the Dudley Family run in; in October, with Beulah McGillicutty, they ask Paul Heyman for a Singapore Cane Match, and at Guilty As Charged they are eliminated in the Three Way Dance (Bubba Ray pins Tommy Dreamer, then Cactus Jack): the reign ends there, 26 October 2007, though they leave the arena with all four belts and take them again from ringside after beating the second generation of Dudleyz on Blood, Sweat and Beers.
reigns.note: The belt is the Dudleyz's own, made and named by them on screen and won from them here. The diary's own title history (PDF p.8) lists it and dates this reign 24 August 2007 (Heatwave) to 26 October 2007 (Guilty As Charged). The diary's text calls the belts the ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship after this match; the title's own page keeps the name the Dudleyz gave it.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-dudleyville-hardcore-tag-team
reigns.label: The Dudley Boyz (Bubba Ray and D-Von)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW/Dudleyville Hardcore Tag Team Championship, listed as "Dudley Boyz (2): 26 October 2007 - 30 November 2007" (in-game dates; PDF p.8); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1545, the Three Way Dance to unify the tag team championships

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the belt is unified with the World Tag Team Championship in the Undisputed Tag Team Championship Match at November To Remember XV (PDF pp.1706-1707).

reigns.how: The Dudley Boyz win the Three Way Dance at Guilty As Charged, which the card bills as the match 'to unify the tag team championships', and take back the Dudleyville belts from the Hardcore Innovators; the Innovators leave with the belts, and retrieve all four again on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In November 2007 Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match at November To Remember XV in which the Dudley Boyz and the Hardcore Innovators unify the tag titles. At November To Remember XV the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators and raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles; the Dudleyville belts are unified with the World Tag Team belts there, on the date (30 November 2007) the diary's history gives.
reigns.note: The history lists this belt separately and gives the reign as running to 30 November 2007, when it is 'unified with the World Tag Team Championship', and the text agrees: the unification is the Undisputed Tag Team Championship Match at November To Remember XV (PDF pp.1706-1707); the World Tag Team history treats the Dudley Boyz as holders of the undisputed titles from 26 October, and each history's date is filed in its own title.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
reigns.label: Vito Thomaselli

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "Vito Thomaselli: 5 November 2006 - 28 February 2007" (in-game dates).

lost.source: SOURCES DISAGREE: the text of the shows ends this reign at November To Remember (26 November 2006, the date the same history gives that card's tag-title change); the diary's own title history runs it to 28 February 2007. Both readings are recorded (see the note).

reigns.how: Vito Thomaselli's first reign in the diary's own history: he pins The Great Sasuke on F' The Mainstream in November after Chris Daniels' chair shot misses him, and keeps the belt on Revolution when a backslide from Daniels leaves both men's shoulders down. He loses the belt at November To Remember in the Stairway To Hell Match with Super Crazy, when Christopher Daniels hangs on to the belt's harness and drops to the floor with it.
reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE: the diary's own International All Action Championship history lists Vito Thomaselli as champion until 28 February 2007 and names no other holder; the text of the shows has Christopher Daniels take the belt from him at November To Remember (Friday, week 4, November, dated 26 November 2006 by the same history's tag-title entries). Both readings are recorded; the end date follows the text, where the belt changes hands.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
reigns.label: Christopher Daniels

won.source: SOURCES DISAGREE: the diary's own text has him win the Stairway To Hell Match at November To Remember (the card the same history's tag-title entries date 26 November 2006); the diary's International All Action Championship history omits this reign and runs Vito Thomaselli's to 28 February 2007. Both readings are recorded.

lost.source: The text of the shows ends this reign at Living Dangerously, and the diary's own history gives the same date, 28 February 2007, for CM Punk's win; the history names no holder between Vito Thomaselli and CM Punk, so it omits this reign (see the note).

reigns.how: Christopher Daniels's reign in the diary's own text: he hangs from the belt's harness after the ladder collapses at November To Remember and drops to the floor with the belt in the Stairway To Hell Match with Vito and Super Crazy, keeps it through December (a no contest with Jushin Lyger on Blood, Sweat and Beers when Michael Shane interferes), beats Michael Shane at Got Blood? with Angel's Wings, and is still champion in February 2007, when his Revolution defence against CM Punk ends in a no contest. At Living Dangerously, in the Triangle Match with Michael Shane and CM Punk, Raven hits him with a chair as he climbs to the top rope and Punk pins him for the belt.
reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE: the diary's own International All Action Championship history names no holder between Vito Thomaselli's win on 5 November 2006 and CM Punk's on 28 February 2007, but the text of the shows has Christopher Daniels hold the belt in between, from November To Remember until Living Dangerously, where Punk beats him for it, the date the history gives for Punk's win. Both readings are recorded; the reign's dates follow the text.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
reigns.label: CM Punk

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "CM Punk: 28 February 2007 - 29 September 2007" (in-game dates); the text of the shows agrees with that date for the win.

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date (a day after the date of the show, Friday, week 4, September 2007), and the text agrees: the loss is the International All Action Championship Match at Anarchy Rulz (PDF p.1419).

reigns.how: CM Punk's first reign in the diary's own history: he pins Christopher Daniels in the Triangle Match with Michael Shane at Living Dangerously after Raven hits Daniels with a chair, pins Daniels again with a low blow on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and attacks Lance Storm, who won an International All Action title shot in the Stairway To Hell match at Baptism Of Fire, and is still champion when the pages of April 2007 end. At Cyberslam he keeps the belt over Lance Storm in the No Way Out Match with a GTS, and at Hardcore Heaven he keeps it over Storm again with a GTS after Monsters Inc chokeslam Storm onto Abyss's knee; he is still champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end. On Revolution in June Punk knocks out Paul Burchill and Shane Douglas with the belt, and at Wrestlepalooza Vito Thomaselli turns on him with a chair; the belt is not defended in this range, and he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, having been powerbombed through a table by Vito at Summer Assylum. At Heatwave in August 2007 Punk hits Burchill with the belt and the new World Heavyweight Champion with a GTS; in September he defends it for the first time in months and keeps it over Lance Storm (a GTS), over Big Sasuke Cool (a GTS after Monsters Inc.'s interference) and over Eddie Guerrero (a GTS), and he is still champion when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end, with Vito Thomaselli booked against him at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Vito Thomaselli pins him with a Crucifix Roll-Up after a Springboard Somersault Plancha takes down Monsters Inc.: the reign ends there.
reigns.note: The diary's own history dates the win 28 February 2007 and the loss 29 September 2007, Anarchy Rulz (PDF p.1419), where Vito Thomaselli pins Punk with a Crucifix Roll-Up. The history names no holder between Vito Thomaselli and CM Punk, while the text of the shows has Christopher Daniels hold the belt in between (see his reign).

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
reigns.label: Vito Thomaselli

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "Vito Thomaselli (2): 29 September 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Anarchy Rulz, PDF p.1419: "He did it! He just outsmarted Punk!"

reigns.how: Vito Thomaselli beats CM Punk at Anarchy Rulz with a Crucifix Roll-Up after a Springboard Somersault Plancha takes down Monsters Inc., and Punk beats him down afterwards. He keeps it over Jushin Lyger with the Vito Driver on Revolution, and the feud turns personal: Punk hits him with a GTS, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers Vito answers by forcing beer and a cigarette on the straight-edge Punk. At Guilty As Charged, in the Last Man Standing Match, Punk and Monsters Inc. beat him down with GTSs, chair shots and Abyss's Black Hole Slam until referee Jim Molineaux stops the match and Bob Artese announces Punk the new champion.
reigns.note: The history dates the win 29 September 2007, a day after the show's date (the show is filed under Friday, week 4, September 2007); the history's dates are the ones filed.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
reigns.label: CM Punk

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "CM Punk (2): 26 October 2007 - 3 November 2007 (stripped of title)" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1555: "Your winner and NEW ECW International All Action Champion..."

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees that the belt is taken from Punk by security guards on Revolution, Monday, week 1, November 2007 (PDF p.1583).

reigns.how: Punk wins the Last Man Standing Match when referee Jim Molineaux stops it and keeps the belt on Blood, Sweat and Beers over Lance Storm with a GTS after eight minutes. On Revolution on the first Monday of November 2007 Paul Heyman has about fifteen security guards strip Punk of the belt ('That International All Action Title... it ain't yours anymore'), and starts a tournament for it among 'hard working, respectful talent': the reign ends there.
reigns.note: The history ends this reign on 3 November 2007 with the title stripped (it then lists the title vacant, 'to be awarded to winner of championship tournament'); the text agrees that Paul Heyman strips the belt on Revolution, Monday, week 1, November 2007 (PDF p.1583) and starts the International All Action Title Tournament, whose final is on the card of November To Remember XV; the history's date is the one filed.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-international-all-action
reigns.label: Ricky Marvin

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW International All Action Championship, listed as "Ricky Marvin: 30 November 2007 - present" (in-game dates); the text agrees: November To Remember XV, PDF p.1694: Marvin pins Slyk Tayshaun Dudley with a Shining Wizard, "it looks like we have our new International All Action Champion".

reigns.how: Ricky Marvin, the winner of the International All Action Title Tournament's semi-final over Excalibur, beats Slyk Tayshaun Dudley in the final at November To Remember XV: Slyk comes back in the fifth minute until Big Dick Jr. slides in and hits his cousin with a Total Penetration, and Marvin pins him with a Shining Wizard in a match the diary rates C-; he dances round the ring with the belt. The Code of Diminishing Extremes read on the Saturday show sets the title to lucha libre rules, a twenty count when a wrestler is outside the ring and victory on two falls out of three.
reigns.note: The history lists the reign as 'present', and the record of these pages ends with Marvin still the champion.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-lioness
reigns.label: Alexis Laree

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW Lioness Championship, listed as "Alexis Laree: 28 September 2007 - present (won a Lioness' Den Match to crown the first champion)" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Anarchy Rulz, PDF pp.1420-1421, the Lioness' Den Match

reigns.how: Alexis Laree wins the first Lioness' Den Match at Anarchy Rulz against Jazz and Kelly Thomaselli: Jazz kicks out of two Alexis Effects, hits her Fisherman Brainbuster on a chair, and Kelly Thomaselli breaks up the cover and hits Jazz with the chair; Alexis rolls Kelly up and hooks her tights for the three, and Joey Styles calls it 'underhanded'. She keeps the belt over Daizy Dudley on Blood, Sweat and Beers, over Beulah McGillicutty and Traci on Revolution and Blood, Sweat and Beers, and over Jazz at Guilty As Charged, when Nattie Neidhart, the 'anonymous blonde', runs in and the two hit a Double DDT; she is still the champion when the pages of October 2007 end. In November 2007 Jazz and Kelly Thomaselli beat Alexis and Nathalie in a Lioness Pack Match, Alexis jumps Kelly after Kelly beats Nathalie, and on the last Revolution before November To Remember XV Alexis pins Jazz in a non-title match after Nathalie hits Jazz with the belt and the two land a Double DDT onto it; Kelly then clears both with the belt and challenges for the title, and the diary's preview of the card bills Kelly Thomaselli against Alexis, the champion. At November To Remember XV Alexis beats Kelly Thomaselli in the Lioness match (the preview bills it with Alexis as the champion) with an Alexis Effect when Nathalie slides in with the Lioness belt and hits Kelly from behind, then Alexis and Nathalie beat Kelly down until Jazz clears them (C). On Revolution on the first Monday of December she beats Mika Akino with an Alexis Effect (D+) and on the Saturday show again (E+, 5:42); Kong, back 'from APW' with Prince Nana, then flattens her with a bodycheck and a Sit-out Powerbomb. The diary's next preview books Kong and Akino against Alexis and Nathalie in a Lioness Pack Match.
reigns.note: The history lists the reign as 'present', so no end date is filed: the diary's record ends with her still the champion.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Raven

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Raven (4): 23 November 2005 - 26 September 2006" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: Raven's fourth reign in the diary's own history and the one billed on Wrestlepalooza, where he beat Goldberg to keep the belt. It carries on through the pages of July to September 2006: Raven keeps it at Summer Assylum when Shawn Michaels interferes against Paul Burchill, and over Goliath at Heatwave. It ends at Anarchy Rulz on 26 September 2006 in the diary's own history, when Shawn Michaels superkicks Raven in a five-on-five brawl and pins him.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Shawn Michaels

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Shawn Michaels (2): 26 September 2006 - 28 October 2006" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: Shawn Michaels' second reign in the diary's own history: he superkicks Raven in a five-on-five brawl at Anarchy Rulz and pins him, and loses the belt at Guilty As Charged, where Stephanie Mcintosh lowblows him in the Triangle Match with Raven and Rob Van Dam and Raven pins him.
reigns.note: The diary's own title history dates the win 26 September 2006 and the loss 28 October 2006; the text places them at Anarchy Rulz and Guilty As Charged.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Raven

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Raven (5): 28 October 2006 - 29 December 2006" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: Raven's fifth reign in the diary's own history: he wins the Triangle Match at Guilty As Charged with a second Evenflow DDT after Stephanie Mcintosh lowblows Shawn Michaels, and presents the belt on the first Revolution of November. It ends at Masters Of Pain on 29 December 2006 in the diary's own history, when Sabu beats Raven for it with a Triple Jump Moonsault after Zakk Wylde punches the champion.
reigns.note: The diary's own history dates the end of this reign 29 December 2006; the text places the loss at Masters Of Pain (Friday, week 4, December).

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Sabu

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Sabu (5): 29 December 2006 - 29 February 2006" (in-game dates; the end as the history prints it is not a calendar date).

lost.source: The text of the shows has Raven beat Sabu on Blood, Sweat and Beers, the show after Living Dangerously; the diary's own title history prints the date as "29 February 2007", which is not a calendar date, so the end is filed at month precision.

reigns.how: Sabu's reign in the diary's own history: he wins the belt at Masters Of Pain from Raven with a Triple Jump Moonsault after Zakk Wylde punches the champion, is jumped by Cactus Jack backstage on Blood, Sweat and Beers, keeps the belt over Cactus Jack at Got Blood? with a modified Northern Lights Suplex and the Triple Jump Moonsault, and in February 2007 faces the challenge of Steve Austin, who saved him from Cactus Jack after the match. At Living Dangerously he keeps the belt over Steve Austin with an Atomic Arabian Skullcrusher through a table, and Raven then hits him with an Evenflow DDT; the next night on Blood, Sweat and Beers Raven beats him for the belt with Paul Burchill's and Goliath's help.
reigns.note: The diary's own title history prints this reign's end as "29 February 2007" (and its start line prints the year 2006 for the end), which is not a calendar date; the text places the loss on Blood, Sweat and Beers, the show after Living Dangerously, so the end is filed at month precision (February 2007).

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Raven

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Raven (6): 29 February 2007 - 1 October 2007" (in-game dates; 29 February 2007 is not a calendar date, so the win is filed at month precision, and the text puts it on Blood, Sweat and Beers, the show after Living Dangerously).

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the loss is the Monday Revolution of October's first week (PDF p.1448).

reigns.how: Raven's sixth reign in the diary's own history: he beats Sabu on the last Blood, Sweat and Beers of February 2007 with an Evenflow DDT after Paul Burchill hits Sabu in the face with the Television Title and Goliath knocks him off the ropes, re-forms the Nest by throwing Charlie Pag and Stephanie Mcintosh through ringside tables, keeps the belt against Shane Douglas at Baptism Of Fire on 29 March 2007 (with CM Punk's interference and three Evenflow DDTs, the last on a chair), which gives him Douglas's powers as commissioner, and is still champion when the pages of April 2007 end. At Cyberslam he keeps the belt over Rhino in the Steel Cage Match when Paul Burchill, the special referee, counts fast and calls a submission Rhino never gave, and Burchill then turns on him with a C-4; at Hardcore Heaven, in a match that is not for the title, he beats Burchill after CM Punk threatens to throw Kelly Thomaselli off the stage, and he is still champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end, with Owen Hart booked to challenge him at Wrestlepalooza and Bret Hart in a Triangle Match for the belt. At Wrestlepalooza Raven keeps the belt in the elimination Triangle Match when Bret and Owen Hart quarrel, Owen makes Bret tap to the Ankle Lock, and Raven hits Owen with the Raven Effect onto a chair; the giant in black, the mystery signing Mark Calaway, Chokeslams him, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman forces him into a non-title match with Vito Thomaselli, where Calaway's Chokeslam lets Vito pin him. At Summer Assylum he keeps the belt over Calaway when Rhino Gores Calaway and Raven covers, and he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with Vito Thomaselli asking Paul Heyman for the title match at Heatwave. At Heatwave in August 2007, in the Barbed Wire Cage Match Raven names, Vito Thomaselli beats him (Burchill's Corkscrew Cross Body from the top of the cage, then the Vito Driver) and is presented with the belt, but CM Punk hits Burchill with the International All Action belt and Vito with a GTS and carries the belt to Raven; on Blood, Sweat and Beers Raven reads out clause 17.2a of the contract (interference from any party voids any title change) and says the belt still belongs to him and that Vito was never champion. Rhino wins the first Buck Stops Here Match at Heatwave to become number one contender and is booked against Raven at Anarchy Rulz; Raven is still champion when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Raven beats Rhino with Mark Calaway's help (Calaway's Elevated Powerbomb and Chokeslam, and Raven pins Rhino) and is then chokeslammed by Calaway. On Revolution on 1 October 2007 Owen Hart makes him tap to the Sharpshooter after Chris Jericho's chair shot: the reign ends there.
reigns.note: The diary's own history gives this reign's start as "29 February 2007", which is not a calendar date, so the win is filed at month precision (the text places it the night after Living Dangerously); the history's end of 1 October 2007 is the Revolution of October's first week (PDF p.1448), where Owen Hart makes Raven tap.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Owen Hart

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Owen Hart: 1 October 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Revolution, Monday, week 1, October 2007, PDF p.1448: "WE HAVE A NEW CHAMPION! WE HAVE A NEW CHAMPION!"

reigns.how: Owen Hart beats Raven on Revolution, the first televised defence of the title since February: he reverses Raven's Evenflow DDT into a Northern Lights Suplex, clears The Nest with a chair, and when Chris Jericho slips in and hits Raven with a chair, locks in the Sharpshooter and Raven taps; referee John Finnegan hands him the belt and Owen weeps. Jericho challenges him on Blood, Sweat and Beers and Paul Heyman books a Number One Contender's Match; Owen is the special guest referee in the tag match of Mark Calaway and Rhino against Raven and Jericho, refuses to count Raven's pin, and saves Jericho from The Nest in the cage match. He has announced that he will retire after Guilty As Charged, and his last match there is the 30-minute Ultimate Submission Match against Jericho: Hart's Sharpshooter wins the first fall, Jericho's Liontamer the second, and Jericho's Sharpshooter the third, and with seconds left Hart reverses a Figure Four into a Sharpshooter; Jericho taps at 30:00 and John Finnegan rules that the tap came after the time limit, so Jericho is declared the champion and Hart hands him the belt.
reigns.note: The history's dates (1 October and 26 October 2007) are the ones filed, and the text agrees: Revolution is a Monday show (1 October 2007 was a Monday) and Guilty As Charged is dated 'the 26th day of October'.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Chris Jericho

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Chris Jericho (2): 26 October 2007 (10:54 pm) - 26 October 2007 (11:02 pm)" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1561: "Your winner and NEW Extreme Championship Wrestling World Heavyweight Champion... Chris Jericho!"

reigns.how: Jericho is declared champion at the end of the Ultimate Submission Match when referee John Finnegan rules that his tap came after the time limit; Owen Hart passes him the belt and raises his hand and the two hug. Raven slides in, boots Hart out of the ring and hits Jericho with a Raven Effect, then uses the Commissioner's right to book one match of his own at each pay-per-view: Raven versus Chris Jericho for the World Heavyweight Title; Raven covers Jericho and Finnegan counts three.
reigns.note: The history times the reign to the minute, 10:54 pm to 11:02 pm on 26 October 2007, so it lasts eight minutes (days: 0). The diary has the Commissioner's right to book a pay-per-view match stand as legitimate (p.1569, Don Callis: 'Raven's controversial reclaiming... was legitimate under promotional guidelines').

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Raven

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Raven (7): 26 October 2007 - 30 November 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1562: "Your winner and new seven-time ECW World Heavyweight Champion... Raven!"

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the loss is the Loser Leaves ECW Match at November To Remember XV (PDF p.1721).

reigns.how: Raven pins Jericho with the Commissioner's match and leaves with the belt as fans throw rubbish into the ring. On Blood, Sweat and Beers Don Callis apologises on the company's behalf and says that the win was legitimate under the promotional guidelines; the company's owner then returns, strips Raven of his powers as Commissioner, gives sole booking power to Paul Heyman and books Raven's defence at November To Remember XV against Paul Burchill: 'The natural order has been restored.' Raven is still the champion when the pages of October 2007 end. In November 2007 Paul Heyman, back in power, tells Raven on Revolution that nobody in the arena is comfortable seeing him as the champion and that Paul Burchill will beat him at November To Remember; Burchill, Vito Thomaselli and Chris Jericho beat members of Raven's Nest on Revolution and on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers Heyman makes the title match a Loser Leaves ECW Match, with anyone outside it who touches either man to be fired and barred from signing with the Federation, and says that the man who stays will be the Undisputed ECW World Heavyweight Champion. Raven is still the champion when the diary's preview of the card ends. Raven loses the Loser Leaves ECW Match to Paul Burchill at November To Remember XV (PDF p.1721) after a contest the diary rates A*: Burchill's C-4 from the top rope and a Shooting Star Press end the reign, and Raven, kneeling in the aisle, is out of ECW (the diary's next preview: 'Never again will Raven be seen in an ECW ring').
reigns.note: The history ends this reign on 30 November 2007, and the text agrees: the loss is the Loser Leaves ECW Match at November To Remember XV (Friday, week 4, November 2007, PDF p.1721); the history's date is the one filed.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Paul Burchill

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the ECW World Heavyweight Championship, listed as "Paul Burchill: 30 November 2007 - present" (in-game dates); the text agrees: November To Remember XV, PDF p.1721: "Your winner and NEW ECW World Heavyweight Champion... 'The New Franchise' Paul Burchill!"

reigns.how: Paul Burchill, entering behind Shane Douglas, Steven Regal, Vito and Kelly Thomaselli, pins Raven at November To Remember XV in the Loser Leaves ECW Match, in a contest with no interference allowed: Raven throws him from the crow's nest wall through two tables and hits the Raven Effect onto a chair, Burchill kicks out, hits a C-4 from the top rope and then a Shooting Star Press for the three, in a match the diary rates A*; Raven is out of ECW and Douglas raises the new champion's hand. Paul Heyman's Code of Diminishing Extremes, read on the Saturday show with Douglas, defends the title under modified British rules, twelve five-minute rounds on a two-out-of-three-falls basis with judges after an hour. Burchill beats CM Punk in a non-title match with a C-4 and a Moonsault after Sabu and The Sandman, 'ECW Enforcers', clear the Nest; on Revolution on the first Monday of December he and Vito Thomaselli beat Punk and Goliath by disqualification, Rhino gores him on that show and again on the Saturday show, where Rhino beats Vito in a number one contendership match and earns the title match at Masters of Pain.
reigns.note: The history lists the reign as 'present', and the record of these pages ends with Burchill still the champion and Rhino the number one contender for Masters of Pain.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Dudley Boys

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "Dudley Boyz (8): 23 May 2006 - 2 August 2006" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: The Dudley Boys' eighth reign in the diary's own history, defended against the Hardy Boys on the first and eighth shows. The diary's text has the Hardy Boys win the belts on the first show of July and the Dudley Boys regain them in August, which the title history does not list.
reigns.note: The diary's own title history gives this reign as ending on 2 August 2006 with no reign for the Hardy Boys between; its text has the Hardy Boys take the belts on the first July show and the Dudley Boys win them back in August.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
reigns.label: New Age Enterprise (Raven and Paul Burchill)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "New Age Enterprise (Raven & Paul Burchill): 2 August 2006 - 9 August 2006" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: Raven and Paul Burchill's reign in the diary's own history, in the company of Charlie Pag: the diary's text has them beat the Dudley Boys for the belts on Revolution after Heatwave and lose them to Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova with Shawn Michaels' help.
reigns.note: The diary's own title history dates this reign 2 to 9 August 2006, but its text places the win after Heatwave, which the same history dates 30 August. The dates are the history's; the order of the shows is the text's.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
reigns.label: Blue World Order (Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "Blue World Order (2): 9 August 2006 - 28 October 2006" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: The second reign of the Blue World Order in the diary's own history: Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova beat Raven and Paul Burchill with Shawn Michaels' help on Revolution after Heatwave. It ends at Guilty As Charged, where Abyss and Goliath win the belts with a Double Chokeslam.
reigns.note: The diary's own title history dates this reign from 9 August 2006, but its text places the win after Heatwave, which the same history dates 30 August. The reign ends on 28 October 2006 in the diary's own history, which the text places at Guilty As Charged (Friday, week 4, October).

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
reigns.label: Monsters Inc. (Abyss and Goliath)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "Monsters Inc. (Abyss & Goliath): 28 October 2006 - 26 November 2006" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: Abyss and Goliath's reign in the diary's own history: they win the belts from the Blue World Order at Guilty As Charged with a Double Chokeslam and keep them on Revolution against the Dudley Boys, with Salvatore and Brandon's interference. It ends at November To Remember, where the Whole F**kin' Show win the belts with a 420 Splash on Abyss.
reigns.note: The diary's own history dates the end of this reign 26 November 2006; the text places the loss at November To Remember (Friday, week 4, November).

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Whole F**kin' Show (Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "The Whole F**kin' Show (Rob Van Dam & Shawn Michaels): 26 November 2006 - 28 February 2007" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: The Whole F**kin' Show's reign in the diary's own history: Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels win the belts from Monsters Inc. at November To Remember with the 420 Splash on Abyss, keep them against Monsters Inc. at Got Blood? and again on Revolution in February 2007, while their friendship strains over their manager Traci. They lose the belts at Living Dangerously, where Rob Van Dam steps off the apron and the Iron Saints pin Shawn Michaels with a Spike Powerbomb.
reigns.note: The diary's own history dates the end of this reign 28 February 2007; the text places the loss at Living Dangerously (Friday, week 4, February).

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Iron Saints (Salvatore and Brandon Thomaselli)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "Iron Saints (Salvatore and Brandon Thomaselli): 28 February 2007 - 29 March 2007" (in-game dates).

reigns.how: The Iron Saints' reign in the diary's own history: Salvatore and Brandon Thomaselli cash in their title shot at Living Dangerously and beat the Whole F**kin' Show for the belts with a Spike Powerbomb on Shawn Michaels after Rob Van Dam steps off the apron, keep them against Crouching Lyger Hidden Dragon on Blood, Sweat and Beers with the Canadian Connection's interference, and lose them at Baptism Of Fire in the first Halflife Handicap match.
reigns.note: The diary's own history dates the win 28 February 2007 and the loss 29 March 2007; the text places them at Living Dangerously (Friday, week 4, February) and at Baptism Of Fire (Friday, week 4, March).

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Whole F**kin' Show (Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "The Whole F**kin' Show (2): 29 March 2007 - 26 October 2007" (in-game dates).

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date, and the text agrees: the loss is the Three Way Dance at Guilty As Charged (PDF p.1545).

reigns.how: The Whole F**kin' Show's second reign in the diary's own history: Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels beat the Iron Saints at Baptism Of Fire in the first Halflife Handicap match, with Michaels's Sweet Chin Music and a Five Star Frog Splash on Salvatore, and are the champions when the pages of April 2007 end, with Rob Van Dam set to defend them while challenging Chris Jericho at Cyberslam. At Cyberslam they keep the belts over Los Increibles in the Ladder Match when Rob Van Dam pulls them down; at Hardcore Heaven Shawn Michaels, bloodied and alone while Van Dam helps Traci, keeps them over the Canadian Connection with a third Sweet Chin Music on Christian; the champions quarrel through June but are still champions when the pages of June 2007's second week end. At Wrestlepalooza they keep the belts over the Hardcore Innovators when Michaels's Diving Elbow and Van Dam's Five Star Frog Splash win simultaneous covers; the Dudley Boyz win the number one contendership on Blood, Sweat and Beers and, at Summer Assylum, the Whole F**kin' Show beat them in the Tables Match with Michaels's Sweet Chin Music through a table on D-Von; they are still champions when the pages of August 2007's first week end. After Heatwave the Whole F**kin' Show attack the new Dudleyville Hardcore Tag Team Champions, the Hardcore Innovators; in September they keep the belts over the Dudley Boyz on Revolution with simultaneous finishers, accept the Innovators' challenge for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz, quarrel after Shawn Michaels is caught covering Traci, and are still champions when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 they lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest after the Dudley Family run in; in October the partners quarrel over the stipulation for the Three Way Dance until Paul Heyman books ladders, chairs, canes and flaming tables, and at Guilty As Charged Shawn Michaels's Super Kick takes Rob Van Dam out of the air and Bubba Ray pins him: the reign ends there.
reigns.note: The diary's own history dates the win 29 March 2007 and the loss 26 October 2007, Guilty As Charged (PDF p.1545), where the Dudley Boyz pin Rob Van Dam after Shawn Michaels's Super Kick.

reigns.title: ecw-worldwide-nevermore-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Dudley Boyz (Bubba Ray and D-Von)

won.source: The diary's own opening pages: its title history for the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships, listed as "Dudley Boyz (9): 26 October 2007 - 4 November 2007" (in-game dates); the text agrees: Guilty As Charged, PDF p.1545: "The Dudley Boyz are the new unified tag champs..."

lost.source: The diary's own title history gives this date; the pages of November 2007 do not show the loss, and the diary's preview of November To Remember XV (PDF p.1676) bills the Dudley Boyz as the champions.

reigns.how: The Dudley Boyz win the Ladders, Chairs, Canes and Flaming Tables Three Way Dance for both sets of tag belts: Bubba Ray eliminates D-Von's opponents in turn, and when Shawn Michaels's Super Kick takes Rob Van Dam out of the air he pins Van Dam. The Hardcore Innovators then leave the arena with the belts, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers the Innovators beat the Second Generation of Dudleyz and take all four belts from ringside again. In November 2007 the Hardcore Innovators still walk to the ring with all four belts, and Bubba Ray and D-Von challenge them for a title match at November To Remember XV; on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match in which the Dudley Boyz and the Innovators unify the titles, and the diary's preview of the card bills the Dudley Boyz as the champions. At November To Remember XV (PDF pp.1706-1707) the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators, who carry both tag belts, in a weapons match with the Second Generation of Dudleyz and Daizy at ringside (a Superbomb through a table for Beulah McGillicutty, a Dudley Death Drop through a flaming table for Tommy Dreamer, B) and raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles. On Revolution on the first Monday of December they lose the Undisputed belts in a restarted Three Way Dance when Slyk Tayshaun Dudley makes Bubba Ray tap to the Boston Crabs.
reigns.note: The history ends this reign on 4 November 2007 and lists the Second Generation of Dudleyz (Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Slyk Tayshaun Dudley) as the champions from then, 'present'; the pages show something else: the Dudley Boyz beat the Hardcore Innovators at November To Remember XV (30 November), are called the first Undisputed ECW Tag Team Champions on the Saturday show and on Revolution, and lose the belts to Slyk and Dick Jr. on Revolution on the first Monday of December (PDF p.1747). The history's date is the one filed; the conflict is stated, not settled.

reigns.how: Slyk Tayshaun Dudley and Big Dick Dudley Jr. win the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles on Revolution on the first Monday of December: the Dudley Boyz's defence against Thomaselli-Thomaselli '08 becomes a brawl when Slyk comes in with a baseball bat and Dick Jr. with a chair, referee Jim Molineaux rules a no contest and the match is restarted as a Three Way Dance, The Sandman canes Dick Jr. and slides Slyk in, Dick Jr. hits Brandon with a Total Penetration, Slyk breaks up Bubba Ray's pin and puts Bubba in the Boston Crabs, and Bubba taps (B-). The Saturday show's backstage scene has the new champions with Daizy Dudley planning to use the belts as leverage over their uncles to learn the family secret; they beat Thomaselli-Thomaselli '08 in their first defence, Brandon tapping to the Boston Crabs while Dick Jr. covers Sal, and the recap has them keep the belts over Christopher Daniels and Tajiri despite in-fighting.
reigns.note: The history dates the win 4 November 2007 and lists the reign as 'present'; the text places the win on the first Monday of December, after the Dudley Boyz's own win of the unified belts at November To Remember XV. The dates are the history's; the order of the shows is the text's.

reigns.how: AJ Styles's first Television reign in the diary's own history: he debuts on Blood, Sweat and Beers in May 2007, turns on Rob Van Dam and Traci with the Canadian Connection and wins the belt at Hardcore Heaven; he beats Rey Mysterio Jr. with a low blow and a small package, takes a second defence on Revolution in June with an illegal use of the ropes, loses a non-title match to Juventud Guerrera, and is still champion when the pages of June 2007's second week end. On Revolution in June he beats Juventud Guerrera with a low blow and the Styles Clash, and at Wrestlepalooza he keeps the belt over Guerrera when Styles pushes Guerrera's foot off the rope before the Styles Clash is counted and Jim Molineaux does not see it; at Summer Assylum he keeps it again when Francine pretends to turn on Guerrera and Christopher Daniels, aligned with Styles, hits Guerrera with the belt; he is still champion when the pages of August 2007's first week end, with Guerrera's challenge for Heatwave on 28 August unanswered and Ultimo Dragon billed against him. At Heatwave in August 2007, in the Stairway To Hell Match, Styles keeps the belt over Juventud Guerrera, who loses his mask: it hangs from one hook and the belt from the other; on Blood, Sweat and Beers in September he keeps it again, beating Jerry Lynn with a roll-up after pointing at the entrance-way to make Lynn look for Kurt Angle; he is still champion when the pages of September 2007's fourth Monday end, with Ultimo Dragon booked against him at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Ultimo Dragon pins him with an Asai DDT after Styles drags Francine into the ring and Dragon cuts off a Styles Clash with an elbow: the reign ends there.
reigns.note: The diary's own history dates the win 29 May 2007 and the loss 28 September 2007, Anarchy Rulz (PDF p.1413), where Ultimo Dragon pins Styles with the Asai DDT.

He keeps it over Big Sasuke Cool (an Asai DDT) on Blood, Sweat and Beers, over Rey Mysterio Jr. on the second Revolution of October (an Asai DDT after Styles misses a springboard clothesline) and in a non-title match against Mysterio on the fourth (a Dragon Suplex after Francine distracts him), and accepts Styles's challenge, made by Francine, for Guilty As Charged. There the four-way Stairway To Hell Match ends his reign when Styles pulls the belt from the strap.
reigns.note: The history's dates (28 September and 26 October 2007) are the ones filed; the text of Anarchy Rulz and Guilty As Charged agrees.

reigns.how: Styles wins the four-way Stairway To Hell Match against Christopher Daniels, Rey Mysterio Jr. and the champion Ultimo Dragon: hanging from the strap that holds the belt alongside Dragon, he shifts his hands onto the belt and crashes to the canvas with it. Juventud Guerrera then runs in with a chair and hits all four men, signalling that he is coming for the belt. On Blood, Sweat and Beers on the first Saturday of November 2007 Styles keeps the title by pinning Juventud Guerrera with a Styles Clash while Guerrera's foot is on the rope and the referee misses it; Guerrera pulls him back through the ropes for a Juvi Driver, and Rey Mysterio Jr., Christopher Daniels and Ultimo Dragon run in and beat Guerrera down until Francine dives on top of him. Styles beats Mysterio with a Styles Clash on Revolution the following Monday, and on Revolution on the last Monday of the month Guerrera pins him in the rematch and wins the title: the reign ends there.
reigns.note: The history ends this reign on 26 November 2007, and the text agrees: the loss is the television title rematch on Revolution, Monday, week 4, November 2007 (PDF p.1662), the show before November To Remember XV; the history's date is the one filed.

reigns.label: Juventud Guerrera

He did it! Guerrera has his first ECW Gold!"

reigns.how: Juventud Guerrera pins AJ Styles on Revolution in the rematch that Paul Heyman has booked for the show before November To Remember XV: Guerrera hooks Styles for a Juvi Driver, Styles slips over his shoulder, Guerrera hits an Enziguiri and Styles climbs for a corkscrew leg drop, the Spiral Tap, but Guerrera hooks his leg and rolls through into a pin, for his first title in ECW. Ultimo Dragon, the number one contender after a three-way match on Blood, Sweat and Beers, appears at the entrance with Francine, points at her and then at his own waist, and the champion's first defence is the World Television Championship Match against him at November To Remember XV. Juventud Guerrera keeps the title at November To Remember XV over Ultimo Dragon, who pulls Francine into the champion's chair swing and later knocks Guerrera out with the belt; Francine breaks up the cover, lowblows Dragon and hits a DDT, and Guerrera hits a 450 Splash for the pin (B), receives the new belt from Jim Molineaux, and kisses Francine. On the Saturday show he beats The Great Sasuke with a Juvi Driver in the twelfth minute and, on Revolution on the first Monday of December, Eddie Guerrero with a Juvi Driver (B); the diary's next preview books him against Christopher Daniels.
reigns.note: The history lists the reign as 'present', and the pages through the first Saturday of December show the champion keeping the belt (the diary's own preview of November To Remember XV and its Saturday show call him a new champion, a week after the win on 26 November); no end date is filed, and the record of these pages ends with Guerrera still the champion.

reigns.how: Won the vacant-to-them title from Heat (Casino & Desperado) at Summer Sizzler 1997, 27 July — see r001a. The reign continued unbroken through Ultra Brawl II, 31 August 1997, where Knightquest pinned Effect to win a "Unification Match" over Cause & Effect (the EUWC North American Tag Team Champions, independently attested at Summer Sizzler the same night as r001a's win — see the companion new reign euwc-northamerican-tag-team-r002), absorbing that title's lineage into this one; the fed's own event-history page calls the Massacre, after this second match, the "Unified International Tag Team Champions."
reigns.note: CORRECTS the reign's own start date, previously recorded as a fresh title win over Cause & Effect on 31 August. HICAL (as International Champion) defeated Chet Jenkins to unify the belts' — the absorbing champion's reign is not restarted there either). This reading requires NO unattested title change (the Massacre is never shown losing the International Tag title between 27 July and 31 August); crediting Cause & Effect with the International Tag title instead (the reading implicit in the wing's existing title epitaph, unit caption and show match record) would require an unattested Massacre loss and an unattested Cause & Effect win, neither of which any held document attests.

Legend’s 117 day streak as champion was brought to an end as Czecher pinned James Dean to become the new eWo Champion" (/promotions/ewo/archive/roster-the-legend.html).

reigns.how: Won a four-way match at Hell & Back — eWo's first pay-per-view of its second run — pinning James Dean rather than champion The Legend, ending Legend's 117-day reign.
reigns.note: Hell & Back is not itself a held document; this account survives only in The Legend's own roster-card retrospective. Reconciles the Hall of Fame page's bare 'eWo Champion (1)' credit to Czecher with an era and a mechanism.

reigns.title: ewo-championship
reigns.label: The Legend

won.source: The promotion’s own About page narrates Cody Clark handing Legend the belt at BWF Danger Zone 2007 (/promotions/ewo/archive/about.html); The Legend’s own roster card: "Legend entered Epic Wrestling Organization as champion... named the first eWo Champion in the process" (/promotions/ewo/archive/roster-the-legend.html).

reigns.how: Awarded the vacant eWo Championship by chairman Cody Clark at BWF Danger Zone 2007, in the ring, moments after Legend's own last match as BWF Champion — the event the fed's own history calls the start of 'the second coming of eWo.' His first defense, per his own roster card, was against the last LWA Champion, Xaria Linette.
reigns.note: Lost to Czecher at Hell & Back — see the following reign.

reigns.title: ewo-championship
reigns.label: The Legend

won.source: The Legend’s own roster card: "Legend’s new finisher the Red Lottery was enough to regain his beloved eWo Championship" at Body Count (/promotions/ewo/archive/roster-the-legend.html).

reigns.how: Regained the title from Czecher at Body Count with his new finisher, the Red Lottery. Defended it afterward against Erin Jacobs at Supremacy, Lawrence Jarvis at License to Thrill, and a Guilty As Charged triple threat against Alexis Sykes and Xaria Linette, then Alexis Sykes again in an Ultimate Tables Match — the fed's own account calls this the only eWo Championship reign to break 100 days twice over.
reigns.note: License to Thrill's own date is fixed by the news page's 27 August 2007 post; Guilty As Charged's by the 1 October 2007 post (/promotions/ewo/archive/news-2007.html; /promotions/ewo/archive/news-headlines-2007.html). None of Hell & Back, Body Count, Supremacy, License to Thrill or Guilty As Charged is itself a held document — every detail here survives only in The Legend's own roster-card retrospective. Lost to Frank Murdoch at The New Black, which followed Violence XIX (14 October 2007) and preceded the fed's own 25 November 2007 closure.

reigns.how: Won a number-one contenders match, then became the first man to pin The Legend in eWo, at The New Black, ending Legend's 126-day reign.
reigns.note: eWo closed on 25 November 2007 with no further record of the title changing hands; the closure itself is the last word on this reign. No roster card of Murdoch's own survives — known only through The Legend's and Xaria Linette's own roster-card retrospectives.
