reigns.how: Awarded outright by FAW president Lisa Hunter, no match; her own on-air framing is muddled -- she describes Mason as "cheated out of the World Championship due to my husband's bad taste in referees," a World, not Universal, grievance, and no reign by "the HaHaKlown" survives on file for this belt specifically. Retained the billing into FAW Panic, February 2003 ("Ladies and gentlemen... Your Universal Champion.... SEAN MASON"), where he self-bills as the promotion's own co-founder returning to claim what he calls rightfully his.
reigns.note: faw-universal's own epitaph already flagged "Xander and Sean Mason both billed as champion" across FAW's later 2003 corpus; this row resolves the Mason side of that flag. The Xander billing is not yet resolved -- watch FAW Extreme Beating Three (30 March 2003) and FAW Panic (6 April 2003), where Xander is independently active, for the actual transition.

reigns.title: faw-universal
reigns.label: Lex Luger

won.source: Billed champion by Tuesday Torture, 20 March 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/tuesday-torture-2001-03-20.html), and confirmed defending by Friday Night Fear, 23 March 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/friday-night-fear-2001-03-23.html: “Lex Luger will defend his Universal title…”) in an upcoming battle royal against Hannibal Lector, Steve Austin and British Bulldog.

reigns.how: Champion by 20 March 2001; how or when he won it from The Olympian is not recorded.
reigns.note: Lost the title defending it in a battle royal at Extreme Beating; the fed's own pay-per-view calendar bills that show for 27 March 2001, but faw-extreme-beating-2001-03 is held at month precision (see that show's own dating note).

reigns.title: faw-universal
reigns.label: Lex Luger

won.source: Shown carrying the Universal title belt at FAW is War, 30 April 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-04-30.html), before a non-title match: “Luger drops of his Universal title belt, and slides in the ring.”

reigns.how: Champion again by 30 April 2001; scheduled to defend it against British Bulldog in a Tables, Ladders and Chairs match at May Day Massacre, 5 May 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/may-day-massacre-card-2001-05-05.html). The match was called off on air “due to injuries to both men,” and FAW's own co-president Sadam Hussain scrapped the title outright the same night (promotions/faw/archive/may-day-massacre-2001-05-05.html): “The Universal Title has been scrapped due to it getting in the way of progression!”
reigns.note: “Scrapped” here is the fed's own on-air word at this snapshot; FAW's own later corpus (Distortion, 2 June 2002; Panic, 29 May 2002 and February 2003; When Worlds Collide 2003, 26 January 2003) still names a champion for this belt, so the title did not stay dark — those later reigns are outside this pass's 2001-sites scope.

reigns.title: faw-universal
reigns.label: The Olympian

won.source: FAW's own champions page, dated March 2001 and captured 21 April 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-champions-2001-03.html) — the earliest surviving record already shows him champion, with Lex Luger the No. 1 Contender.

reigns.how: Already FAW Universal Champion on the fed's own earliest surviving snapshot, billed against Lex Luger in an I Quit Match for the title on the fed's own cards page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-cards-2001-03.html). No result of that match survives, but Luger is billed champion by the fed's next surviving show.
reigns.note: The loss to Luger is inferred from Luger being billed champion afterward, not directly recorded; exact date unknown. Holder now resolves to the-olympian-faw, minted from direct read of Tuesday Torture (13 and 20 March 2001), where the same name recurs as a trash-talking former champion reduced to undercard interference.

reigns.title: faw-us
reigns.label: Cyrus Skar

won.source: FAW Breakdown #1, 2002-08, read in full: Skar is simply presented the newly created title, replacing the European Championship he already held.

reigns.how: Awarded the newly created title in place of the European Championship he already held; no match.

reigns.title: faw-womens
reigns.label: Callie Stratus

won.source: FAW's own results and awards mirror (promotions/faw/archive/may-day-massacre-2001-05-05.html), read in full

reigns.how: Won a five-way battle royal (also involving Debbie, Sarah, and Zoe) over defending champion Trish Stratus at May Day Massacre, 5 May 2001 (Whoopie Cushion, pinfall).
reigns.note: Open-ended within this pass's scope; the surviving record's next dated Women's reign (faw-womens-r001, Tanya Vigilante) is not shown until 2002, so the record between is a gap, not an assertion of a single unbroken reign.

reigns.title: faw-womens
reigns.label: Tanya Vigilante

won.source: FAW May Day Massacre: No Laughing Matter, 2002-05, read in full: Tanya Vigilante (Tony Vigilante's wife, unannounced) sunset-flips defending champion Courtney Charisma Carter for the pin and the title.

reigns.how: Sunset-flip pinfall over champion Courtney Charisma Carter.

reigns.title: faw-womens
reigns.label: Trish Stratus

won.source: Already FAW Women's Champion entering May Day Massacre, 5 May 2001; read in full.

reigns.how: Already champion entering May Day Massacre, 5 May 2001; how or when she won the title is not recorded in the surviving record.
reigns.note: Loses the title to Callie Stratus in a five-way battle royal at May Day Massacre, 5 May 2001 (Whoopie Cushion, pinfall).

reigns.title: faw-womens
reigns.label: Courtney Charisma Carter

won.source: Undated in the surviving record; billed as defending champion entering May Day Massacre (2002-05, faw-may-day-massacre-no-laughing-matter-2002-05), read in full. No corroborated win date survives between Callie Stratus's own unrecorded loss (faw-womens-r000b) and this show.

reigns.how: Unknown -- billed champion entering the read show.
reigns.note: Loses the title to Tanya Vigilante at May Day Massacre; see faw-womens-r001.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Pyro

reigns.how: Won the World title at Breakaway 2001, in a match also involving Axle, Mystic X, and Spike (the Hall of Fame's own "Axle Mystic X and Spike" read as three names run together, not one hyphenated name, confirmed by Panic, 14 June 2001, read in full, which debuts Axle as a distinct fourth man added to a Mystic X/PyRo/Spike World Title match at Breakaway). The reign lasted about a month across two pay-per-views.
reigns.note: The Hall of Fame also credits Pyro with a second, fifteen-day reign, undated; it is not given a row of its own here.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: American Psycho

won.source: FAW's own Hall of Fame page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-hall-of-fame.html)

reigns.how: Took the gold off Pyro and held it for around a month.
reigns.note: The Hall of Fame separately dates the same win to the eve of Disaster Down Under.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Spider

won.source: FAW's own Hall of Fame page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-hall-of-fame.html)

reigns.how: Won the World title a month after taking the International and Hardcore belts, defended it against all comers inside a twenty-four-hour period and won a four-on-one gauntlet the same night.
reigns.note: Billed as Spider; the same character was billed Vincent from Diabolical Day 2002 onward.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Spawn

won.source: FAW's own Hall of Fame page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-hall-of-fame.html)

reigns.how: Beat Spider for the title after a lengthy bout, then defended it at the pay-per-view against Crimson Lord.
reigns.note: Possibly the same reign as r009d (Spawn, directly witnessed winning the vacant title at Summer Slaughter, 23 September 2001) -- but this row's own Hall-of-Fame-sourced how text (beating Spider, then defending against Crimson Lord) does not match what that show's own read shows (Spawn beats Skipster last in an improvised ice cube match, never faces Crimson Lord there); left as its own row rather than merged, since the discrepancy is unresolved.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jim ‘JLC’ Phoenix

won.source: FAW's own Hall of Fame page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-hall-of-fame.html)

reigns.how: Beat Spawn for the World Championship in the bout FAW's own Hall of Fame calls the standard-setter for its roleplays. The fed's own record says he was never beaten for the belt.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Skipster

won.source: FAW's own Hall of Fame page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-hall-of-fame.html)

reigns.how: Won the World Title, then lost it to Pyro in a street fight.

lost.source: Not itself read; Pyro is already billed FAW World Champion (c) entering the Diabolical Day 2001 main event against Skipster (promotions/faw/archive/diabolical-day-2001.html, read in full), with no version of the actual title change surviving in the held record. Corroborates this reign's own "how" note (from the fed's own Hall of Fame page), which already states Skipster lost the title to Pyro in a street fight.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Pyro

won.source: Not itself read; corroborated by Diabolical Day 2001's own "PyRo (c) vs Skipster" billing (promotions/faw/archive/diabolical-day-2001.html, read in full) and by reign r003's own note (from the fed's own Hall of Fame page) flagging an undated, un-rowed second Pyro reign of about fifteen days.

reigns.how: Reclaimed the title from Skipster off-screen, before Diabolical Day 2001; the actual title change is not shown in the surviving record. First directly shown as champion at Diabolical Day 2001, retaining against Skipster in a street fight with a powerbomb.

lost.source: Not itself read; dated and evidenced only by FAW IS WAR (30 July 2001, promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-07-30.html, read in full)'s own recap of Disaster Down Under (29 July 2001, unread -- no served page exists in the held record).

reigns.note: This is the fed's own Hall-of-Fame-flagged "second, fifteen-day [Pyro] reign" (see r003's own note) -- given its own row now that this pass's read of Diabolical Day corroborates it, though the exact title-change date/method still isn't shown anywhere in the held record.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Skipster

won.source: Not itself read; evidenced only by Skipster's own line at FAW IS WAR, 27 August 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-08-27.html, read in full), asking his stablemates whether he'll 'have to defend the World title at Summer Slaughter' -- the actual title change is never shown or otherwise described anywhere in the held record. The likeliest point is Entrapment (19 August 2001), itself unread.

reigns.how: Title change from The Omega Fro never shown in the surviving record. Not itself directly shown as champion anywhere in the held record either -- referenced only in dialogue.

lost.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-09-03.html), read in full

reigns.note: A second-degree gap even by this lane's own standard: unlike the other Disaster Down Under/Entrapment-era title changes, this one is inferred from a single line of dialogue rather than a direct recap statement -- recorded because two independent lines this same show corroborate it (the Commish's own "former champion" remark, and Skipster's own line), not because either alone would be sufficient.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: HaHaKlown

won.source: FAW's own Hall of Fame page and Diabolical Day 2003 recap (already cited); corroborated by direct read of Tuesday Torture, 13 March 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/tuesday-torture-2001-03-13.html), which stages the actual title-deciding three-fall match against Dogg.

reigns.how: The first FAW World Champion. The fed's own record says he was never beaten for the belt: he held it for roughly three months and handed it to his own sidekick Deadman before becoming president.
reigns.note: No date survives for either end of this reign; both edges are honestly unknown. Upgraded to an exact date on direct read of the deciding match itself: a three-fall (Hell in a Cell Street Fight / Submission / Buried Alive) encounter with Dogg, won 2 falls to 1, aided by an errant Olympian interference. FAW's own later recap (faw-is-war-2001-04-30.html) describes a brief interruption at Extreme Beating (2001-03) — HaHaKlown was made a co-champion with Sean Mason after a Laughing Scaffolding match neither man could actually lose — before "HaHaKlown won back his title the next show"; the fed's own retrospective frames the overall run as an unbroken ~3-month reign never lost in a straight fall, so that blip is recorded here rather than split into separate reign rows. Lost/ended 11 May 2001 (Panic), not by a pinfall but by retiring from in-ring competition to become FAW's third on-screen co-president alongside Bill Clinton and Sadam Hussain; Deadman is crowned new champion by acclamation the same night after his own separate hardcore-match win, not by beating HaHaKlown for the belt.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Deadman

won.source: FAW's own UK site (promotions/faw/archive/panic-2001-05-11.html), read in full — Sadam Hussain crowns him new champion in the ring immediately after his own hardcore-match win over TBRM.

reigns.how: Crowned new FAW World Champion by acclamation (Sadam Hussain, in the ring) on 11 May 2001, immediately after winning a separate hardcore match over debuting TBRM; not a title-match pinfall over the previous champion HaHaKlown, who retired from wrestling into the co-presidency the same night.
reigns.note: Loses the title at an unrecorded date before Panic, 7 June 2001, when Mystic X is declared champion; FAW IS WAR (28 May 2001) itself, read in full, still bills Deadman as sitting champion throughout that broadcast, so the exact turnover point is not corroborated anywhere in the surviving record.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Mystic X

won.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/panic-2001-06-07.html), read in full

reigns.how: Declared champion on-air by President Bill Clinton, overriding a dispute from VP Hellmaster over the circumstances; the same broadcast's own video package claims the actual change happened off-screen at FAW IS WAR, 28 May 2001, in a TLC-rules match this pass's own read of that show's own text does not corroborate (see faw-world-heavyweight-r002's own note) -- recorded here as an unresolved contradiction in the corpus, not resolved either way. Retains the same night in a Hardcore Rules match over The British Bomber after a corrupt-official stipulation (VP Hellmaster installed as the match's own referee) is short-circuited by an ally's run-in.
reigns.note: The fed's own later Hall of Fame page has Pyro winning the World title at Breakaway 2001 by defeating "Axle Mystic X and Spike" -- consistent with this reign, if loosely worded.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: American Psycho

won.source: Not itself read; dated and evidenced only by FAW IS WAR (30 July 2001, promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-07-30.html, read in full)'s own recap of Disaster Down Under (29 July 2001, unread -- no served page exists in the held record).

reigns.how: Beats Pyro for the title at Disaster Down Under, 29 July 2001, with Mystic X interfering and a controversial referee's decision (both sides' own account: Pyro's promo the next night blames Mystic X outright); the actual match is not shown in any surviving text this pass has read. This is a SEPARATE, later reign from faw-world-heavyweight-r004's own earlier American Psycho reign -- the same performer, a second run with the title.
reigns.note: Immediately precedes r009 (The Omega Fro), the fed's own Hall-of-Fame-sourced next reign in this title's undated 2001 chain -- this row's own 29 July 2001 date is the first hard anchor point in that chain since r008b/r003's own Breakaway dating.

lost.source: Not itself read; the title is billed vacant entering FAW IS WAR, 13 August 2001 (promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-08-13.html, read in full, Tony Blair's own line: 'the newly vacated World and International titles'), with no version of how American Psycho lost or vacated it surviving anywhere in the held record.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The Omega Fro

won.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-08-13.html), read in full -- supersedes the fed's own bio card's bare 'undated 2001' placeholder with a hard date.

reigns.how: Wins a vacant-title fatal 4-way (Shawn Johnson, Skipster, and a returning Pyro billed as the show's own 'mystery man'), teaming with Furious Alliance stablemate Skipster against the other two before finally turning on him too, and pins Skipster with the Armageddon. Mystic X runs in after the bell and chairs both Fro and Skipster, setting up his own promised title shot the following Monday.

lost.source: Not itself read; FAW IS WAR (27 August 2001, promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-08-27.html, read in full) refers to The Omega Fro outright as "the former FAW champion," with no account anywhere in the held record of when or how he lost the title. The likeliest point is Entrapment (19 August 2001), itself unread -- no served page exists in the held record, the same gap as Breakaway and Disaster Down Under.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Pyro

won.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-09-03.html), read in full

reigns.how: Beats Skipster by submission to the 3rd Degree Burn, directly shown. Pyro's third reign with the title.

lost.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/faw-is-war-2001-09-17.html), read in full

reigns.note: Retains against Bone Crusher, then announces his own departure from FAW after the bell and vacates the title outright rather than defending it at Summer Slaughter, directly shown.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Spawn

won.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/summer-slaughter-2001.html), read in full

reigns.how: Wins the vacant title (open since Pyro's own relinquishment, 17 September 2001) in a four-way Hell In A Cell/Glass Tables/Last Man Standing/Ultimate Hardcore match against Shawn Johnson, Skipster and Vincent (billed Spider); the cell itself catches fire and collapses mid-match, and the finish plays out in an improvised "ice cube match" between Spawn and the last-eliminated Skipster.
reigns.note: Possibly the same reign the fed's own Hall of Fame page describes in row r006 (also labeled Spawn) -- but that row's own "how" text ("Beat Spider for the title... then defended it at the pay-per-view against Crimson Lord") does not match what this show's own read shows (Spawn beats Skipster last, not Spider, and never faces Crimson Lord here); filed as a separate row rather than merged, since the Hall of Fame's own summary may compress a later, distinct reign or simply misstate this one's own details.

lost.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/deceit-2001-2001-11-23.html), read in full

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: JLC

won.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/deceit-2001-2001-11-23.html), read in full

reigns.how: Wins a 1-hour Iron Man match against champion Spawn at Deceit, 7 falls to 6.

lost.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/evil-intentions-2001-12-23.html), read in full

reigns.note: Unable to compete in his own scheduled Hell In A Cell/TLC defense after being attacked repeatedly through the day and finally run down by an unidentified vehicle in the parking lot -- his attacker is never identified in the held record; the title is contested and won by another man in his enforced absence.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The British Bomber

won.source: FAW's own site (promotions/faw/archive/evil-intentions-2001-12-23.html), read in full

reigns.how: Retrieves the belt hung above the ring in an 8-man Hell In A Cell/TLC match (in JLC's own enforced absence), carried up a ladder by new xCw co-owner Tom The Bomb after the cell floor collapses under him.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The British Bomber

won.source: the fed's own roster-database bio cards (faw.projectefed.com/cgi-bin/roster.cgi), workshop-held, never served

reigns.how: Champion going into the 19 January 2002 Panic, having been installed after Tom The Bomb's own screwjob finish to an eight-man Hell in a Cell.
reigns.note: Direct read of FAW Panic, 18 January 2002, confirms and slightly corrects the bio card's own “19th January” date for this loss: the actual served show, which stages the title-deciding fall itself, is dated 18 January 2002. Both dates are recorded here.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Chris Thunder

won.source: FAW Panic, 18 January 2002, read in full: Chris Thunder rolls up a distracted British Bomber for the pin and the title, moments after Lee Smith hauls interloping special-interest referee Tom The Bomb away from ringside.

reigns.how: Defeated The British Bomber on the 19th January edition of Panic.
reigns.note: Direct read of When Worlds Collide, 27 January 2002, confirms the loss and corrects the bio card's own “28 January” date by one day: JLC, refereeing Spider's corner, ambushes British Bomber to stop an English Lock submission on Thunder, then throws Spider on top of Thunder for the pin. Both dates are recorded rather than silently resolved.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Spider

won.source: When Worlds Collide, 27 January 2002, read in full: JLC, refereeing Spider's own corner, ambushes and removes British Bomber from a submission hold on Chris Thunder, then throws Spider on top of Thunder and counts the pin himself.

reigns.how: Beat Chris Thunder for the title at the fed's January pay-per-view. Lost the title to Spawn on FAW IS WAR, 12 February 2002.
reigns.note: The bio card's own “28 January” win date is one day off the actual served show's date (27 January 2002, FAW/xCw's own first joint pay-per-view); both are recorded rather than silently resolved. A three-man match with three referees, one per corner (Lee Smith for Thunder, Tom The Bomb for Bomber, JLC for Spider) — JLC's own corner assignment doubling as the pinfall-counting referee is the mechanism of the win.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Spawn

won.source: FAW IS WAR, 12 February 2002, read in full: Spawn pins Spider (Vincent) with The Last Kill in a No Holds Barred title match.

reigns.how: Pinned champion Spider with The Last Kill in a No Holds Barred match. Lost the title to The Omega Fro at Extreme Beating II, 31 March 2002, with a returning Tony Vigilante clearing out a reunited Omens of Death interference.
reigns.note: Immediately after winning, Spawn is ambushed by Crimson Lord (a casket-and-corpse angle) and the physical title belt is taken from him at ringside; the reign is recorded from the in-ring result, and left open pending whatever show resolves the theft.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The Omega Fro

won.source: Extreme Beating II, 31 March 2002, read in full: The Omega Fro pins champion Spawn with the Armageddon after Tony Vigilante clears out interference from a reunited Omens of Death.

reigns.how: Pinned champion Spawn with the Armageddon.
reigns.note: Open-ended as of this read. Tony Vigilante, who made the save, turns on Fro immediately after the bell. Lost the title at "Breaking Point," a 2002 pay-per-view booked in-storyline on Panic (12/27 April 2002, faw-panic-2002-04-12/27) and Hot Stuff (21 April 2002) as a Fatal Four-Way (Fro defending against Tony Vigilante, Ben Hart, and Spawn) -- no recap of that show survives in the held record. Tony Vigilante is confirmed the new champion by Distortion 6 (2002, faw-distortion-6-2002), read in full, which bills him as reigning champion entering its own Hell in a Cell main event. CORROBORATED (May Day Massacre, 2002-05, read in full): a recap video narrates this same title change in more detail -- Vigilante, aided by New School (Kyle Kilbane and Shawn Herrera), stripped Fro of the title at Breaking Point. FURTHER CORROBORATED (Panic, 3 May 2002, faw-panic-2002-05-03, read in full): a second replay segment shows the fuller Breaking Point sequence -- New School (Kyle Kilbane, Shawn Herrera) run in during a Fro/Ben Hart brawl also involving Spawn and Tony Vigilante, help Vigilante clear out Fro and Hart, then double-superkick and jackknife-powerbomb Spawn before Vigilante submits him with three chairs laid over the other three men, each reading "Justice Has Prevailed."

lost.source: FAW Breaking Point (re-dated April 2002; promotions/faw/archive/breaking-point-2003.html), read in full: Tony Vigilante submits Spawn (not champion The Omega Fro, permitted under this Fatal Four Way's own no-DQ rule) to win the title, with a debuting New School's help.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Tony Vigilante

won.source: FAW Breaking Point (re-dated April 2002; promotions/faw/archive/breaking-point-2003.html), read in full -- supersedes this row's own earlier inferred won-date (a bare 'champion by June 2002' snapshot with no match). Wins a Fatal Four Way (also involving champion The Omega Fro, Spawn and Ben Hart) by submitting Spawn, with a debuting tag team, New School (Shawn Herrera and Kyle Kilbane), running in to clear the way.

reigns.how: Submits Spawn in a No-Disqualification Fatal Four Way at Breaking Point, with New School's interference -- the champion (The Omega Fro) did not have to be pinned under this match's own explicit rule.
reigns.note: SOURCES ORDER UNRESOLVED: the June 2002 snapshot has Vigilante as champion and the Hall of Fame has The British Bomber winning the belt at Diabolical Day that July, so this reign precedes r013 in calendar order. Both receipts are recorded rather than resequenced. UPDATE: Vigilante loses the title clean via submission (his own Justification, reversed) to Spawn in a four-way Hell in a Cell main event, undated beyond "2002" but placed four days before May Day Massacre. This is a primary-source read outranking the June 2002 champions-page snapshot that originally dated this reign, so it now supplies the reign's lost edge -- but it does NOT resolve the existing sources-order tension the predecessor flagged: that June snapshot still bills Vigilante as champion, meaning either he regained the title again before June (not yet corroborated anywhere in the held record) or the snapshot itself is simply wrong/stale. FURTHER UPDATE (May Day Massacre, 2002-05, read in full): this same show explicitly bills Vigilante as still-reigning champion (carrying the physical belt, addressed as champion) in its own six-man Old School vs New School main event -- directly contradicting the Distortion 6 loss recorded above, despite May Day Massacre airing chronologically after Distortion 6. Left unresolved -- a genuine fed-side continuity error between two shows, not a Museum reading error. CONFIRMED (Diabolical Day 2002, 21 July 2002, faw-diabolical-day-2002-2002-07-21, read in full): this show's own referee introduction explicitly describes Tony Vigilante holding "the Title he left vacant" as a prop while serving as special guest referee for the tournament final -- direct primary-source confirmation the title was vacant entering this show, corroborating this row's own closing note rather than resolving the still-open Distortion-6/May-Day-Massacre contradiction, which remains unaddressed.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Spawn

won.source: FAW Distortion 6, 2002, read in full: Spawn makes champion Tony Vigilante tap out to a reversed Justification in a four-way Hell in a Cell main event also involving Skipster and The British Bomber.

reigns.how: Submission win over champion Tony Vigilante with Vigilante's own finisher, reversed.
reigns.note: May Day Massacre (faw-may-day-massacre-no-laughing-matter-2002-05), the next show chronologically, may bear on this. Left unresolved.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The British Bomber

won.source: FAW's own Hall of Fame page (promotions/faw/archive/faw-hall-of-fame.html): “After winning the FAW World title and XWW World title at Diabolical day 2002”.

reigns.how: Won the FAW World Championship and the invading XWW's own World Championship on the same night, at Diabolical Day 2002.
reigns.note: No served recap of the title change survives in the held record; the fed's own Diabolical Day 2002 recap is held, and the Hall of Fame's account is what dates the reign.

reigns.title: faw-world-heavyweight

The 2002 run spells it "Primetime". Angelo Deville pinned Jason O'Neil to win the Primetime title. Defences on record. Glory 8, 22 August 2002: Angelo Deville made John Jupiter submit to the Soprano to keep the Primetime title. Glory 10, 4 September 2002: The masked Dead Presidents broke up Angelo Deville's match with Jesse Ramey and the referee called for the bell, and Deville left still Primetime Champion. Glory 12, 26 September 2002: Angelo Deville's defence against Azala Zameer ended in a no contest. Bad Moon Rising, 20 October 2002: Ming let Angelo Deville pin Azala Zameer and the referee called for the bell on a count the text calls a shoulder-up, and Deville kept the Primetime title. Glory 16, 30 October 2002: Magnum Wolf tapped out to the Soprano at once, and Angelo Deville kept the Primetime title. Glory 19, 20 November 2002: Angelo Deville made Cassius Deamont submit to the Soprano, keeping the Primetime title and winning Deamont's FSW contract.

Three retentions inside the span are on cards: WorldWide of 3 Apr 2011 (a Rampage Group Stage Hardcore Match against Jimmy Thunder, which ends "Bryan Mayhem did it! He retains!" after a belly-to-belly suplex through a broken table), WorldWide of 4 May 2011 (against The Idol, "The winner of this match, and STILL GCW Hardcore Champion, Bryan MAYHEM!") and WorldWide of 22 May 2011 (against Shaman, "Bryan: Mayhem retains, Mayhem retains!" and "the ref hands Mayhem the hardcore title"). So the title was still his on 22 May 2011. The belt was then vacant from 28 Jul 2011 until 15 Aug 2011, when the Commissioner awarded it.

The list was not kept current after 2010 and is recorded as stale, not as evidence. Recorded on the night itself, and not smoothed: the commentary disputes the award before it happens — "Yale: I think there needs to be some official way for it since he never officially beat Mayhem" — and both men object to the letter afterwards. One successful defence is held, and it is the Vanguard unification: Rampage of 11 Oct 2011, billed "a one-title-leaves match", won on the Cruzifix Slam — "Andrews: Here is your winner...the GCW Hardcore Champion...The SoCal Prophet...BRAAAAAAD! CRUUUUUUUUUUUUZZZZZZZ!!!" and closing "Bryan: What a war that was, and we've got a solidified Hardcore Champion!" The commentary of 10 Jan 2012 calls that match "his first actual defense of the belt", which does not count the unification as one; both statements stand.

The reign is recorded as ending with the title vacant between Shockwave 2002 and Dangerous Games 2002; no held card shows how it left him. The card of Warpath 2005 reintroduces the belt with no champion: President Caldera tells Capo, who has taken it, "YOU ARE NOT TELEVISION CHAMPION" and announces "we will be crowning the new Television Champion" in a battle royal, which WorldWide 15 (2 Jun 2005) holds without him.

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — the federation's own record carries a de-facto / de-jure split across the last two months of this reign, and both halves are recorded. Tyson DeBough physically took the belt at Tsunami of 12 Aug 2007 and kept it. The fed's own newsdesk of 5 Sep 2007: "Yes, Jay Terror is still the GCW Television Champion, and the records will continue to indicate as much. Tyson DeBough stole the title, and the only reason he still has it is because President Caldera seems to admire the moxie." Of 13 Aug 2007, DeBough's own claim — "Steal? I just took what was rightfully mine. I earned the right to wear this belt." — against the interviewer's — "But Terror never lost to you, or O'Shea. He is the rightful champion." The Television Title History page agrees with the newsdesk and dates the change to Dangerous Games: "After stealing Terror's Television Title belt and keeping it under the protection of President Caldera for almost a month, Tyson DeBough got a chance to win the title outright at Dangerous Games in a ladder match. Terror was stunned by DeBough who took the title home fairly." The reign is filed to 14 Oct 2007, the date the page and the newsdesk both give; the two months DeBough held the physical belt are recorded here and not as a reign of his own. The page's own Reign cell reads '157 days'. At Warpath 2007 (3 Jun 2007) he unified this belt with the Vanguard Championship, beating Katie O'Clare under Vanguard Rules.

Five HDTV title matches sit inside the bracket and Johnny Borealis is named in every one of them; the fed's own title log names no champion on any of them. The win itself stays bracketed — "for almost an entire year" and "the better part of a year" in two later cards are consistent with it and do not date it. Make History', 5 Feb 2009) gives a different mechanism: 'after LeStatt Knight had ended Banned & Exiled~! first record breaking title reign, he was forced into picking a partner by President Steven Caldera. At WorldWide 91, on June 18th, 2008, LeStatt Knight named Chris Storm his partner. On that reading Knight ended the Banned & Exiled~! reign alone around 6-6-08, and the joint Knight-and-Storm reign the page dates to that same day did not begin until Storm was named his partner twelve days later, at WorldWide 91 on 6-18-08. Filed on the page's own date; the news post's mechanism is recorded here rather than applied, and no separate WorldWide 91 reign is filed — the count the article itself gives is already satisfied without one. won.source: the main event of the Wrestlecade write-up of 2004-04-26, where Josh pins Ice for the three count after the Youthful Descent (para 1063)

lost.source: the Dark Rituals write-up of 2004-10-26, the World title match: Josh "repeatedly slamming it on the canvas signifying his submission" to the ankle lock, and West: "the winner of the match...........and NEW GW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION......MAVERICK RENO!!!!"

reigns.note: Agrees with the old site's own title history, line 2: "On April 26, 2004, 'American Youth' Josh defeated Ice at Wrestlecade IV!" Billed champion at the Evolution of 5 July 2004 (para 584) and defends at the Whiplash of 31 August 2004. The fed's own later billing calls him "the longest reigning World Champion in GLOBAL history" (the Evolution of 13 June 2005, para 1314).

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Maverick Reno

won.source: the Dark Rituals write-up of 2004-10-26, the World title match: Josh "repeatedly slamming it on the canvas signifying his submission" to the ankle lock, and West: "the winner of the match...........and NEW GW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION......MAVERICK RENO!!!!"; the Evolution of 2004-11-01 still bills him the champion (para 46, "Reno's back, and World Champ")

lost.source: the Evolution write-up of 2004-11-01, para 305 ("the Global Wrestling World Championship is vacant") and paras 318-328: Christina McCoy carries the belt up the ramp to Bubba McCoy and drops it; para 323, Creed: "Bubba just stripped one of their own of the World Title!"

reigns.note: The Crossfire of 28 June 2004 (para 951) has him promise "One month from tonight... I will be your new World Champion!" He made 'American Youth' Josh submit to the ankle lock for it at Dark Rituals on 26 October 2004. Bubba McCoy stripped him of it at the Evolution of 1 November 2004, and it stayed vacant until Reload on 14 January 2005.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: 'Superstar' Ken Partridge, Jr

won.source: the Reload write-up of 2005-01-14, paras 1177-1181 ("Zenith after trying to fight out taps out", "KPJ HAS DONE IT!!!!", "KPJ is handed the title"); the old site's own title history line 3 gives the same day: "On January 14, 2005, 'Superstar' Ken Partridge, Jr defeated Christian Zenith and Jackson for vacated title."

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (Christian Zenith) begins here: the High Octane write-up of 2005-03-07, para 969: "NEW Global Heavyweight champion of the world!!!! Christian Zenith!!!"

reigns.note: The staging is the Main Event triple threat of the Reload of 14 January 2005 (its own opening line gives only "January 05"), paras 1174-1178: "The Epidemic!!!! KPJ has Zenith locked in tight!"... "Zenith... taps out"... "KPJ HAS DONE IT!!!!" The history's day and the show's own month agree, and the PTC forum's Reload announcement was posted that evening. He is billed "the reigning World heavyweight champion" going into the High Octane of 7 March 2005 (para 823). The write-up itself gives no day.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Christian Zenith

won.source: the High Octane write-up of 2005-03-07, para 969: "NEW Global Heavyweight champion of the world!!!! Christian Zenith!!!"

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (Salaok) begins here: the old site's own title history line 4: "On April, 2005, Salaok defeated Corvus and Christian Zenith at Clash of the Champions."

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — the old site's own title history, line 4, dates this change 2005-02-28 ("Christain Zenith defeated 'Superstar' Ken Partridge in a Hell in a Handbasket match at High Octane"); the show's own dateline reads 7 March 2005, and the reign follows the dateline. Both readings stand.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Salaok

won.source: the old site's own title history line 4: "On April, 2005, Salaok defeated Corvus and Christian Zenith at Clash of the Champions."

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (Train, below) begins here: the Wrestlecade write-up of 2005-05-15, the announcement of "your new World Champion and STILL World Tag Team Champion Train!"

reigns.note: The history gives the month only. The Evolution of 15 April 2005 (para 411) already bills Zenith "a former Television and World Champion", and the Evolution of 29 April 2005 (para 943) bills Salaok "The current GLOBAL HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION". The show the history names ("Clash of the Champions") is not among the served write-ups. No card for the night of this change survives in Global's own booking record; the date is the fed's own title history's.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Train

won.source: the Wrestlecade write-up of 2005-05-15, the announcement of "your new World Champion and STILL World Tag Team Champion Train!"

lost.source: the last dated billing of Train as champion (the Evolution of 13 June 2005, para 921, "newly crowned GLOBAL World Champion Train") and the first of Mindy Mercer (the Whiplash of September 2005)

reigns.note: Agrees with the old site's own title history, line 5: "On May 15, 2005, Train defeated Derek Frost and then Salaok in a Double Jeopardy Match at Wrestlecade." How his reign ended is not in any dated text; the old history carries no further line until March 2006.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Mindy Mercer

won.source: the Whiplash of September 2005, paras 1310-1311: "Mindy rolls off of Dawn ... The referee hands her the world title." -- a defence, the first billing of her as champion

lost.source: the Showdown in Tokyo of 29 November 2005 (para 547) bills Christian Zenith "STILL Global Wrestling World Champion"

reigns.note: Her win and her loss are both in undated shows or none; the brackets are the dated shows either side. No card for the night of this change survives in Global's own booking record; the dates given are the bracket the fed's own record supports.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Christian Zenith

won.source: the Showdown in Tokyo write-up of 2005-11-29, para 547

lost.source: the next reign on this belt ('The Big Dawg' Jake Hix) begins here: the Reload write-up of 2006-01-12, para 677: "new Global Heavyweight Champion of the World! THE BIG DAWG! JAKE HIX!!!!!"

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — inside one show. The Showdown in Tokyo of 29 November 2005 ends its World Championship match (Christian Zenith vs. Seymour Almasy) "Your winner of the match, as a result of a disqualification, and STILL Global Wrestling World Champion...CHRISTIAN ZENITH!" (para 547); the same show's main event, written by another hand, twice treats Emoticon as the World champion (para 802, "Shadow or McFarlane will go to Reload to face Emoticon for the World title!!!!!"; para 880, "The crowd erupts as the NEW World Champion; Emoticon runs down chair in hand..."). The reign follows the match result and leaves paras 802 and 880 as written; the next show, the Reload of 12 January 2006, bills Zenith the champion (para 501). Both readings are recorded here. No card for the night of this change survives in Global's own booking record; the dates given are the bracket the fed's own record supports.

won.source: the Reload write-up of 2006-01-12, para 677: "new Global Heavyweight Champion of the World! THE BIG DAWG! JAKE HIX!!!!!"

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (Brick) begins here: the High Octane write-up of 2006-02-24, para 581: "Here is your NEW Global Heavyweight Champion: BRICK!" (a Dog Collar match won by touching four turnbuckles, paras 520, 567-575)

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Brick

won.source: the High Octane write-up of 2006-02-24, para 581: "Here is your NEW Global Heavyweight Champion: BRICK!" (a Dog Collar match won by touching four turnbuckles, paras 520, 567-575)

lost.source: the Clash of the Titans write-up of 2006-04-21 (dated circa; see the show), the World Championship hardcore match, para 456: "the winner of this match, and new Global World Champion!!! The Big Dawg! Jake Hix!!!"

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — the old site's own title history line 6 dates this win 2006-03-15 ("On March 15, 2006, Brick defeated 'The Big Dawg' Jake Hix."); the show's own date is 2006-02-24. Both readings stand. The fed's own current-champion pointer on its 2006 site names him the World champion; that pointer is an end point of the 2006 site, not of the record.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: 'The Big Dawg' Jake Hix

won.source: the Clash of the Titans write-up of 2006-04-21 (dated circa; see the show), the World Championship hardcore match, para 456: "the winner of this match, and new Global World Champion!!! The Big Dawg! Jake Hix!!!"

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (John "The Prophet" Adams) begins here: the Showdown in Tokyo write-up of 2006-12-13, para 1698: "NEW Global Heavyweight Champion of the World, John 'The Prophet' Adams"

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — the old site's own title history, line 7, dates this change 2006-07-14 ("On July 14, 2006, 'The Big Dawg' Jake Hix defeated Brick."); the fed's own text puts it at Clash of the Titans, April 2006 (the Clash of the Titans write-up, para 456, and the Fusion of 16 May 2006, para 745: "At Clash Of The Titans he defeated Brick"). Both readings stand. Defends at the Fusion of 27 September 2006 (no contest) and at the Dark Rituals of 31 October 2006 (title for title, winning the International too).

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: John "The Prophet" Adams

won.source: the Showdown in Tokyo write-up of 2006-12-13, para 1698: "NEW Global Heavyweight Champion of the World, John 'The Prophet' Adams"

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (Eryc Morgan) begins here: the Reload write-up of 2007-01-24, para 1678: "NEW World Heavyweight Champion, 'The Dark Flame' ERYC MORGAN!!!" (No Holds Barred Ironman; Cold Embrace at :01, para 1676)

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — the old site's own title history line 8 dates it 2006-12-17 ("On December 17th, 2006 John Adams defeated Jake Hix"); the show's own date is 2006-12-13. Both readings stand.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Eryc Morgan

won.source: the Reload write-up of 2007-01-24, para 1678: "NEW World Heavyweight Champion, 'The Dark Flame' ERYC MORGAN!!!" (No Holds Barred Ironman; Cold Embrace at :01, para 1676)

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (BloodAngel) begins here: the Fusion write-up of 2007-02-15, para 931: "NEW Global Wrestling World Champion... BLOODANGEL!"

reigns.note: The old history carries no line for this change.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: BloodAngel

won.source: the Fusion write-up of 2007-02-15, para 931: "NEW Global Wrestling World Champion... BLOODANGEL!"

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (Jake Hix, below) begins here: the High Octane write-up of 2007-02-22, main event, para 1275: "The winner of this match, and still Global World Championship champion, Jake Hix!!!"

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — on the night this reign ended. The High Octane of 22 February 2007 introduces BloodAngel as "Global's World Champion" going into its main event, a World Heavyweight Championship fatal fourway elimination (para 1174), and Jake Hix is the last man standing; the announcer's closing call then names him "still Global World Championship champion" (para 1275), a wording that reads as a defence and not a win. The reign follows the match: BloodAngel is the outgoing champion and Hix the new one. Both readings stand.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: 'The Big Dawg' Jake Hix

won.source: the High Octane write-up of 2007-02-22, main event, para 1275: "The winner of this match, and still Global World Championship champion, Jake Hix!!!"

lost.source: the next reign on this belt (BloodAngel) begins here: the old site's own title history line 10: "On April 7th, 2007, BloodAngel defeated 'The Big Dawg' Jake Hix."

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — on the night this reign began. The High Octane of 22 February 2007 introduces BloodAngel as champion going into the main event, a fatal fourway elimination (para 1174), and has Hix as the last survivor; the announcer's closing call names Hix "still Global World Championship champion" (para 1275), which reads as a defence and not a win. The reign follows the match: Hix wins the belt that night. Both readings stand. Billed "current Global World Heavyweight Champion" at the Fusion of 15 March 2007 (para 40).

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: BloodAngel

won.source: the old site's own title history line 10: "On April 7th, 2007, BloodAngel defeated 'The Big Dawg' Jake Hix."

lost.source: the Fusion write-up of 2007-06-01, paras 19, 25: Brandi Sights announces his absence and vacates the title

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — the old site's own title history, line 11, has "On June 1, 2007, Eryc Morgan defeated BloodAngel."; the Fusion of 1 June 2007 vacates the belt in BloodAngel's absence and Morgan wins the vacancy from Jocque Noreault. Both readings stand. The old history's date for this win falls inside the dated bracket (Hix billed champion at the Fusion of 15 March 2007; BloodAngel billed "the current World Champion" at the Fusion of 27 April 2007, para 783). No dated show of 7 April 2007 is held. He defends at the WrestleCade of 20 May 2007. No card for the night of this change survives in Global's own booking record; the date is the fed's own title history's.

reigns.title: gw-world-heavyweight

won.source: the Fusion write-up of 2007-06-01, para 1320: "NEW GLOBAL WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION, THE DARK FLAME, ERYC MORGAN!" (the vacancy, filled by a lottery-drawn match against Jocque Noreault)

lost.source: the Fusion write-up of 2007-09-22, paras 13-19 and 378-381: all four of the fed's belts come in vacant after an offscreen mass release ("contracts did not get resigned and the champs were released"; "the Exodus of Many", para 33)

reigns.note: Defends at the Whiplash of 1 July 2007 (two falls to one; the whole match is replayed at the Fusion of 7 July 2007, para 412). At the Master of the Mat of 31 August 2007 he is billed as Corvus and retains twice ("STILL Global World Heavyweight Champion...CORVUS!!!", para 847); the same show names the two as one man (para 741, "the rechristened Eryc Morgan, who is once again going by the name of Corvus"). The old site's current-champion file names him first, as "e-morgan".

The lineage was unified into the International Xtreme Championship the same night.

reigns.title: gwf-2006-cruiserweight

reigns.label: Terrorize & Stryfe

won.source: Won a multi-team match over FIRE and the Party Animals at W.A.R. to fill the vacant titles.

reigns.note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champions, the Party Animals, on 24 May 1997.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tag
reigns.label: the Party Animals (Sam & Gabe)

won.source: Won the titles at Mega Fight.

reigns.note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champions, Double Impact, attested by September 1997.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tag
reigns.label: Double Impact (Steven Stryfe & Tyson Tercell)

won.source: Billed as champions on the federation's 12 and 24 September 1997 broadcasts; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

reigns.note: The federation's own 24 September broadcast calls them its "ONLY two time champions," implying an intervening loss and regaining of these titles that no surviving document in the held record carries. A defense against Tha Horsemen took place at the federation's final pay-per-view; the announcing team's own talk of "a rematch" afterward suggests they retained.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-triangle
reigns.label: Immorality

won.source: Named the first-ever HCW Triangle Champion in a segment of the Beachblast broadcast.

lost.source: A tournament to decide a new champion was announced for the federation's 15 October 1997 broadcast; its outcome does not survive in the held record.

reigns.note: The same Beachblast broadcast's own commentary elsewhere calls Chris Hunter "still HCW Triangle Champion" in an earlier segment — an inconsistency in the federation's own record that this collection preserves rather than resolves.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tv
reigns.label: "Vile" Vince Viper

won.source: Won the eight-man tournament final over Patty Babes Carter at British Invasion to become the first Television Champion.

reigns.note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champion, Austin Starr, who is billed champion by September 1997.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tv
reigns.label: Damon Zex

won.source: Crowned champion on the federation's 18 November 1997 broadcast.

reigns.note: A defense against Angus was announced for the federation's next Thursday broadcast on 3 December 1997; no result survives.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-tv
reigns.label: Austin Starr

won.source: Billed champion by September 1997, chased by challenger Sammy the Kid; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

reigns.note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champion, Damon Zex, on 18 November 1997.

won.source: Won the finals of a 32-entrant tournament run across three broadcasts.

lost.source: Lost the title to "Franchise" Shane Dreamer at W.A.R.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-us
reigns.label: "Franchise" Shane Dreamer

won.source: Defeated Jon Stilwater for the title at W.A.R.

reigns.note: The federation's own later commentary recalls Cyanide beating him for the title "the first week he came here," though the transition itself is not carried by any surviving document.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-us
reigns.label: Cyanide

won.source: Billed as champion at Mega Fight (24 May 1997), where he retained the title in a three-way match over Mammoth and Mike "The Mechanic" Malone; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

reigns.note: Still champion when the federation retired this title on 23 July 1997, replacing it with the new Television Championship.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
reigns.label: "Wild Thing" Jonnie Adonis

won.source: Won the 30-man over-the-top battle royal at the federation's first pay-per-view, March Mayhem.

lost.source: The federation's own broadcasts still bill him as champion through the 5 April title tournament finals and call him the former champion by the following Thursday's show (10 April); the vacating itself is not carried by any surviving document.

reigns.note: The vacated title was to be awarded by a three-way match, held at the next pay-per-view.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
reigns.label: El Perfecto

won.source: Won a triangle match over Patty Babes Carter and the Heartbreaker at W.A.R. to fill the vacant championship.

reigns.note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champion, the Heartbreaker, who is billed as champion by 1 July 1997.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
reigns.label: Chris Hunter

won.source: Won a six-man, two-ring open-barbwire steel-cage elimination match, "Hardcore Hell," at Cage Wars.

reigns.note: Cage Wars itself does not survive in the held record; only its announcement and its aftermath do. Still billed champion on 18 November 1997. No title-change document survives for the transition to the next and final champion, Lord Doomsday, sometime before 3 December 1997.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
reigns.label: the Heartbreaker

won.source: Billed as HCW World Champion on the allied WOWA's own 1 July 1997 broadcast; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

reigns.note: No title-change document survives for the transition to the next champion, Chris Hunter, who wins the title at Cage Wars on 14 September 1997.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1997-world
reigns.label: Lord Doomsday

won.source: Billed champion by the federation's final pay-per-view, November Armageddon, on 3 December 1997; the title-change document itself does not survive in the held record.

reigns.note: Retained the title against Chris Hunter in a Dog Collar Texas Tornado double-cage match that ended in a one-hour draw at November Armageddon, the federation's final pay-per-view — the last champion of record before the federation's closure.

reigns.title: hcw-hardcore-1999-tv
reigns.label: "Asshole" Andy Simmons

reigns.title: heavyweight-maritime-wa-1999
reigns.label: the Riot King

won.source: Defeated "Yukon" Jack Roberts by submission for the vacant championship.

reigns.note: The first champion in the title's history; still champion at the close of this record.

reigns.title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
reigns.label: Mr. Justice

reigns.note: Attacked and laid out by a masked man moments after winning the title; the title changes hands to Mass Destruction off-page some time before the fed's own 27 June 1998 newsletter.

won.source: Already billed champion entering Sharp Turn (28 February 1998); no document in this record shows the win itself.

The fed's own newsletter (issue 1, 27 June 1998), reporting Mass Destruction as "the new SWL World Champion" after turning on Gravedigger and joining the kick Ass order at the fed's own Pay Per View, Warzone (21 June 1998); no document in this record shows the title actually changing hands at that event.

reigns.title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
reigns.label: American Heartthrob

reigns.note: The promotion's first-ever recorded champion, per the fed's own history; lost the title to Sniper at a pay-per-view named in that same history and independently corroborated as an SWL event, "In Your Face: Heartbreak Hotel," which does not survive in the held record.

reigns.title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
reigns.label: Sniper

won.source: The fed's own third-person "SWL History" newsletter (5 November 1997), naming the pay-per-view "In Your Face: Heartbreak Hotel" as the site of the title change; the event does not survive in the held record.

reigns.note: Lost the title off-page to Mr. Excellent some time before 22 November 1997.

reigns.title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
reigns.label: Mr. Excellent

won.source: The character's own self-posted recruitment advertisement (22 November 1997), corroborated by the fed's own Monday Madness broadcast (1 December 1997), where he retains the title in a non-title handicap loss.

reigns.note: Recorded from the champion's own contemporary claim, corroborated by the fed's own broadcast defending it. Lost the title off-page to Insanity some time before the promotion's own In Your Face: Sharp Turn pay-per-view (28 February 1998), where Insanity already holds it entering the show.

reigns.title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
reigns.label: Insanity

won.source: The fed's own Ring Masters broadcast (22 March 1998): Insanity is introduced entering the main event already carrying the SWL World Heavyweight Title, having lost it to Mr. Justice at Sharp Turn (28 February 1998, already a reign of record on this title).

reigns.note: A second reign, won back off-page from Mr. Justice; retained in a no-contest at Ring Masters. Recorded as vacated when the champion announced his own firing from the promotion around 8 April 1998, on suspicion of spying for a rival federation; no document names his successor directly.

reigns.title: heavyweight-swl-1997b
reigns.label: "Arrogent" Anthony Mislan

won.source: The fed's own King of the Mats pay-per-view (24 May 1998), where Anthony Mislan enters already champion; won off-page some time after Insanity's own firing (circa 8 April 1998).

reigns.note: Retained at King of the Mats when the referee stopped his own challenger's match after Mislan's leg broke on the ring stairs; a stoppage win does not transfer the title, though a thirty-day defense clause is raised as a cliffhanger, unresolved in this record. The title changes hands off-page to Mass Destruction (already a reign of record) some time before the fed's own newsletter of 27 June 1998.

reigns.title: heavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
reigns.label: Mighty Quinn

won.source: Won the vacant championship in the promotion's own Heavyweight Royal Rumble broadcast, eliminating Snake Zurlock last.

reigns.note: Still champion at this record's own latest 2000 data point, a 13 May 2000 ranking update.

reigns.title: heavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
reigns.label: Pure Pain

won.source: Billed as the reigning UWF Heavyweight Champion on the promotion's own "Rage for Order" card, 8 January 1999.

reigns.note: Lost the title to Holy Terror in a match not read for this record, some time between 22 January and 3 February 1999.

reigns.title: heavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
reigns.label: Holy Terror

won.source: Billed by the promotion's own 3 February 1999 broadcast as the recent dethroner of the UWF Heavyweight Championship.

reigns.note: Lost a non-title match to a debuting Johnny Reb on "Blackout," after which the promotion's own broadcast declared the championship and its own top ten rankings in "utter turmoil," pending resolution.

reigns.title: heavyweight-uwf-arena-1998
reigns.label: JJ Rock

won.source: This title change is not shown in the surviving record; the promotion's own last attested 1999 champion is Holy Terror, and JJ Rock is later named as the title's abandoning holder in the 2000 Heavyweight Royal Rumble broadcast.

reigns.how: Abandoned the title rather than defend it, described in the promotion's own words as having "won the UWF Championship and left it to rot," leaving it vacant ahead of the Heavyweight Royal Rumble.
reigns.note: This gap in the ledger, between Holy Terror's last 1999 attestation and JJ Rock's own abandonment, falls on the promotion's own weekly broadcasts not held in this record.

reigns.note: "We crowned a new US champion" -- the fed's own broadcast text.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-cruiserweight-championship
reigns.label: El Diablo Rolande

reigns.how: Won by pinfall.

lost.source: Loses back to The Usurper on "Friday Fights" (29 May 1998), also recapped within "June 12 Friday Fights."

reigns.note: Both the win and the loss are recapped, not originally served, documents; cited here as primary-source recap footage rather than the originating broadcasts, which lie outside the held record's corpus.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-cruiserweight-championship
reigns.label: The Usurper (fourth reign, by his own count)

won.source: Pins El Diablo Rolande with a bridging back suplex in 5:22 on "Friday Fights" (29 May 1998), recapped within "June 12 Friday Fights"; commentary calls it "his fourth Cruiserweight Title."

reigns.how: Won by pinfall.

lost.source: Loses to Alucard Belmont on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998).

reigns.note: Retains against El Diablo Rolande in a rematch on "June 12 Friday Fights" before losing it three days later.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-cruiserweight-championship
reigns.label: Alucard Belmont

won.source: Beats The Usurper for the title on "Monday Mania" (15 June 1998).

reigns.note: Retains against El Diablo Rolande at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998, 14:09), against The Usurper at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998, 11:41), and against Vic Valiant by disqualification on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" (14:18) after Aero's ringside interference.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Predators

won.source: Billed champions, retaining the title over Hellfire and Serial Killa of the Apocalypse on "Monday Mania" (22 June 1998); no document in this record shows how or when they won it.

lost.source: No document in this record shows how or when the title left The Predators' hands.

reigns.note: Recorded as champions from billing; a large, untracked gap separates this reign from the Insano Boys' own 2001 reign.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Insano Boys

won.source: Already billed World Tag Team Champions by the promotion's own 9 September 2001 broadcast; no document in this record shows how or when they won the title.

reigns.how: Retains over Johnny Pyro and The Stud by disqualification on "Superstar Challenge" (7 September 2001).
reigns.note: Still champions as of 7 September 2001, with a defense against the Legion of Pain (Nighthawk and Viper) announced for "Clash of the Titans VII" (9 October 2001, outside this record).

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
reigns.label: The Night Stalker

won.source: Pins Vic Valiant in 10:54 at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998), his first Television Championship.

reigns.how: Won by pinfall.

lost.source: Loses to Tony Sanders by pinfall on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" after Legion of Pain interference (Jay Hawke's chair shot, followed by "Foolkiller" Jason Bell knocking out Tony Sanders and placing him atop Stalker for the pin).

reigns.note: Retains against Vic Valiant ("June 26 Friday Fights"), Bomb ("July 4 Friday Fights"), Aero ("July 10 Friday Fights"), and Jay Hawke ("Super Bowl of Wrestling II," 21 July 1998) before losing it.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
reigns.label: Tony Sanders

won.source: Wins the title on "August 5 Superstar Challenge" after Legion of Pain interference leaves The Night Stalker pinned "under questionable means."

reigns.how: Won by pinfall, with outside interference.

lost.source: By "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998), the Television Championship is shown vacant and The Night Stalker -- not Sanders -- is the one stripped of it under a one-title-per-wrestler rule; no document in the held record shows how or when Sanders lost the title to Stalker.

reigns.note: A further untracked transition: Night Stalker holds the Television Championship again by November, alongside the World Heavyweight Championship, triggering the promotion's own rule against holding two titles at once.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
reigns.label: "Stone Cold" Steve Anderson (billed masked as Tyrone the Psychopathic Soldier)

won.source: Wins the sixteen-man tournament final over Tony Sanders in 3:38 at "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998), unmasking afterward.

reigns.how: Won a single-elimination tournament final by pinfall (Stone Cold Stunner).
reigns.note: Retains against Tony Sanders by count-out on "November 20 Friday Fights" after voluntarily leaving the ring mid-match; the title does not change hands on a count-out under the promotion's own rules.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
reigns.label: "Double V" Vic Valiant

won.source: Billed champion entering "Parade of Champions," with commentary noting he has held "every title currently available except the World Title" and "two TV Title reigns"; the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

lost.source: Loses to The Night Stalker, who wins his first Television Championship, at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998), the culmination of Stalker's own HIWF Gauntlet run.

reigns.note: Recorded as champion from billing; no document in the held record shows how or when he won this particular reign.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-television-championship
reigns.label: The Night Stalker (second reign)

won.source: Not attested by any document this collection holds; recorded only from the promotion's own "Clash of the Titans II" press release, which states he is being stripped of the title.

lost.source: Stripped by President J. Adam Hawkins ahead of "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998) under a rule barring one wrestler from holding two HIWF titles at the same time -- he had also won the World Heavyweight Championship by this point.

reigns.note: The sixteen-man tournament originally announced as a World Heavyweight Championship number-one-contender tournament is repurposed on the spot to crown the new, vacant Television Champion.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-us-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Mantua Thunder

won.source: Pins Hellfire with a chair-assisted flying bulldog at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998).

reigns.how: Won by pinfall, using a chair.

lost.source: Retains against James Kira later the same night, and against Vic Valiant on "Monday Mania" (11 August 1998); no further document in the held record shows how or when the title left his hands.

reigns.note: By "November 20 Friday Fights" the Jamaican Stud is shown holding the title instead; the transition is not attested by any document this collection holds.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-us-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Hellfire

won.source: Billed champion, retaining a two-out-of-three-falls defense against "Foolkiller" Jason Bell at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998); the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

lost.source: Loses to Mantua Thunder at "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998) after a chair shot.

reigns.note: Recorded as champion from billing; no document in the held record shows how or when he won the title.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-us-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: "Jamaican Juggalo" the Jamaican Stud

won.source: Not attested by any document this collection holds; first shown as reigning champion on "November 20 Friday Fights."

reigns.note: Retains against Mantua Thunder by disqualification (foreign-object powder) on "November 20 Friday Fights"; the title itself does not change hands on a disqualification finish under the promotion's own rules.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Mr. Shh! (billed "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh)

won.source: Wrestling masked, pins Nighthawk at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998) with Legion of Pain interference; unmasks himself the next night on "Monday Mania" as Mr. Shh!

reigns.how: Won by pinfall, with outside interference.

lost.source: Retains through at least "Super Bowl of Wrestling II" (21 July 1998, by double disqualification); no further document in the held record shows how or when the title left his hands.

reigns.note: A gap follows in the held record: by "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998) Chris Hart is described as a former World Champion who had already won and lost the title at least once by that point, and Night Stalker is shown holding it, won 'with the Jamaican Stud's help' from Hart. Neither the end of this reign nor Chris Hart's own first win is attested by any document this collection holds.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: "The Working Man" Chris Hart (second reign)

won.source: Pins The Night Stalker in 8:36 at "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998).

reigns.how: Won by pinfall.
reigns.note: Still champion as of "November 20/21 Friday Fights"; a rematch against Night Stalker is booked for 12 December 1998, outside the held record.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Nighthawk

won.source: Billed champion, retaining in a falls-count-anywhere defense against Leon Redfield on the promotion's own 10 May 1998 home video, recapped within "Parade of Champions"; the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

lost.source: Loses to a masked "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh (revealed as Mr. Shh!) at "Parade of Champions" (21 June 1998) after Legion of Pain interference.

reigns.note: Recorded as champion from billing; no document in the held record shows how or when he won the title.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship

lost.source: Loses the title to The Night Stalker with the Jamaican Stud's assistance, per Chris Hart's own account; no document in the held record shows the match itself.

reigns.note: Presumed from Chris Hart's own on-air claim and his billing as a 'former HIWF World Champion' before Clash of the Titans II; grade presumed, not primary-source, since the win and loss are not independently attested.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: The Night Stalker

won.source: Not attested by any document this collection holds; recorded from Chris Hart's own account (see r003) and this wing's own "Clash of the Titans II" press release, which shows him as reigning champion entering that show.

lost.source: Loses to Chris Hart at "Clash of the Titans II" (17 November 1998).

reigns.note: Also survives a separate 'controversial' title defense against Chris Hart the Saturday before Clash of the Titans II, per that show's own press release; that match's own result is not stated and is not treated as a further reign change here. Also stripped of the Television Championship the same week under a one-title-per-wrestler rule -- see the Television Championship's own reign r004.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship

won.source: Already champion, and by then also described as the owner of the Supreme Wrestling Federation, when he retains over new Silent Assassins recruit Randall Flagg at "Clash of the Titans VI: Class Dismissed" (9 May 2000); no document in this record shows how or when he regained the title after his first reign.

lost.source: The promotion's own retrospective broadcast (9 September 2001) states he "would hold onto that title for another two months before finally losing it to Pagan"; the title change itself is not otherwise attested in this record.

reigns.note: A gap follows the earlier-held reign of Chris Hart (world-r005) and this reign; neither the end of Hart's reign nor the start of this one is attested by any document this record holds.

reigns.title: hiwf-entity-e-1998-world-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Pagan

won.source: The promotion's own retrospective broadcast (9 September 2001) states Mr. Shh! "would hold onto that title for another two months before finally losing it to Pagan," roughly two months after 9 May 2000; the title change itself is not otherwise attested in this record.

lost.source: No document in this record shows how or when the title left Pagan's hands.

reigns.note: By the time of the reopened 2001 HIWF's own World Heavyweight Title tournament, The Stud is billed champion; no document in this record attests to the tournament's own final or to how The Stud won the title.

reigns.note: Still champion as of 9 September 2001, announced to defend the title against El Cholo at "Clash of the Titans VII" (9 October 2001, outside this record).

lost.note: Chained onto wave-C90-L281's own not-yet-folded correction to this same record's own won field (1997-05-31).

won.source: The Harlequins defeat Night Patrol for the United States Tag Team Championship, per the fed's own live broadcast (msg_id ynjRtuSKYOMJ, served under this wing); corroborated the same week by the fed's own newsdesk column (msg_id 0ybYyMtgX-AJ, served under this wing). No exact stripping date survives in this pass's own reading; the reign ends sometime before Deathbringer's own tenure and well before Otto Verhoeven's 12 October 1996 Casket Match win (r03, now dated by this same pass).

Hardin (r01) and Deathbringer (r02); the Psycho was later cleared of the vandalism charges and granted the key to the city of New York, per the same retrospective, but the title itself was never restored to him.

won.source: Otto Verhoeven defeats Deathbringer in a Casket Match at Ring Wars II to win the World Heavyweight Championship, per a Classics re-broadcast recap naming the match (msg_id YU7YNiln5hkJ, served under this wing); a second Classics episode independently dates Ring Wars II itself to 12 October 1996 (msg_id RZAWIRGkW0kJ, served under this wing). This dates and sources the reign for the first time; it had previously been visible only in the fed's own weekly rankings table.

No results report for the show itself survives in the held record; the December 1998 billing already on file (outside this wing's own pre-read) is consistent with an unbroken reign from this date.

No title-loss document survives in the held record, so `lost` is left unset.

won.source: ERRATUM CORRECTED: the previously-cited date and source do not survive scrutiny. The cited document (msg_id zks8f84PxncJ, a Monday Musings column dated two days after the claimed win) instead shows Requiem still champion on 20 September, publicly announcing he is quitting Genesis after retaining the title against "Sychosys" Joe Petrow that same night (see iiwf-intercontinental-r09's own corrected Hour Two citation, same broadcast) -- no title change is shown or claimed anywhere in that document. "The Triple Cross" is an unrelated epithet for Brody Thunder, first seen at Ring Wars IV (8 November 1997, msg_id Bt7Q6x6OGhMJ, not served under this wing), not a dated event. This pass's own reading instead finds the actual title match -- Requiem [c] vs. "Lone Wolf" Brody Thunder -- opening on IIWF Saturday Night, 4 October 1997 (msg_id uzmeMkXL4xQJ, served under this wing; lead-in at msg_id n3VDCBezuBMJ, served under this wing), the first primary-source sighting of this title change. The surviving record does not carry this broadcast's own remaining parts, so the finish itself is not recovered; the win is therefore bounded no earlier than 4 October 1997 and no later than 8 November 1997 (Ring Wars IV, where Thunder is already champion). Still billed as reigning champion at the Second Annual Golden Grapple Awards, 22 November 1997 (served under this wing, msg_ids iW-VEdvXCN8J et al.), successfully defended against "Outlaw" J.W. Hardin at Ring Wars IV, 8 November 1997, per the fed's own broadcast (msg_id uLPaM8-M4_EJ, served under this wing; also recapped at msg_id 2YRX93Cx0QYJ, served under this wing), and through December 1997.
