reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: JD Morgan

won.source: Eleventh Hour, Friday, 12th November 2011 (in-game): "Ten Man Battle Royal ... for the MAW All Action title ... Winner: JD Morgan (C-)"; the diary's own title records list "JD Morgan November 2011 1 Won in a Battle Royal" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won the first All Action title in the ten-man battle royal at Eleventh Hour, in which the Second Sons work as a unit until Morgan throws out Sheriff Blaze, Bradford Peverell, Chance Fortune, Antonio and Cameron Vessey and ends it by gorilla-pressing Casey Valentine onto his partners; he keeps the belt against Ernest Youngman in a submission match at Farewell Tour on 22nd November, with a Cross Atlantic Stretch, and loses it on the night of Remember November, when the belt is up for grabs all night and Kid Arachnid hits him with a steel chair backstage.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Kid Arachnid

won.source: Remember November, Friday, 26th November 2011 (in-game): the All Action title is declared up for grabs all night; the diary's own title records list "Kid Arachnid (KC Glenn) November 2011 0" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won backstage at Remember November by hitting JD Morgan with a steel chair as he arrives and pinning him; held the belt for a few minutes, until Firebird brings it down on the back of his head and Black Eagle covers him.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Black Eagle

won.source: Remember November, Friday, 26th November 2011 (in-game): the All Action title is declared up for grabs all night; the diary's own title records list "Black Eagle November 2011 0" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won from Kid Arachnid backstage at Remember November, after Firebird hits Arachnid with the belt and Eagle pins him; he is sneaking out of the arena with it when a hooded backstage worker drops him into a stack of chairs.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Wanda Fish

won.source: Remember November, Friday, 26th November 2011 (in-game): the All Action title is declared up for grabs all night; the diary's own title records list "Wanda Fish November 2011 0 1st female champion" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won from Black Eagle in the arena corridor at Remember November by dropping him into a stack of chairs and covering him; she is revealed as Wanda Fish, the first woman to hold the belt, and loses it a few minutes later when Shady K and Knuckles corner her.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Knuckles

won.source: Remember November, Friday, 26th November 2011 (in-game): the All Action title is declared up for grabs all night; the diary's own title records list "Knuckles November 2011 0" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won from Wanda Fish in the corridor at Remember November with a clothesline, a big boot and a one-foot cover; he and Shady K are posing in the ring after beating the West Texas Peacekeepers when Amazing Fire Fly comes out of the crowd.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Amazing Fire Fly

won.source: Remember November, Friday, 26th November 2011 (in-game): the All Action title is declared up for grabs all night; the diary's own title records list "Amazing Fire Fly November 2011 0" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won from Knuckles in the ring at Remember November with a Sky High Fire Fly after a dropsault from the crowd, monkey flip and spinning kicks on Shady K; he bounces backstage celebrating until JD Morgan chairs him and covers him with a foot on his throat.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: JD Morgan

won.source: Remember November, Friday, 26th November 2011 (in-game): the All Action title is declared up for grabs all night; the diary's own title records list "JD Morgan (2) November 2011 7" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Regained from Amazing Fire Fly backstage at Remember November with a chair and a foot on his throat, after the belt has changed hands six times in a night. He keeps it against Jonnie Perez and Providence in a three-way at End Of Days, where Haley Buck is at his side, and against Riley McManus at New Year, Old Rivalries, the Invitational tie that Rip Chord makes a title match too, with the Cross Atlantic Stretch; at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012 he is still the champion. He keeps the belt against Bradford Peverell at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February, Wanda Fish and Fumihiro Ota in a Triple Threat at All Or Nothing on 12th February, Kashmir Singh at Third Time's The Charm on 5th March and Kirk Jameson in a submission match at March Madness on 12th March, wins the Gold Rush match at April Showers on 5th April, taking the Traditional title in it, and loses the All Action belt to Donnie J in a ladder match at South East Crisis on 8th April 2012. The diary's own title records list the reign as "JD Morgan (2) November 2011 7".

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Donnie J

won.source: South East Crisis, Monday, 8th April 2012 (in-game): "Donnie J vs. JD Morgan (c) in a ladder match for the MAW All Action title ... Winner: Donnie J (C+)"; the diary's own title records list "Donnie J April 2012 0" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won from JD Morgan in a ladder match at South East Crisis, which Rip Chord orders so that Donnie can feel at home, the belt hung from a hook fifteen feet over the ring: Morgan topples the ladder from the top, J lands on the top rope, slingshots himself back on a second ladder, grabs the belt and hangs from it with a wide smile until the catches give way and he drops to the mat holding it, as Haley Buck screeches at ringside. He loses it to Aaron Andrews in the title-versus-title match at May The Force Be With You on 5th May 2012.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Aaron Andrews

won.source: May The Force Be With You, Friday, 5th May 2012 (in-game): "Donnie J (c) vs. Aaron Andrews (c) for the MAW All Action and MAW Heavyweight titles ... Winner: Aaron Andrews (B-)"; the diary's own title records list "Aaron Andrews May 2012 0" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won at May The Force Be With You in the title-versus-title match that Rip Chord announces, the All Action belt being, in his words, a little spicier than the others, one he can put on the line at any time: Andrews, who already holds the Heavyweight title, beats Donnie J in twenty-two minutes by blocking a dive from the top rope with a standing leap, turning it into a superplex and winning with the Twisting Face Crusher, and so becomes a double champion. He loses the All Action belt back to Donnie J at Great Lakes Madness four days later.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Donnie J

won.source: Great Lakes Madness, Tuesday, 9th May 2012 (Great Lakes, in-game): "Donnie J vs. Aaron Andrews (c) for the MAW All Action title in a two out of three falls match ... Winner: Donnie J (B-)"; the diary's own title records list "Donnie J (2) May 2012 7" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Regained at Great Lakes Madness, after he asks for the rematch his contract gives him, in a two-out-of-three-falls match for the All Action title only (Rip Chord will not give him a Heavyweight title match after losing a week before): Andrews takes the first fall in under ten minutes with a Twisting Face Crusher, Donnie levels it with the Death On Miami Beach after almost fifteen minutes, and in the slower third fall he catches Andrews's leg, drills him with a dragon whip and rolls up into a bridging cradle for three. At Mother, May I? on 12th May he fails to win the Heavyweight title from Andrews in a thirty-minute Iron Man match; he keeps the belt against Father Johan in a pole match at High Noon on 5th June 2012, Firebird in a submission match at South East Madness on 9th June, Eddie Powell and Citizen X at Summer Showdown on 12th June, Firebird again at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, JD Morgan in a thirty-minute draw for this and the Traditional title at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July, Powell and Rudy Velasquez at Summernova on 5th August and Providence in a ladder match at South East Grand Parade on 9th August, and loses it to Black Eagle, who pins him backstage with Firebird's help, at Iron on 12th August.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Black Eagle

won.source: Iron, Friday, 12th August 2012 (in-game): Black Eagle pins "Dogfight" Donnie J backstage for the MAW All Action title, and Donnie J pins him in a corridor to "recover his All Action title"; the diary's own title records list "Black Eagle (2) August 2012 3" and "Donnie J (3) August 2012 0" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Won backstage at Iron when Rip Chord declares that the title can change hands anywhere so long as a qualified referee is there to make the call: Donnie J is ambushed from both sides by the Dark Raptors, Firebird throws him into a stack of crates, and when Eagle seizes his partner from behind and throws him headfirst into Donnie, Eagle dives on top of the champion and gets a three count, taking the title from round Donnie's waist. Amazing Fire Fly's Cutter through a table brings a two count that Firebird breaks up, and Lassana Makutsi's challenge is met with kicks; Firebird then turns on Eagle in a darkened corridor, and Donnie J, who blasts Firebird with a metal briefcase, pins the gasping Eagle with a Death From Miami Beach to take the belt back the same night.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Donnie J

won.source: Iron, Friday, 12th August 2012 (in-game): Donnie J pins Black Eagle backstage "to recover his All Action title"; the diary's own title records list "Donnie J (3) August 2012 0" under MAW All Action.

reigns.how: Regained the same night at Iron, in a darkened backstage corridor, after Firebird turns on Black Eagle: Donnie hits Firebird in the face with a metal briefcase, scores with a Death From Miami Beach on the still-gasping Eagle and makes the three-count, then winks at Sienna LeNoir and asks whether it reminds her of anyone she used to know. He is still the All Action champion at the end of this range, standing with Kashmir Singh and Brandon Smith to protect Sienna at Back To School on 5th September.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Erik Strong

won.source: The diary's own title records at the end of the saved copy ("Final MAW Title Records 2005 – 2018", under MAW World): "Erik Strong June 2007 8" (won, defences; in-game dates). The Rip Chord Invitational card (Friday 26th January 2008) bills him "Erik Strong (c)".

reigns.how: Erik Strong's reign, won in June 2007 by the diary's own title records, which count eight defences. He holds the belt as the diary opens and retains it at each defence until Where It All Begins Again, where he loses a three-way to Jean Cattley and Black Eagle.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Jean Cattley

won.source: Where It All Begins Again, Friday 26th October 2008 (in-game); the diary's own title records list "Machine" Jean Cattley (2), won October 2008, under MAW World.

reigns.how: Won the belt for the second time by pinning Erik Strong in the three-way at Where It All Begins Again; the card for Remember November bills him as champion. He loses the belt to Steven Parker in a thirty-minute Iron Man match at Where It All Begins Again in October 2009.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Steven Parker

won.source: Where It All Begins Again, Friday, October 26th 2009 (in-game): "Steven Parker vs. "Machine" Jean Cattley (c) for the MAW Heavyweight title in a thirty minute Iron Man match ... Winner: Steven Parker (C)"; the diary's own title records list "Steven Parker (2) October 2009 10" under MAW World.

reigns.how: Won from Jean Cattley with a Future Shock at 29:21 of a thirty-minute Iron Man match at Where It All Begins Again; he keeps the belt against Darryl Devine at Remember November and Cameron Vessey at End Of Days and against Champagne Lover at The Rip Chord Invitational, then loses it that night to Jay Chord, who cashes in his guaranteed title shot straight after the match.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Jay Chord

won.source: The Rip Chord Invitational, Saturday, January 27th 2010 (in-game): "Steven Parker (c) vs. Jay Chord for the MAW Heavyweight title ... Winner: Jay Chord (D)"; the diary's own title records list "Jay Chord January 2010 16" under MAW World.

reigns.how: Won from Steven Parker with a Cradle Piledriver right after Parker's defence against Champagne Lover, by cashing in the title shot guaranteed to the 2009 Rip Chord Invitational winner; he keeps the belt against Thom Morgan, Stevie Grayson, Amazing Fire Fly and Kirk Jameson, fights Aaron Andrews to a time-limit draw at April Showers, and keeps it against Erik Strong at Summer Showdown in June 2010, the Masked Patriot at Beach Blast, Fumihiro Ota and Firebird in a three-way at Summernova, Brandon Smith at Iron, Steve Flash at Back To School and Trent Shaffer at All The Leaves Are Brown, until he loses it to Aaron Andrews in a thirty-minute Iron Man match at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2010, by two falls to one.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Aaron Andrews

won.source: Where It All Begins Again, Friday, 26th October 2010 (in-game): "Aaron Andrews vs. Jay Chord (c) for the MAW Heavyweight title ... Winner: Aaron Andrews (2-1, C-)"; the diary's own title records list "Aaron Andrews October 2010 41" under MAW World.

reigns.how: Won from Jay Chord in a thirty-minute Iron Man match at Where It All Begins Again, by two falls to one: Jay took the first with a Super DDT, Andrews levelled with a Standing Hot Shot, and after Rip Chord's bell, Andrews's plancha on Rip and a second Standing Hot Shot the referee ruled that Jay's shoulders had been down for the full count of the last fall while Andrews's had come up at two; he keeps the belt against Joey Poison (Toxin) at Eleventh Hour in November, Hugh de Aske at Remember November, Matthew Gauge at Season's Beatings, Jay Chord in a street fight at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011, Primus Allen at The Rip Chord Invitational, Firebird at March Madness and JD Morgan at April Showers. He keeps it against Black Eagle on 12th May, Erik Strong on 26th May, Kirk Jameson, Hugh de Aske, JD Morgan, Firebird and Jay Chord in a six-man Gold Rush match on 12th June, Fumihiro Ota on 12th July, Hugh de Aske on 26th July, Steve Flash on 12th August, Chance Fortune on 26th August and Ernest Youngman on 12th September, Brandon Smith on 26th September, Randy Bumfhole in a time-limit draw on 12th October, Kirk Jameson on 26th October, Chance Fortune on 22nd November, Steve Flash on 26th November, Fumihiro Ota on 12th December and Randy Bumfhole at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012, Jared Johnson at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February 2012, Kashmir Singh on 12th February, Wanda Fish on 2nd March in her last match, Brandon Smith on 5th March, Jim Force on 12th March, Steve Gumble on 8th April, Randy Bumfhole in a steel cage match on 12th April, which the narrator counts as his thirtieth title defence, and Donnie J in a title-versus-title match on 5th May and a thirty-minute Iron Man match on 12th May, having used the right to refuse a challenger that is written into his contract to have Randy Bumfhole thrown out of the Gold Rush match at April Showers; in the diary's pages from June to September 2012 he keeps it against Lassana Makutsi on 5th June, Fumihiro Ota on 9th June, in what the narrator counts as his thirty-fourth defence, KC Glenn on 12th June, Bradford Peverell on 5th July, Kid Toma on 12th July and Rich Money in a thirty-minute draw on 5th August, and is still the champion at the end of this range.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-rip-chord-invitational
reigns.label: Antonio

won.source: The diary's own title records, under Rip Chord Invitational: "Antonio January 2008 Tournament Final"; the diary's January 2009 news column says "Antonio won the tournament last year".

reigns.how: The 2008 Rip Chord Invitational winner, called "the reigning RCI champion" in the diary's January 2009 news column; the title passes to the 2009 tournament's winner, Kid Arachnid.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-rip-chord-invitational
reigns.label: Kid Arachnid

won.source: The Rip Chord Invitational, Saturday, January 27th 2009 (in-game): "Rip Chord Invitational Final: Fumihiro Ota vs. Kid Arachnid ... Winner: Kid Arachnid (D+)"; the diary's own title records list "Kid Arachnid (Jay Chord) January 2009 Tournament Final" under Rip Chord Invitational.

reigns.how: Won the final over Fumihiro Ota at The Rip Chord Invitational with a Cradle Piledriver and was unmasked as Rip Chord's son Jay when he used Rip's own DDT on the Invitational trophy; still the champion at the end of this range. The title passes to the 2010 tournament's winner, Primus Allen.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-rip-chord-invitational
reigns.label: Primus Allen

won.source: The Rip Chord Invitational, Saturday, January 27th 2010 (in-game): "RCI Final: Erik Strong vs. Primus Allen ... Winner: Primus Allen (D-)"; the diary's own title records list "Primus Allen January 2010 Tournament Final" under Rip Chord Invitational.

reigns.how: Won the 2010 tournament final over Erik Strong with the Running Powerslam, after beating Stevie Grayson and Kirk Jameson; he stays the Firm's enforcer and the Invitational champion through the rest of this range, and puts his career against the Masked Patriot's mask at All Or Nothing. His reign ends at the 2011 tournament on 21st January 2011: he spends the title shot his crown carries on a Heavyweight title match against Aaron Andrews the same night and loses to a Standing Hot Shot and a dive from the top rope, and Kirk Jameson wins the tournament.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-rip-chord-invitational
reigns.label: Kirk Jameson

won.source: The Rip Chord Invitational, Sunday, 21st January 2011 (in-game): "Final: Kirk Jameson vs. Hugh de Aske for the Rip Chord Invitational Challenge title ... Winner: Kirk Jameson (C+)"; the diary's own title records list "Kirk Jameson January 2011 Tournament Final" under Rip Chord Invitational.

reigns.how: Won the 2011 tournament on its one night, beating Antonio with the Bullseye, Firebird with a Bullseye from the top rope and Hugh de Aske, in their third match of the night, with a counter into a Bullseye and an arm across the chest, and is handed the trophy by Rip Chord; he spends the guaranteed title shot his crown carries on Aaron Andrews at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011 and loses, and holds the Invitational title until Kid Arachnid wins the 2012 tournament on 12th January 2012.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-rip-chord-invitational
reigns.label: Kid Arachnid

won.source: The Rip Chord Invitational, Friday, 12th January 2012 (in-game): "RCI: Kid Arachnid vs. JD Morgan for the Rip Chord Invitational title ... Winner: Kid Arachnid (C-)"; the diary's own title records list "Kid Arachnid (KC Glenn) January 2012 Tournament Final" under Rip Chord Invitational.

reigns.how: Won the 2012 tournament on its one night, beating Jared Johnson with a Cradle Piledriver, Firebird with a Cradle Piledriver and JD Morgan in the final with a Cradle Piledriver and a Superkick, Morgan having been distracted when he looks to Haley Buck for guidance; he is handed the trophy by Rip Chord and takes off the mask to say that his name is KC Glenn. He cashes in his guaranteed title shot against Aaron Andrews at Summer Showdown on 12th June 2012 and loses, and leaves MAW after Beach Blast on 12th July; the diary's pages in this range do not say who holds the Invitational title next.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Canadian Blondes

won.source: The diary's own title records at the end of the saved copy ("Final MAW Title Records 2005 – 2018", under the tag titles): "The Canadian Blondes (2) June 2007 3" (won, defences; in-game dates). The Rip Chord Invitational (Friday 26th January 2008) bills them as the champions.

reigns.how: The Canadian Blondes' second reign, won in June 2007 by the diary's own title records, which count three defences; Oscar Golden and Flash Savage defend against Perez & Shaffer in January and April 2008 before losing the belts in the Beach Blast ladder match.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Perez & Shaffer

won.source: Beach Blast, Friday 26th July 2008 (in-game); the diary's own title records list "Perez & Shaffer July 2008 1".

reigns.how: Won the belts in the Beach Blast ladder match, defended them against C-V-2 at Iron and lost the team when Frankie Perez left for WLW, so that Trent Shaffer carried the belts into the next show with a new partner.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Shaffer & Grayson

won.source: Fall Of The King, Friday 26th September 2008 (in-game); the diary's own title records list "Grayson & Shaffer September 2008 5" with the note "S. Grayson replaced F. Perez"; the text does not say when Frankie Perez left, only that Trent Shaffer brought a new partner.

reigns.how: Trent Shaffer, still holding the belts, introduces Stevie Grayson as his new partner and the pair keep them against Stardust and Raphael and against Jacob Jett and Findlay O'Farraday; the card for Remember November has C-V-2 as the challengers. They lose the belts to the Gauge Brothers at The Rip Chord Invitational in January 2009.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Gauge Brothers

won.source: The Rip Chord Invitational, Saturday, January 27th 2009 (in-game): "Shaffer & Grayson (c) vs. The Gauge Brothers for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: The Gauge Brothers (C-)"; the diary's own title records list "The Gauge Brothers January 2009 1 M. & G. Gauge" under MAW Tag Team.

reigns.how: Won in the tag title match at The Rip Chord Invitational, when Greg Gauge caught Trent Shaffer in a Depth Gauge, and lost at All Or Nothing a month later to Morgan & Benning, who were the quickest winners of the night's qualifying matches.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Morgan & Benning

won.source: All Or Nothing, Friday 26th February 2009 (in-game): "Morgan & Benning vs. The Gauge Brothers (c) for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: Morgan & Benning (D)"; the diary's own title records list "Morgan & Benning February 2009 2 T.Morgan/J.Benning" under MAW Tag Team.

reigns.how: Won at All Or Nothing with Morgan's Finest and a Joe And Behold, kept against C-V-2 at March Madness and the Canadian Blondes at Spring Fever, kept the belts when C-V-2 won a Summer Showdown match by countout, and lost them to C-V-2 at Iron.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: C-V-2

won.source: Iron, Friday, 26th August 2009 (in-game): "Morgan & Benning (c) vs. C-V-2 for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: C-V-2 (D-)"; the diary's own title records list the reign as "Valentine & Johnson August 2009 9 J. Johnson replaced C. Vessey", which names the later line-up.

reigns.how: Won at Iron when Cameron Vessey caught Joe Benning with a Flying V, and still the champions at the end of this range, with Internet Favourites booked against them on the card for Fall Of The King. Cameron Vessey leaves for USPW in March 2010 and Casey Valentine carries the belts on with Jared Johnson.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Valentine & Johnson

won.source: April Showers, Tuesday, 16th April 2010 (in-game): "Morgan & Benning vs. Antonio and Raphael vs. Valentine & Johnson (c) for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: Valentine & Johnson (D-)"; the text does not say which day Johnson was brought in: the February 2010 page says Vessey "would be leaving before the next show" and March Madness has Valentine with no partner. The diary's own title records list the whole reign, from the Iron win, as "Valentine & Johnson August 2009 9 J. Johnson replaced C. Vessey".

reigns.how: The belts C-V-2 won at Iron pass into the hands of Casey Valentine and his new partner Jared Johnson when Cameron Vessey leaves for USPW; they keep them in the April Showers three-way with Morgan & Benning and Antonio & Raphael, against Morgan & Benning at Spring Fever and against Shaffer & Grayson at Mother, May I?, against the Internet Favourites at Beach Blast, against Morgan & Benning at Iron and in a three-way with the Internet Favourites and Ricochet & Sharp at Back To School, and lose them to the Canadian Blondes in a three-way at Fall Of The King on 26th September 2010, Johnson carrying the match while Valentine looks disinterested after his quarrel with Jean Cattley.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Canadian Blondes

won.source: Fall Of The King, Friday, 26th September 2010 (in-game): "Internet Favourites vs. Valentine & Johnson (c) vs. The Canadian Blondes for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: The Canadian Blondes (D-)"; the diary's own title records list "The Canadian Blondes (3) September 2010 6" under MAW Tag Team.

reigns.how: Won from Valentine & Johnson in a three-way with the Internet Favourites at Fall Of The King, after Jared Johnson eliminated the Favourites and the Blondes overwhelmed him with their tandem offence: the team's record third reign. They keep the belts in a four-team ladder match against the Bailey Boys, Morgan & Benning and Antonio & Raphael at Where It All Begins Again in October 2010, with Flash Savage retrieving them, and against Brandon Smith and Joe Benning on the 11th November tour show, against Smith & Singh at Remember November in November 2010, when Flash Savage pulls down the top rope and Smith is beaten with a Canadian Crab, against the Internet Favourites on the 11th December tour show, the Bailey Boys at Season's Beatings and Smith & Singh on the 25th December tour show, and lose them to Kashmir Singh and Jean Cattley at New Year, Old Rivalries on 12th January 2011, when Singh names Cattley as his partner in place of the injured Brandon Smith.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Cattley & Singh

won.source: New Year, Old Rivalries, Friday, 12th January 2011 (in-game): "'Machine' Jean Cattley and Kashmir Singh vs. The Canadian Blondes (c) for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: Cattley and Singh (D+)"; the diary's own title records list "Cattley & Singh January 2011 3" under MAW Tag Team.

reigns.how: Won from the Canadian Blondes at New Year, Old Rivalries when Kashmir Singh, using the clause that a winning team would get a title match without naming Brandon Smith, brings in Jean Cattley as his partner and Cattley scores with the Mood Swing on Flash Savage. They keep the belts against Antonio & Raphael at Leap Into The Unknown, the Blondes at Third Time's The Charm and Thrash and Firebird at April Showers, until the Canadian Blondes take the belts from them at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, Oscar Golden pinning Cattley with the Golden Shower; Cattley then loses a Loser Leaves Town match to Casey Valentine and leaves for the SWF.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Canadian Blondes

won.source: Spring Fever, Tuesday, 23rd April 2011 (in-game): "Kashmir Singh and 'Machine' Jean Cattley (c) vs. The Canadian Blondes for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: The Canadian Blondes (D)"; the diary's own title records list "The Canadian Blondes (4) April 2011 11" under MAW Tag Team.

reigns.how: Won from Cattley & Singh at Spring Fever, ten minutes in, when the champions' lack of cohesion lets them down once more and Oscar Golden scores the pin on Jean Cattley with the Golden Shower; the narrator notes that the Blondes have more than a hundred matches together as a team. They keep the belts against the Young Americans on 12th May, Smith & Singh and the Dark Raptors in a three-way on 26th May, Kid Arachnid and Amazing Fire Fly on 12th June, the West Texas Peacekeepers on 26th June, when they debut the O, Canada!, Smith & Singh and Ford & Speed in a three-way on 12th July, Leftie Wilkes and Ben Williams on 26th July, The Quest on 26th August and the Young Americans on the 4th September tour show, the Young Americans and Smith & Singh in a three-way at Fall Of The King on 26th September, the Young Americans on the 3rd October tour show and the Internet Favourites on 24th October, until Smith & Singh take the belts from them at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011, Kashmir Singh catching Oscar Golden with the Cal-Cutter, and so end the reign at six months.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Smith & Singh

won.source: Where It All Begins Again, Friday, 26th October 2011 (in-game): "Smith & Singh vs. The Canadian Blondes (c) for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: Smith & Singh (D+)"; the diary's own title records list "Smith & Singh October 2011 10 B.Smith/K.Singh (2)" under MAW Tag Team.

reigns.how: Won from the Canadian Blondes at Where It All Begins Again, ending their fourth reign at the six-month mark: Kashmir Singh plays face-in-peril for the Blondes' showboating until Flash Savage crashes and burns on a springboard senton and Brandon Smith bulls his way through the champions, and Singh catches a rising Oscar Golden with the Cal-Cutter. They keep the belts against the Second Sons at Remember November, in a three-way with the Dark Raptors and Ford & Speed at Season's Beatings, against Ford & Speed at End Of Days, against Firebird and Citizen X at New Year, Old Rivalries (Smith finally beating Citizen X) and, at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January 2012, in a three-way with Ford & Speed and Lockdown, when Singh pins Greg Ford with a Cal Cutter after Lockdown have been put out; at Great Lakes Crisis on 2nd March 2012 they beat the Canadian Blondes, who have cashed in their rematch, Smith finishing Flash Savage with a Backdrop Driver, at March Madness on 12th March they beat the Second Sons, Singh pinning Antonio with a Bombay Duck, and at May The Force Be With You on 5th May they beat the Second Sons again with Smith's Backdrop Driver on Casey Valentine; at High Noon on 5th June 2012 they keep the belts in a three-way against the Second Sons and Ford & Speed, Smith catching Casey Valentine with an Inverted Piledriver, and at Summer Showdown on 12th June they lose them to The Dark Raptors, Firebird pinning Singh with the Phoenix Firebird Splash.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Dark Raptors

won.source: Summer Showdown, Friday, 12th June 2012 (in-game): "Smith & Singh (c) vs. The Dark Raptors for the MAW Tag Team title ... Winners: The Dark Raptors (C-)"; the diary's own title records list "The Dark Raptors June 2012 3 Firebird/B. Eagle" under MAW Tag Team.

reigns.how: Won from Smith & Singh at Summer Showdown, on the night Black Eagle returns from his spinal surgery: Eagle, freshly healed, avoids and evades the champions' early attacks before bringing Firebird in, Firebird wears Singh down with precision strikes, and when Eagle ambushes Smith and takes him over the top rope with a leg lariat, Firebird gets Singh down on the mat and scores with the Phoenix Firebird Splash. They keep the belts against the West Texas Peacekeepers on 9th July 2012, the XX Factor on 5th August and Spectrum Infinity on 12th August, and lose them to Team Honor at Back To School on 5th September, when Jared Johnson's MDK Powerbomb leaves Eagle vulnerable to Lassana Makutsi's Carolina Crossface.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Team Honor

won.source: Back To School, Friday, 5th September 2012 (in-game): "Team Honor vs. The Dark Raptors (c) for the MAW Tag Team titles ... Winners: Team Honor (C-)"; the diary's own title records list "Team Honor September 2012 4 J. Johnson/L. Makutsi" under MAW Tag Team.

reigns.how: Won at Back To School from the champions Firebird and Black Eagle, whom they were not much fancied to beat: Jared Johnson matches the Dark Raptors hold for hold while Lassana Makutsi takes to the air as gracefully as the masked men before outbrawling them on the mat; Eagle turns to Sienna LeNoir for support and gets none, walks into Johnson's MDK Powerbomb, and Makutsi drills Firebird with a Lassana Stunner to stop his interference and locks the Carolina Crossface on Eagle, who taps out. They are still the champions at the end of this range.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Stevie Grayson

won.source: March Madness, Friday 26th March 2009 (in-game): "Mayhem Battle Royal for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Stevie Grayson (D)"; the diary's own title records list "Stevie Grayson March 2009 4 Won in a Battle Royal" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: The first Traditional champion, who won the Mayhem Battle Royal at March Madness with a Shining Wizard on the Masked Patriot, and kept the belt against Jay Chord at Spring Fever and Curtis Jenkins at Summer Showdown before losing it to Darryl Devine at Beach Blast.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Darryl Devine

won.source: Beach Blast, Friday, 26th July 2009 (in-game): "Stevie Grayson (c) vs. Darryl Devine for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Darryl Devine (D+)"; the diary's own title records list "Darryl Devine July 2009 1" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won from Stevie Grayson at Beach Blast with the Devine Dream Drop, and kept the belt at Iron with a Super Devine Dream Drop on Ultimate Phoenix; still the champion at the end of this range. He loses the belt to Stevie Grayson at Where It All Begins Again in October 2009.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Stevie Grayson

won.source: Where It All Begins Again, Friday, October 26th 2009 (in-game): "Stevie Grayson vs. Darryl Devine (c) for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Stevie Grayson (D+)"; the diary's own title records list "Stevie Grayson (2) October 2009 6" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: His second Traditional reign, won back from Darryl Devine with the 460 Degree Splash at Where It All Begins Again; he is off his game against Hugh de Aske at End Of Days and loses the belt to the Cut Throat Driver.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Hugh de Aske

won.source: End Of Days, Friday, 26th December 2009 (in-game): "Stevie Grayson (c) vs. Hugh de Aske for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Hugh de Aske (D)"; the diary's own title records list "Hugh de Aske December 2009 7" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won from Stevie Grayson with a Cut Throat Driver at End Of Days, the pirate's first title; he keeps it against Fumihiro Ota at The Rip Chord Invitational, Hugh Lee at All Or Nothing, "Bulldozer" Brandon Smith (a time-limit draw) at March Madness and Kirk Jameson at April Showers, and loses it to Aaron Andrews at Spring Fever.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Aaron Andrews

won.source: Spring Fever, Friday, 26th April 2010 (in-game): "Aaron Andrews vs. Hugh de Aske (c) for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Aaron Andrews (C)"; the diary's own title records list "Aaron Andrews April 2010 4" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won from Hugh de Aske with a Flying Body Press in the Spring Fever main event, a match Jay Chord and Rip Chord gave him in place of a Heavyweight shot; he keeps the belt against Antonio at Mother, May I?, against Casey Valentine and Jared Johnson in a triangle match at Summer Showdown, Firebird at Hotter Than Hot and Toxin at Beach Blast, until Primus Allen beats him at Iron on 26th August 2010.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Primus Allen

won.source: Iron, Friday, 26th August 2010 (in-game): "Aaron Andrews (c) vs. Primus Allen for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Primus Allen (C-)"; the diary's own title records list "Primus Allen August 2010 2" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won from Aaron Andrews at Iron when he caught Andrews's leap from the turnbuckles and turned it into a Powerslam, the title becoming "the property of The Firm"; he keeps it against Kirk Jameson at Back To School and Joe Benning at Fall Of The King, both with the Running Powerslam, and loses it at Where It All Begins Again, when he runs shoulder-first into the ringpost against his handpicked challenger Jonnie Perez and taps out to the P-Clutch.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Jonnie Perez

won.source: Where It All Begins Again, Friday, 26th October 2010 (in-game): "Jonnie Perez vs. Primus Allen (c) for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Jonnie Perez (D-)"; the diary's own title records list "Jonnie Perez October 2010 10" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won from Primus Allen at Where It All Begins Again in only his third MAW match, with a P-Clutch on the shoulder Allen had hurt on the ringpost; he keeps the belt against Raphael on the 4th November tour show, Curtis Jenkins on the 11th and Antonio on the 25th, Jared Johnson on the 4th and 11th December tour shows and again on 4th January, Roderick Remus on the 25th December tour show, Matthew Gauge at End Of Days on 26th December and Jefferson Stardust on 11th January 2011, and loses it to Gauge at The Rip Chord Invitational on 21st January when Gauge twists out of the P-Clutch into a Depth Gauge.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Matthew Gauge

won.source: The Rip Chord Invitational, Sunday, 21st January 2011 (in-game): "Jonnie Perez (c) vs. Matthew Gauge for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Matthew Gauge (C)"; the diary's own title records list "Matthew Gauge January 2011 0" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won from Jonnie Perez at The Rip Chord Invitational when Perez, who has Gauge wilting in the P-Clutch, slackens his grip and Gauge twists loose into a Depth Gauge; the shortest of reigns, as Gauge's commitments in Japan are known to the better-informed fans and he has to drop the belt at Leap Into The Unknown, losing it to Hugh de Aske in a three-way with Perez.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Hugh de Aske

won.source: Leap Into The Unknown, Friday, 12th February 2011 (in-game): "Jonnie Perez vs. Matthew Gauge (c) vs. Hugh de Aske for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Hugh de Aske (C-)"; the diary's own title records list "Hugh de Aske (2) February 2011 6" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won from Matthew Gauge in a three-way with Jonnie Perez at Leap Into The Unknown with the Cutthroat Driver, a belt Gauge has to drop because he is leaving for Japan; he keeps it against Perez on the 18th February tour show, Jean Cattley at All Or Nothing and "Regular" Joe Benning at Third Time's The Charm. He keeps it against Fumihiro Ota at Spring Fever on 23rd April 2011, Providence on 26th May, Black Eagle on 26th June and, in a fifteen-minute draw, Jay Chord on 12th July, is no longer available for the touring shows now that, in the narrator's words, he has "wised up to his true worth", and loses the belt to Primus Allen at Summernova on 12th August 2011.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: Primus Allen

won.source: Summernova, Friday, 12th August 2011 (in-game): "Hugh de Aske (c) vs. Primus Allen for the MAW Traditional title ... Winner: Primus Allen (C)"; the diary's own title records list "Primus Allen (2) August 2011 9" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won from Hugh de Aske at Summernova with a Sitout Spinebuster, after throwing the champion into a bank of lockers backstage and carrying the match through a flying lariat that seemed to give Hugh the answer; the second reign of his career. He keeps the belt against Ernest Youngman at Iron on 26th August, an extended squash, and against Steve Flash and Erik Strong in a three-way at Back To School on 12th September, Bradford Peverell at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October, Riley McManus at Season's Beatings, Jared Johnson in a fifteen-minute draw at End Of Days, Kid Arachnid on 5th January 2012 and Kirk Jameson at The Rip Chord Invitational on 12th January, KC Glenn in a time-limit draw at Leap Into The Unknown on 5th February 2012, Randy Bumfhole at Third Time's The Charm on 5th March and Lassana Makutsi at March Madness on 12th March, and loses it at April Showers on 5th April 2012 in the six-champion Gold Rush match, when JD Morgan hits him with A Shot Of JD and pins him.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-traditional-championship
reigns.label: JD Morgan

won.source: April Showers, Friday, 5th April 2012 (in-game): "KC Glenn vs. Brandon Smith vs. Kashmir Singh vs. JD Morgan (c) vs. Primus Allen (c) vs. Aaron Andrews (c) in a Gold Rush match ... Winner: JD Morgan (C)"; the diary's own title records list "JD Morgan April 2012 12 Won in a Gold Rush match" under MAW Traditional.

reigns.how: Won in the six-champion Gold Rush match at April Showers, which Rip Chord revives from the year before with every champion entered and a title lost to any champion who is pinned or made to submit: with Haley Buck screaming at him from the outside to make the cover, Morgan turns Primus Allen round into A Shot Of JD and pins him, so keeping the All Action title and taking the Traditional title as well. He keeps it against Bradford Peverell and Lord Geoffrey Windameer in a three-way at Mother, May I? on 12th May 2012, putting Peverell away with the Cross Atlantic Stretch after a half nelson suplex, and keeps it in the diary's pages from June to September 2012 against Steve Gumble in a draw at High Noon on 5th June, Amazing Fire Fly at Summer Showdown on 12th June, Gumble at Hotter Than Hot on 5th July, Donnie J in a thirty-minute draw at Great Lakes Grand Parade on 9th July, Black Eagle with the Mid Atlantic Stretch at Beach Blast on 12th July, Sean Deeley at South East Grand Parade on 9th August and Rudy Velasquez at Iron on 12th August; he is pinned by Deeley in a non-title six-man match at Back To School on 5th September, and is still the champion at the end of this range.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-trios-championship
reigns.label: The Firm

won.source: March Madness, Friday, 26th March 2010 (in-game): "The Watch vs. The Firm for the MAW Trios titles ... Winners: The Firm (D+)"; the diary's own title records list the reign as "Cattley, Allen & Powell March 2010 2", though the text puts Darryl Devine in the match and with a Trios belt.

reigns.how: Won in the first trios match, against The Watch, at March Madness, when Jean Cattley's Mood Swing finished Ultimate Phoenix; Jean Cattley, Darryl Devine and Ryan Powell carry the belts, and they keep them against Fumihiro Ota and the Internet Favourites at April Showers. Darryl Devine is gone by Summer Showdown in June 2010 and Primus Allen takes his place as the third man against Shane Nelson, Amazing Fire Fly and Riley McManus, with Allen and Ryan Powell scoring the pins; they lose the belts to Fumihiro Ota, Brandon Smith and Kashmir Singh at Hotter Than Hot on 9th July 2010, with Powell on his way to SWF.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-trios-championship
reigns.label: Smith, Ota & Singh

won.source: Hotter Than Hot, Tuesday, 9th July 2010 (in-game): "Ota, Smith and Singh vs. The Firm (c) for the MAW Trios titles ... Winners: Ota, Singh and Smith (D)"; the diary's own title records list "Smith, Ota & Singh July 2010 2" under MAW Trios.

reigns.how: Won from The Firm at Hotter Than Hot, with Ryan Powell, already on his way to SWF, on the losing side; Firebird chairs the new champions straight after the match. They keep the belts against Ricochet, Sharp and Toxin at Summernova and, in a two-fall win, against Jared Johnson, Nelson Callum and Roderick Remus at Eleventh Hour in November 2010, until The Triple Threat take the belts from them at Season's Beatings on 12th December 2010, when Firebird's appearance distracts Ota and Jared Johnson scores with the Carolina Crossface.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-trios-championship
reigns.label: The Triple Threat

won.source: Season's Beatings, Friday, 12th December 2010 (in-game): "Smith, Singh and Ota (c) vs. The Triple Threat for the MAW Trios titles ... Winners: The Triple Threat (D-)"; the diary's own title records list "Johnson, Remus & Callum December 2010 7" under MAW Trios.

reigns.how: Won from Smith, Ota & Singh at Season's Beatings, the team's first match, when Firebird's appearance distracts Fumihiro Ota and Jared Johnson scores with the Carolina Crossface. They keep the belts against Amazing Fire Fly and the Internet Favourites at End Of Days, against Amazing Fire Fly and the Bailey Brothers on 26th January 2011, against Matt Hocking, Joe Benning and Jonnie Perez on 4th March and against Amazing Fire Fly and Smith & Singh on 4th April, on the 4th May tour show against Riley McManus, Amazing Fire Fly and Jonnie Perez, on the 18th May tour show against the Young Americans and Amazing Fire Fly and on 4th July against Amazing Fire Fly and the West Texas Peacekeepers, until The Firm take the belts from them at Summernova on 12th August 2011, Kid Arachnid pinning Nelson Callum with the Cradle Piledriver.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-trios-championship
reigns.label: The Firm

won.source: Summernova, Friday, 12th August 2011 (in-game): "Kid Arachnid, Chance Fortune and Randy Bumfhole vs. The Triple Threat (c) for the MAW Trios title ... Winners: The Firm (D+)"; the diary's own title records list "Arachnid, Fortune & Bumfhole August 2011 1" under MAW Trios.

reigns.how: Won from The Triple Threat at Summernova, the first main-show defence of the belts in a long time, when Kid Arachnid, Chance Fortune and Randy Bumfhole, all debuted since the champions won the titles, see Bumfhole and Fortune taken out of the game and Nelson Callum left alone with Arachnid, who snares him with a Cradle Piledriver. They keep the belts against The Fallen at Back To School on 12th September, when Bumfhole catches Firebird with the Bumfhole Buster, and lose them to the Second Sons at Where It All Begins Again on 26th October 2011 when Casey Valentine pins Kid Arachnid with the Sweet Sweet Heartbreak, Chance Fortune and Antonio, and Randy Bumfhole and Cameron Vessey, having fought one another out of the match.

reigns.title: maw-10-simple-rules-trios-championship
reigns.label: The Second Sons

won.source: Where It All Begins Again, Friday, 26th October 2011 (in-game): "The Firm (c) vs. The Second Sons for the MAW Trios titles ... Winners: The Second Sons (C)"; the diary's own title records list "Vessey, Valentine & Antonio October 2011 - Retired November 2011" under MAW Trios.

reigns.how: Won from The Firm at Where It All Begins Again, when Chance Fortune and Antonio and Randy Bumfhole and Cameron Vessey cancel one another out and Casey Valentine, who has returned to an old routine of roundhouse punches, pins Kid Arachnid with the Sweet Sweet Heartbreak; Antonio, Casey Valentine and Cameron Vessey are the team, with Vessey on loan from USPW. At Eleventh Hour on 12th November Rip Chord retires the Trios titles and the three are thrown out of the battle royal for the new All Action title.

reigns.title: mbe-world-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Doc Silver

won.source: MBE's own Title History document (its 19th recorded reign): defeated Justin Evitable in a decision match at an earlier pay-per-view billed MBE Total Elimination, not itself served

reigns.note: Retained the title against Promo on the first fwrestling.com-era show read this pass (20 July 2007); no further title match survives in the held record.

reigns.title: mbe-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Thrillbillies

won.source: MBE's own Title History document (its 29th recorded reign) states the Thrillbillies won these titles from a prior champion team at an event billed MBE Awakenings, not itself served; the document's own printed day-and-month for this entry conflict with MBE's own FAQ, posted 29 June 2007, which already lists the Thrillbillies as champions, so only the year is used here

reigns.note: Retained the titles in a ladder match against the Sheffield Wednesday Lot on the first fwrestling.com-era show read this pass (20 July 2007); no further title match survives in the held record.

reigns.title: mbwf-1992-air-wave
reigns.label: The Electric Youth

won.source: The newsletter of 18 March 1993: the title "was won by THE ELECTRIC YOUTH at the M.B.W.F.'s WINTER BASH 1992" (promotions/mbwf-1992/archive/m-b-w-f-news-1993-03-18.html).

reigns.how: Beat Evil Einstein at Winter Bash 1992; billed to defend against him again at Friday Ferocity #6 on 26 March 1993; still champion when he beat Scourge at Grapple Wars.

reigns.title: mbwf-1992-all-comers
reigns.label: Colossus

won.source: Grapple Wars 1: "*FIRST* All-Comers Champion" (promotions/mbwf-1992/archive/m-b-w-f-grapple-wars-1-part-2-1993-06-18.html).

reigns.how: Won the final of the All-Comers tournament over Noose Lupack and was the title's first champion.

reigns.title: mbwf-1992-ladies-world
reigns.label: Angel Pit Bull

won.source: Grapple Wars 1: "*NEW* Ladies World Champion" (promotions/mbwf-1992/archive/m-b-w-f-grapple-wars-1-part-1-1993-06-18.html).

reigns.how: Beat the Countess with her Flip Side finisher.

reigns.title: mbwf-1992-ladies-world
reigns.label: The Countess
reigns.how: The first woman to enter the league, and so champion automatically; lost the title to Angel Pit Bull at Grapple Wars.

reigns.title: mbwf-1992-master-of-the-ring
reigns.label: The Gross Gladiator

won.source: The newsletter of 18 March 1993: "THE GROSS GLADIATOR took the Master of the Ring title when he defeated SCOURGE on 11.30.92, on a Monday Madness show" (promotions/mbwf-1992/archive/m-b-w-f-news-1993-03-18.html).

reigns.how: Beat Scourge on a Monday Madness show, with a defence due within 14 days; lost the title to the Great Tadaka at Grapple Wars.

reigns.title: mbwf-1992-master-of-the-ring
reigns.label: The Great Tadaka

won.source: Grapple Wars 1: "*NEW* Master of the Ring" (promotions/mbwf-1992/archive/m-b-w-f-grapple-wars-1-part-1-1993-06-18.html).

reigns.how: Pinned the Gross Gladiator in the third match after referee Don Animal counted three over a shoulder the announcers thought was off the mat.

reigns.title: mbwf-1992-master-of-the-ring
reigns.label: Scourge
reigns.how: Holder when the Gross Gladiator beat him on a Monday Madness show on 30 November 1992; no earlier date survives.

won.source: Recorded as the first champion winning a battle royal in Bulletin #08 at the Georgia Mountain Center, Gainesville, Georgia; the sheet does not name an opponent. The first champion.
Beat Jumpman Michael Jordan in Bulletin #11 at Cobo Hall, Detroit, Michigan.
Beat Lightning Mountain in a three-way dance in Bulletin #23 at Cobo Hall, Detroit, Michigan.
Beat King Of Extreme in Bulletin #25 at the Philadelphia Spectrum, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Beat Bloodscream in Bulletin #26 at the Georgia Dome, Atlanta, Georgia.
Beat "Dangerous" Dave Howard in Bulletin #28 at the Houston Civic Center, Houston, Texas. A second reign for Lightning Mountain.

Beat Lightning Mountain in a title-versus-title match in Bulletin #33 at the Alamo Dome, San Antonio, Texas. Champion's own STW World Heavyweight title was also on the line. In Bulletin #34, STW officially stripped Champion of this title, since he then also held both the STW and CPW World Heavyweight titles and could not devote the time to it; he is recorded as the last title holder, as in Bulletin #35 the belt was unified with the vacant International title to form the Unified Double Crown championship.

reigns.title: new-era-pcx
reigns.label: Chaos

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own International Intrigue pay-per-view (taped 20 June 2005, aired 5 September 2005, held show, enrichment-only, not served): the PRODIGY Classic Xtreme Championship tournament final, a Tables, Ladders and Chairs match in which the belt is winched fifteen feet above the ring and the only way to win is to climb to it. Chaos beats Dallas Carter, climbing the one working ladder after a Chaos Bomb off the top rope through a table bridged between two ladders. Carl Jacobs announces the result on air: "the winner of the match ... and the first ever New ERA PRODIGY CLASSIC(C) XTREME CHAMPION.......... CHAOS!" The same broadcast's own opening commentary establishes the title as new and vacant, created by Juliet Marceau's own 27 January 2005 RAPTURE announcement in honour of the old PRODIGY circuit where New ERA's founders started, and filled by a four-man tournament.

reigns.note: The FIRST reign of this title: the belt is crowned here, not merely defended. The chain into the tournament, all from the federation's own broadcasts: Chaos beats the Sinner in an Exploding Turnbuckles first-round match (17 February 2005 RAUCOUS); Marcus LaRoque fills the other three semifinal places from the final three of that same night's ten-man Newcomer Battle Royal, won by Rex Reynolds over Dallas Carter and Thomas Lombardi; Chaos then beats Thomas Lombardi in a Taipei Death Match on the RAPTURE whose own tape date is 28 May 2005, and Dallas Carter beats Rex Reynolds in a Buried Alive match on the 30 May 2005 RAUCOUS. The federation's own 19 September 2005 RAUCOUS still bills Chaos champion and has John Doe beat him in a non-title Falls Count Anywhere match to earn a shot at the belt; Doe wins the belt from him in a Leather Strap match on the 12 January 2006 RAUCOUS.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast of 12 January 2006: John Doe beats Chaos in a Leather Strap match and is announced 'NEW PRODIGY CLASSIC XTREME CHAMPION'.

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast of 12 January 2006: in a Leather Strap match John Doe beats the champion Chaos, and Carl Jacobs announces 'NEW PRODIGY CLASSIC XTREME CHAMPION ... JOHN DOE!'; the commentary calls it DREDD's first title victory in New ERA. The match follows his Falls Count Anywhere win over Chaos on the 19 September 2005 RAUCOUS.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 3 February 2006): Doe defends in a Scaffold and Tables match against Chaos and Trevor Cane, and Chaos Chaosbombs him from the scaffold through burning tables and is announced 'NEW PRODIGY© CLASSIC XTREME CHAMPION'.

The belt stays on him through all of them.

reigns.title: new-era-television
reigns.label: MWG

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own BattleBRAWL pay-per-view (3 December 2004, held show, enrichment-only, not served): MWG, the #1 contender since Alex Borden's stripping, enters last in the over-the-top BattleBRAWL Rumble and eliminates the final two men, Cameron Cruise and Jason Payne, together with a running knee lift. Carl Jacobs announces him on air as "the recipient of the FIRST EVER BattleBRAWL Championship Cup ... as WELL as the NEW ERA of WRESTLING TELEVISION CHAMPION." The broadcast's own pre-match commentary establishes the vacant title (stripped from Alex Borden on the 28 September 2004 RAUCOUS) was on the line, awarded to the rumble's own winner.

reigns.note: This is MWG's FIRST New ERA Television Championship reign; his second (already held as r001, won 20 June 2005 at International Intrigue) is a separate, later reign of the same title after it sat vacant for several months — see the correction to r001 in reigns-corrections-new-era-of-wrestling.json. This reign is numbered r006 rather than by date order to avoid an id collision with r002-r005, which are already assigned to the earlier reigns in this chain. True chronological order of the title's reigns to date: Jean Rabesque (r002, won 2004-04-05) -> Chaos (r003, won 2004-06-05) -> Suicide (r004, won 2004-07-06) -> Alex Borden (r005, won 2004-08-06) -> MWG's first reign (r006, this row, won 2004-12-03) -> MWG's second reign (r001, won 2005-06-20).

The referee rules the title cannot be awarded to either man ("the referee isn't awarding the title to EITHER competitor"), and it sits vacant. New ERA's own International Intrigue broadcast (20 June 2005) recaps this directly: "The championship was held in limbo the past few months, due to a spectacular match between Madonna Wayne Grossard and Jason Payne that ended in a draw."

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 19 September 2005, aired 4 January 2006; the show's own on-screen EPISODE heading reads RAUCOUS 22): in the main event the Phantom Republican pins the champion Jean Rabesque with a sunset flip and a handful of tights, after the Masked Man walks down the ramp and Rabesque abandons an almost-locked Figure Four to shout at him. Carl Jacobs announces the result on air: "Ladies and gentlemen .... The winner of this match ....... and NEW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION......... THE PHANTOM REPUBLICAN", and Tom Gheorghe closes the broadcast with "Phantom Republican ... is the World Heavyweight champion". The 12 January 2006 RAUCOUS card from which this reign's own start was previously inferred is the first captured card to follow this broadcast's own air date of 4 January 2006, and bills the same man champion.

reigns.note: The title-change match is recorded directly: New ERA's own RAUCOUS of 19 September 2005, aired 4 January 2006, in which the Phantom Republican pins Jean Rabesque with a sunset flip and a handful of tights while the Masked Man distracts the champion from the ramp (see won.source). The 12 January 2006 card's own retrospective line about ending Jean Rabesque's "year plus long reign" refers back to this same match rather than to a second one. The reign ends on the 5 July 2006 RAUCOUS, when Jonathan Marx wins the title in a Texas Tornado Tag Team match.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 5 July 2006): in a Texas Tornado Tag Team match Jonathan Marx makes Beau Michaels submit to the Marxism while the Phantom Republican is caught in the ropes, and Marx is announced the new World Heavyweight Champion.

reigns.title: new-era-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jonathan Marx

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 5 July 2006, aired 16 July 2006; on-screen RAUCOUS 25): in a Texas Tornado Tag Team match where a fall on either man of the champion's team wins the title, Jonathan Marx makes the Phantom Republican's partner Beau Michaels submit to the Marxism while the champion hangs in the ropes. Carl Jacobs announces ‘Your NEW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION … ‘GENTLEMAN’ … JONATHAN MARX!’.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 19 December 2006): Shawn Hart makes Marx's arm fall three times in the Fujiwara armbar in an impromptu title match, after John Doe and Jean Rabesque turn on him.

reigns.note: He retains over the Phantom Republican by submission at BattleBRAWL 2 (19 September 2006).

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 19 December 2006, aired 22 December 2006; on-screen RAUCOUS 27): the contract Jonathan Marx signs at a contract signing is for a title match that night, and Shawn Hart, the BattleBRAWL 2 rumble winner, wins with the Fujiwara armbar. Carl Jacobs announces him the new World Heavyweight Champion, Shawn Jessica Hart, PhD.

lost.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 31 December 2006): in a shopping-mall FAO Schwartz match Luster powerbombs Hart and drags Jonathan Marx over him for the three count.

reigns.title: new-era-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jonathan Marx

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own RAUCOUS broadcast (taped 31 December 2006, aired 15 January 2007; on-screen RAUCOUS 28): Jonathan Marx pins Shawn Hart in the FAO Schwartz Match, Dominican Style, after Luster's powerbomb on Hart, and regains the title; the commentary calls him the first man to hold it twice.

reigns.note: This is Marx's second reign. The end of the reign is not established in the broadcasts read for this entry.

reigns.title: new-era-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Shawn Hart

won.source: WFW:NE's own Unplugged card (18 July 2009) bills Larry Tact and Shawn Jessica Hart, PhD, both World Heavyweight Champion entering a stated unification match between them, the card's own main event; the following Destrucity II card (23 January 2010) bills Hart alone as champion.

reigns.note: No results document records the unification match's own outcome directly; the win is inferred from the following card's own billing. The co-championship this reign resolves is itself only attested by billing: a 28 June 2009 RAUCOUS card names Rocko Daymon and Larry Tact co-champions, and by 18 July 2009 the co-champion positions had shifted to Tact and Hart; no document in the held record explains the change between the two pairings.

reigns.title: new-era-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The First

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own BattleBRAWL 3 card (20 March 2011) already bills The First champion, entering a defense against a rival whose own promo on the same card states he took the belt from that rival directly; New ERA's own Cyberstrike 02 lineup (8 February 2011, read but not served) still billed that same rival champion six weeks earlier, bounding the change to within that window.

reigns.note: The exact date and event of this title change are not captured in the held record; the previous documented champions were 2009's co-titleholders. New ERA's own rules document (dated 15 January 2011 in its own text) separately states its reigning World Heavyweight Champion "became" the first champion under this renamed title at the same transition, without naming him.

reigns.title: new-era-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Mr. Entertainment

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own Cyberstrike 07 lineup (17 April 2011, read but not served) already bills Mr. Entertainment champion, four weeks after BattleBRAWL 3 billed The First; he is billed champion again three shows later at PrimeTime (31 May 2011).

reigns.note: No results document in the held record names how or when the title passed from The First to Mr. Entertainment; an honest gap bounded between two captured cards.

reigns.title: new-era-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Fanatic

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own PrimeTime card (31 May 2011) bills Mr. Entertainment defending against Fanatic in the main event; New ERA's own Cyberstrike 11 lineup (23 July 2011, read but not served) bills Fanatic champion two months later, indicating he won at or shortly after PrimeTime.

reigns.note: No results document survives for PrimeTime; the title change is inferred from the next captured card's own billing, the same method used for this title's earlier documented changes.

reigns.title: new-era-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The First

won.source: New ERA of Wrestling's own Cyberstrike 12 card (12 August 2011) bills Fanatic defending against The First in the main event; New ERA's own Cyberstrike 13 lineup (25 August 2011, read but not served) bills The First champion two weeks later. The First remains billed champion at BANNED in the US II (6 April 2015), defending against a wrestler cashing in a banked shot; his own roster bio card independently records two New ERA Championship reigns, matching this and his earlier r004 reign.

reigns.note: The First's title status between Cyberstrike 13 (25 August 2011) and BANNED in the US II (6 April 2015) is not captured in the held record, which carries no documents dated between the federation's own 2011 hiatus and its March 2015 return; whether he held the belt continuously or regained it during the unread gap is an honest open question. BANNED in the US II's own results are not captured, so whether he retained here is likewise unresolved.

reigns.how: Lost to John Hitchin at Xtrememania V, per Hitchin's own retrospective account the following night (results-tns185.html, 5 September 2004 capture, “the first post-XtremeMania Storm”): “Last night, in front of millions of people worldwide, I defeated the NGW Champion…EX-Champion Scott King for the World Title.” No exact date is held for this event itself — “last night” relative to the 5 September capture places it circa 4 September 2004.
reigns.note: Billed NGW World Heavyweight Champion on results-bf180.html (a show its own text places “next month” before Xtrememania V, i.e. roughly August 2004), and again on results-tns182.html (2 September 2004) defending against John Hitchin in the main event (won by DQ, no title change) — both narrowing this reign's own unknown win date to sometime between 1 June 2004 and roughly August 2004. This resolves most, but not all, of the wing's own flagged “champion at last word” contradiction (results-tns197.html, 22 February 2005, showed Hitchin, not Scott King, still defending the World Title): the served show corpus now shows Hitchin regaining the belt in early September 2004 and holding it at least through February 2005, spanning the November 2004 recap's own claim that Scott King was “champion at the fed's own last word” — that recap's own claim is not itself corroborated by any served show and is not resolved here, left standing as the recap's own word against the more granular dated show evidence.
