reigns.title: nlwf-2009-junior-heavyweight
reigns.label: Brenton Cyrus

won.source: New Era: 'the first ever Junior Heavyweight Champion, Brenton Cyrus' after the four-way.

reigns.how: Won the four-way for the first Junior Heavyweight title; lost it by disqualification to Johnny Electric on Direct Hit 7.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-junior-heavyweight
reigns.label: Johnny Electric

won.source: Direct Hit 7: Marissa Johnson announces 'new Jr Heavyweight Champion, Johnny Electric' and Carmine Vestieri rules the title can change on a disqualification.

reigns.how: Won the title by disqualification from Brenton Cyrus; lost it in a three-way at War Games.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-junior-heavyweight
reigns.label: Tapido Delevega

won.source: War Games: Tapido Delevega pins Bobby Ocean with the Seville Thrill and is called the new Junior Heavyweight Champion on Direct Hit 8.

reigns.how: Won a three-way at War Games; defended against Master of Disaster on Direct Hit 10; lost it to Alex Mark at King of the Throne.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-junior-heavyweight
reigns.label: Alex Mark

won.source: King of the Throne: Alex Mark wins the electrified barbed-wire match and is announced Junior Heavyweight Champion on Direct Hit 11.

reigns.how: Won the title from Tapido Delevega at King of the Throne; kept it against Anthony Bennett on Direct Hit 11; put it up in the unification match on Direct Hit 12.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-no-limit
reigns.label: Death Angel

won.source: Its champions page: Death Angel awarded the title on Direct Hit 03/10/09; Direct Hit 7 (14 March) calls him 'No Limit Champion Death Angel'.

reigns.how: Awarded the title; forfeited it to Chuck Matthews at the Hall of Fame show for Johnny Styles.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-no-limit
reigns.label: Chuck Matthews

won.source: Hall of Fame show for Johnny Styles: Ramirez Silva announces that Death Angel must forfeit the No Limit title to Chuck Matthews; its champions page dates the start 02/23/09, which the shows contradict.

reigns.how: Took the title in the trade with the West; kept it against Jake Stunner (Direct Hit 8, by Carmine Vestieri's ruling), against Anthony Bennett and Chad Vargas at King of the Throne, and against Jake Stunner on Direct Hit 13; lost it to Frank Hart at the Hall of Fame show for Joe Santiago.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-no-limit
reigns.label: Frank Hart

won.source: Hall of Fame show for Joe Santiago: 'new No Limit Champion, Frank Hart'.

reigns.how: Won the title from Chuck Matthews with the DVD Moment; kept it against Death Angel at Guilty as Charged; his champions page says he forfeited it; the date of the change to Swan Lee is not on the recovered pages.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-no-limit
reigns.label: Swan Lee

won.source: Simple Survival calls Swan Lee 'the current No Limit Champion' and he beats Hazard to keep it; its champions page says Frank Hart forfeited and lists Swan Lee as champion.

reigns.how: Champion by Simple Survival, where he retained against Hazard.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-north-american
reigns.label: Jackson

won.source: Tournament to the Title: 'the NLWF North American Champion, Jackson' after a match for the first title.

reigns.how: Won the first North American title in a match against Keith Cunningham at Tournament to the Title, breaking his own forearm along the way; lost it in the Best of Seven Series.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-north-american
reigns.label: Keith Cunningham

won.source: Direct Hit 5: Ramirez Silva ends the Best of Seven Series after Keith Cunningham leads two matches to one and names him 'the new North American Champion'.

reigns.how: Awarded the title after the Best of Seven Series; lost it to The Mexican Samurai in an MMA-rules match at War Games.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-north-american
reigns.label: The Mexican Samurai

won.source: War Games: The Mexican Samurai makes Keith Cunningham go limp in an armbar; its champions page records the change.

reigns.how: Won the title from Keith Cunningham at War Games; lost it in a three-way on Legacy 4.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-north-american
reigns.label: Frank Hart

won.source: Legacy 4: Frank Hart pins The Mexican Samurai with the Cardiac Arrest in a three-way with Peter Kaymakcian.

reigns.how: Won a three-way on Legacy 4; lost it to Alex Mark in the unification match on Direct Hit 12.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-north-american
reigns.label: Alex Mark

won.source: Direct Hit 12: 'the first ever Undisputed' North American Champion after beating Frank Hart in the unification match; its champions page records it.

reigns.how: As Junior Heavyweight Champion, beat Frank Hart in a unification match, absorbing the Junior Heavyweight title; lost the Undisputed North American title to Demetrius Randall in a Hangman Horrors match at Guilty as Charged.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-north-american
reigns.label: Demetrius Randall

won.source: Guilty as Charged: 'new North American Champion, Demetrius Randall'.

reigns.how: Won a Hangman Horrors match from Alex Mark; kept it against Tyler Lucas and Cain Alexander (Direct Hit 15) and Joe Santiago by forfeit; lost it to Frank Hart on Simple Survival.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-north-american
reigns.label: Frank Hart

won.source: Simple Survival: 'NEW North American Champion, Frank Hart'.

reigns.how: Won the title from Demetrius Randall at Simple Survival.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-proving-grounds
reigns.label: Conor O'Sullivan

won.source: Its champions page: Conor O'Sullivan beat Tantrum at Proving Grounds, 04/25/09; the Proving Grounds show is not among the recovered pages.

reigns.how: First champion on its champions page, from the Proving Grounds show; lost it to Aaron O'Shea in a three-way on Legacy 7.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-proving-grounds
reigns.label: Aaron O'Shea

won.source: Legacy 7: Aaron O'Shea pins Tantrum with the Dublin Domination in a three-way and is handed the title; its champions page dates it 05/09/09.

reigns.how: Won the Proving Grounds title from Conor O'Sullivan on Legacy 7; kept it against Tantrum and Outsider at Guilty as Charged; Direct Hit 14 says the title match was voided after his trade to Legacy, and he still carries it on Legacy 11.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-tag-team
reigns.label: Ryan Apollo

won.source: The one-year show: 'since Nick and Chuck can't compete at this time...RYAN APOLLO is the NEW NLWF TAG TEAM CHAMPION!'

reigns.how: Declared champion by default on the one-year show; his billed partner Brenton Cyrus was not there, and the announcer names only Ryan Apollo.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-tag-team
reigns.label: Nick Ridicule and Chuck Matthews

won.source: The one-year show bills 'Ridicule and Matthews' against 'Cyrus and Apollos', announcing 'one half of the tag-team champions, Nick Ridicule', and says Chuck Matthews is still missing.

reigns.how: Champions entering the one-year show; neither could compete (Nick Ridicule was in an ambulance after the New Dawn's attack and Chuck Matthews was missing) so the title went to Ryan Apollo.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-undisputed
reigns.label: The Notorious K.I.D

won.source: His own words on the one-year show: 'Last week I not only beat Steven to become the newest Undisputed Champion'; the show's weekly Monday cadence puts last week at 11 January.

reigns.how: Beat Steven Angel for the Undisputed title the week before the one-year show; lost it in the main-event street fight when Jason Hawk pinned him.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-undisputed
reigns.label: Jason Hawk

won.source: The one-year show: 'HERE IS YOUR WINNER...AND NEW UNDISPUTED CHAMPION...JASON HAWK'.

reigns.how: Won the three-way street fight against Steven Angel and the champion The Notorious K.I.D by pinning him after a shooting star swanton.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-undisputed
reigns.label: Steven Angel

won.source: The one-year show's champion K.I.D says he beat Steven Angel to become the newest Undisputed Champion, so Steven Angel held the title before him.

reigns.how: Held the Undisputed Championship before the week of 11 January 2010, when The Notorious K.I.D beat him for it (his own account).

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal
reigns.label: Havoc

won.source: Its champions page: Havoc 'won battle royal' at Legacy on 03/07/09; Legacy 1 (8 March 2009 on its archive list) is not among the recovered pages, but Legacy 2 calls him Universal champion.

reigns.how: Listed as winning a battle royal on Legacy; billed Universal Champion on Legacy 2.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal
reigns.label: Shayne Wolf

won.source: War Games: the Steel Asylum triple threat; the referee awards the belt to Shayne Wolf.

reigns.how: Won the Steel Asylum at War Games, called by Legacy 3 'Universal Champion Shayne Wolf'; lost it to Havoc on Legacy 3.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal
reigns.label: Havoc

won.source: Legacy 3: Havoc tombstones Shayne Wolf and is called 'newly re-attained' Universal Champion.

reigns.how: Regained the title from Shayne Wolf on Legacy 3; lost it to The Mexican Samurai at a house show shortly before Legacy 4.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal
reigns.label: The Mexican Samurai

won.source: Legacy 4 presents The Mexican Samurai as the new Universal Champion after beating Havoc at a house show; its champions page dates his reign 04/19/09.

reigns.how: Won the title from Havoc at a house show; Havoc claimed he was still champion, and the pages then unify the two belts into the Undisputed Universal Championship in The Mexican Samurai's favor; lost it when Tails cashed in the Championship Case at King of the Throne.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal
reigns.label: Tails

won.source: King of the Throne: John Griffyn announces 'the new Undisputed Universal Champion, the Epic Messiah, Tails'.

reigns.how: Unmasked from a Jason mask after Ramirez Silva blew up the cell, cashed in the Championship Case and pinned The Mexican Samurai, Havoc (as Dwayne Hurst) and Johnny Styles in turn with Silva counting; lost the title to Cyber Punk on Direct Hit 12.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal
reigns.label: Cyber Punk

won.source: Direct Hit 12: 'the new Undisputed Universal Champion, Cyber Punk'; Legacy 7 next day calls him Legacy's Undisputed Universal Champion.

reigns.how: Beat Tails with the Cyber Death Driver on Direct Hit 12; lost it to Kaos in a first blood match at Guilty as Charged.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal
reigns.label: Kaos

won.source: Guilty as Charged: 'the new Universal Champion, Kaos'.

reigns.how: Won a first blood match from Cyber Punk with a razor-bladed boot; kept it against Demetrius Randall and Cyber Punk; eliminated by Demetrius Randall on Simple Survival.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal
reigns.label: Frank Hart

won.source: Simple Survival: the draw 'un-unified' the Undisputed Universal Championship and Marissa Johnson names Frank Hart and Demetrius Randall 'both, NEW Universal Heavyweight Champions'; its champions page lists Frank Hart as Direct Hit's Universal champion.

reigns.how: One of the two champions named after the draw in the Universal Championship final at Simple Survival, as Direct Hit's champion.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal-legacy
reigns.label: Demetrius Randall

won.source: Simple Survival: named one of two new Universal Heavyweight Champions; its champions page lists him as Legacy's Universal champion.

reigns.how: One of the two champions named after the draw in the Universal Championship final at Simple Survival, as Legacy's champion.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal-tag-team
reigns.label: DX Affliction

won.source: Direct Hit 6: 'NEW Universal Tag Team Champions, DX Affliction'.

reigns.how: Beat One World Nation with The End Result on Direct Hit 6; Johnny Styles gave up his half to Jake Stunner on Direct Hit 8.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal-tag-team
reigns.label: Joe Santiago and Jake Stunner

won.source: Direct Hit 8: Johnny Styles hands the tag title to Jake Stunner and announces 'Joe Santiago and Jake Stunner' as the new champions; its champions page calls it awarded.

reigns.how: Awarded the titles on Direct Hit 8; lost them in a ladder match on Direct Hit 9.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal-tag-team
reigns.label: Brenton Cyrus and Chuck Matthews

won.source: Direct Hit 9: Salvation pulls both belts down in the ladder match.

reigns.how: Won a ladder match on Direct Hit 9; kept the titles against Tapido Delevega and Dark Tiger (Direct Hit 11) and, in the unification match on Direct Hit 12, absorbed the World Tag Team title as the Undisputed Tag Team Champions; Chuck Matthews traded his belt for the Freedom title after Cyrus was traded.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-universal-tag-team
reigns.label: 25 to Life

won.source: Legacy 11 calls Brenton Cyrus and The Mexican Samurai, 25 to Life, the tag champions; its champions page says The Mexican Samurai replaced Chuck Matthews.

reigns.how: Champions by Legacy 11 after Cyrus's trade to Legacy; the date they took the belts is not on the recovered pages.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-womens-world
reigns.label: Tiffany Starr

won.source: Its champions page: Tiffany Starr beat Prescilla at Legacy 10 on 06/07/09; the Legacy 10 show is not among the recovered pages.

reigns.how: First champion on its champions page; kept it against Emily Brown on Legacy 11 and Simple Survival.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Tails

won.source: Its champions page lists Tails as first World champion, 'awarded title', one day, at Tournament to the Title; on the card itself Ramirez Silva tells the tournament winner Cyber Punk he is only the number one contender, says 'the title holder is this man', and Tails walks out holding the belt.

reigns.how: Named the title holder by Ramirez Silva at the end of Tournament to the Title, walking out with the belt; the champions page gives his reign as one day.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Cyber Punk

won.source: Its champions page lists Cyber Punk as 'Awarded Title' on 02/1/09; the Tournament to the Title page itself ends with Tails holding the belt, and Direct Hit 3 (7 February) bills Cyber Punk as 'your NLWF World Heavyweight Wrestling Champion', so the award fell between the two pages.

reigns.how: Awarded the title after winning the Tournament to the Title (the award itself is not on the recovered pages); kept it against Cipher on Direct Hit 3 (by disqualification) and Havoc at New Era; lost it to Joe Santiago at War Games.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Joe Santiago

won.source: War Games: 'the winner of the match, Joe Santiago' after the I Think He's Dead; its champions page records the change.

reigns.how: Pinned Cyber Punk at War Games; kept the title against Cyber Punk on Direct Hit 8; walked out of King of the Throne instead of defending it.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Brenton Cyrus

won.source: King of the Throne: Brenton Cyrus escapes the cage with the belt; the Direct Hit pages thereafter call him World Heavyweight Champion.

reigns.how: Won the first King of the Throne match; defended against Skye Chamberlain (Direct Hit 11, 2 May), Mexican Samurai (Guilty as Charged), Conor O'Sullivan (Legacy 11) and five challengers in the Steel Asylum at Simple Survival, the last recovered 2009 page. The one-year show of 18 January 2010 bills The Notorious K.I.D as 'Heavyweight and Undisputed Champion', so the reign ended at a date and in a way the recovered pages do not give.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Heart Attacks

won.source: Tournament to the Title: 'the new NLWF Tag Team Champions, The Heart Attacks'.

reigns.how: Beat the Straight Edge Gunners at Tournament to the Title; its champions page lists the titles awarded to Havoc and Death Angel the same day.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Asylum (Havoc and Death Angel)

won.source: Its champions page: Havoc and Death Angel 'awarded titles' on Direct Hit 02/01/09; the Asylum carries the gold on Direct Hit 3 and wins the Direct Hit 4 title match.

reigns.how: Awarded the titles; held them through February; the champions page then lists Havoc with Shadow Demon and the card of Legacy 4 names Havoc and Shayne Wolf as champions.

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Mexican Samurai and Shadow Demon

won.source: Legacy 4: Shadow Demon pins Havoc with the Shadow Crusher; The Mexican Samurai holds the tag belt afterward; its champions page records the change.

reigns.how: Won the titles on Legacy 4; the date the reign ended is not on the recovered pages (the titles are unified on Direct Hit 12).

reigns.title: nlwf-2009-world-tag-team
reigns.label: Havoc and Shayne Wolf

won.source: Legacy 4 (11 April 2009) bills the match as for 'the NLWF World Tag Team Titles' and Havoc and Shayne Wolf are the champions.

reigns.how: Champions by Legacy 4; lost the titles to The Mexican Samurai and Shadow Demon there.

reigns.title: nlwp-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Kid Ego

won.source: Wins a twenty-man Royal Rumble for the newly-vacant title, per the promotion's own pay-per-view broadcast.

reigns.note: The last two entrants, both members of the same faction, are eliminated by each other's own faction ally's interference; the win is credited to Kid Ego by the promotion's own broadcast.

won.source: Won a fourteen-man battle royal, eliminating Eric Righteous last at 38:41, on Tuesday Night's Main Event.
Won the title by beating King Butcher in bulletin #52. The sheet marks the lineage missing after bulletin #57.

won.source: Spring Slams' own inaugural North Eastern title match.

reigns.how: Beats Sandy Fields in the inaugural title match at Spring Slams.

reigns.title: north-eastern-iwc-colbycup-1998

won.source: The fed's own title-history sheet, posted 5 August 1998 (msg_id g0n7TWP2OFQJ), collected but not served per the collection's own credits/roster practice.

reigns.how: Beats Highway Star, per the fed's own title history.
reigns.note: Retains against the Candyman by count-out at Brawl For It All (10 May 1998).

reigns.title: north-eastern-iwc-colbycup-1998
reigns.label: Candyman

won.source: The fed's own title-history sheet, posted 5 August 1998 (msg_id g0n7TWP2OFQJ), collected but not served per the collection's own credits/roster practice.

won.source: The fed's own title-history sheet, posted 5 August 1998 (msg_id g0n7TWP2OFQJ), collected but not served per the collection's own credits/roster practice.

reigns.how: Won a match billed "Ultimate Jeopardy," per the fed's own title history.

reigns.title: north-eastern-iwc-colbycup-1998

won.source: The fed's own title-history sheet, posted 5 August 1998 (msg_id g0n7TWP2OFQJ), collected but not served per the collection's own credits/roster practice.

won.source: Won the title with a tiger suplex, avenging a loss to the same champion two months earlier.
Already billed as champion entering the promotion's own pay-per-view of 26 September 1997; no document in this record states when or how he won it.

lost.source: Lost the title to a tiger suplex in an upset.

reigns.title: now-tag-team
reigns.label: the Decapitators

won.source: Already billed as the promotion's own reigning Tag Team Champions entering the pay-per-view of 26 September 1997; no document in this record states when or how they won it.

reigns.note: Retained the title by countout after a brutal outside brawl involving a chair shot and a concrete powerbomb.

won.source: Won the title with a top-rope Flying Tomahawk leg drop, both men left unconscious.
Already billed as champion, undefeated at 8-0, entering the promotion's own pay-per-view of 26 September 1997; no document in this record states when or how he won it.

lost.source: Lost the title and his own undefeated streak to a top-rope Flying Tomahawk leg drop.

reigns.title: npw-cabin-boy
reigns.label: Mickey D

won.source: No won-date survives; the reign is recorded only in the past tense, years later, by a third party.

reigns.how: Unrecorded. The reign is known only from Tsunami Oni's own recollection of it in a PTC roleplay of 24 April 2005 (/promotions/ptc/rp/cw2-rp-making-bath-time-fun.html), which names the holder and the belt and nothing else.
reigns.note: Filed with an unminted holder: "Mickey D" is a competitor in PTC's own Cruiserweight Tournament 2 and a trainee of Tsunami Oni's in the UWF corpus, but has no registry row yet and his principal promotion is PTC, not NPW — the mint belongs to a PTC-scoped pass, not this one. The past tense ("he WAS Cabin Boy Champion") is the only evidence the reign ended; no losing match, date or successor survives.

reigns.title: npwa-cruiserweight
reigns.label: Atticus "The Jester" Payne

won.source: Billed the undefeated Cruiserweight Champion of the World, criticized on-air for rarely defending the title, Mayhem 18 May 1998 -- no won date survives in the held record.

reigns.how: Standing champion at the start of the record; no won date witnessed.
reigns.note: Listed to defend against "Flyboy" Will Geddings the following week (Mayhem 25 May 1998 card); retained (Shooting Star Press) over Doug Arnott, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special, 13 Oct 1998.

reigns.title: npwa-millennium
reigns.label: "Untouchable" Randy Gant

won.source: Billed the reigning Millennium Champion entering Mayhem, 29 Sep 1998, described as having won the title 'not too long ago' -- title created and first won off-screen, in or after the held record's June-August 1998 gap.

reigns.how: Won off-screen; the title's own first reign.

lost.source: Mayhem, 29 Sep 1998: a Coal Miner's Glove triangle match against "Superstar" Steve Sampson and Rick Kilgore, restarted from a Locutus-Dark Justice bout after all four men brawled; Sampson used a second glove (planted by Locutus) to pin Gant.

reigns.title: npwa-millennium
reigns.label: "Superstar" Steve Sampson

won.source: Mayhem, 29 Sep 1998: won the Coal Miner's Glove triangle match over Randy Gant and Rick Kilgore.

reigns.how: Won from Randy Gant in a Coal Miner's Glove triangle match, Mayhem 29 Sep 1998.
reigns.note: Challenged "Breakfast" Bobby Toast for the World Heavyweight Championship, retaining the Millennium belt by virtue of not defending it (Mayhem, 6 Oct 1998, lost the World Title match by DQ-in-Toast's-favor -- i.e. Sampson won by DQ); retained the Millennium belt against Randy Gant, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special, 13 Oct 1998; scheduled to defend against The Cougar the following week per that show's own announcement.

reigns.title: npwa-north-american
reigns.label: "Sadistic" Steve Stone

won.source: Valentine's Day Massacre '97: won a 15-man King of the Hill gauntlet.

reigns.how: Won a 15-man King of the Hill gauntlet -- the first NPWA North American Champion.
reigns.note: Retained against Mark Bagwell at April Assault (11 Apr 1997).

reigns.title: npwa-north-american
reigns.label: "Breakfast" Bobby Toast

won.source: Thursday Night Thrashings, 5 June 1997, Belfast, Northern Ireland: pinned Sadistic Steve Stone.

reigns.how: Won from Steve Stone.
reigns.note: Retained against the Silent Striker at Armageddon '97 (3 Aug 1997).

reigns.how: Won from Mustafa.

won.source: Not directly witnessed: r006 (Major Victory) carries no lost date in the wing's existing record; Kilgore is billed champion by Mayhem, 29 Sep 1998, the held record's next dated card carrying this title.

reigns.how: Won from Major Victory off-screen, in the held record gap.

reigns.title: npwa-north-american
reigns.label: Mustafa

won.source: NPWA's delayed New Year broadcast, the "January 1st" Show, 4 January 1998.

reigns.how: Won from The Cougar after Arain of the Perfect Role Models, installed as acting replacement referee when senior referee Willie Feldman was knocked out at ringside, ruled the pinfall Mustafa's way; commentary called the decision controversial.

lost.source: NPWA Mayhem, 18 January 1998: lost to Major Victory.

reigns.title: npwa-north-american
reigns.label: Major Victory

won.source: NPWA Mayhem, 18 January 1998: pinned champion Mustafa with the Americannon shoulderblock after Gan Green tripped Mustafa outside the ring.

reigns.how: Won from Mustafa.

reigns.title: npwa-north-american-tag-team
reigns.label: The Cult

reigns.note: Retained (Locutus wrestling in Armageddon's place) over the Larson Brothers, Mayhem 6 Oct 1998.

reigns.title: npwa-north-american-tag-team
reigns.label: Assault and Battery

won.source: Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special, 13 Oct 1998: Tom Harris rolled up Locutus for the pin, winning the belts for himself and Eddie Simpson.

reigns.how: Won from The Cult, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special, 13 Oct 1998.

lost.source: Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998: a masked interloper struck Eddie Simpson with brass knuckles moments before Jack Hammer covered him.

reigns.title: npwa-north-american-tag-team

reigns.how: Won from Assault and Battery at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998, aided by an unidentified masked interloper.
reigns.note: A commentator remarks the Masters are the first NPWA team to hold both the World and North American Tag Team belts.

won.source: Xmas Gory '96: defeated Col. Buddy Lee Jarrett.

reigns.note: First OSW Heavyweight Champion. The roster bio card gave the month only ("March 2002"); the fed's own title history and write-up of Crowning Glory date it to 10 March 2002. Defences on record. Slam!, 23 March 2002: with Drew Hostyle and Frankie Bones against Timo Bolamba and Aimz, the champion's side lost by disqualification and he stayed champion. Slam!, 30 March 2002: a handicap match against two men billed as Timo Bolamba and Aimz, announced as a successful title defence. Slam!, 6 April 2002: against Tempest, who won by disqualification, so the title did not change. Head on Collision, 28 April 2002: beat Ivan Stanislav and was announced as still champion.

reigns.title: osw-united-states
reigns.label: Tyler Nelson

won.source: The fed's own title history, wrestling site capture of 21 July 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html): "March 16, 2003, Crowning Glory 2 PPV, Tyler Nelson d. Kid Wonder (c) for Soy Boy Memorial Title."

reigns.how: Won the Soy Boy Memorial Title from Kid Wonder at Crowning Glory 2 and renamed it the United States Title on Sunday Night Slam, 23 March 2003. On the 30 March 2003 Slam (osw-slam-2003-03-30) he is billed "the United States Champion" and keeps it over Scott Taylor, by cheating. Vacated it on order of Jane Reagan on 4 May 2003, a week after winning the World Heavyweight Title from Ivan Stanislav.
reigns.note: Neither Crowning Glory 2 nor the 4 May 2003 Slam is served; the dates are the title history's. The 30 March card's own commentary says he "just won the damn title" and shows his "newly fashioned United States title".

reigns.title: osw-united-states
reigns.label: Politically Incorrect

won.source: The fed's own title history, wrestling site capture of 21 July 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html): "May 25, 2003, Sunday Night Slam, Politically Incorrect (William S. Powell and Reginald V. Lovecraft) win the Chaos In The Cage Match and are declared co-holders of the United States Champiobship."

reigns.how: Declared co-holders after the Chaos In The Cage match: Powell and Lovecraft, who interfered in the match, made a simultaneous pin on D-Kay Calyx, and because the only rule was that the first pin or submission won, both were named co-titleholders. The fed's lawyers found no proof the match contract was violated (U.S. Title Follow-up, 27 May 2003), so the pair were allowed to defend the belt as a tag team. On 28 May 2003 they handed the belt to OSW officials, refusing to carry a title with the American flag on it, said two new belts were being made, and promised to reveal them on Slam at a first defence against Asa Fountain; no served card shows that defence. Lost it to Azala Zameer at Ascension (osw-ascension-2003-06-29), where they are billed "the OSW American Champions".
reigns.note: The 25 May 2003 Slam is not served; the date is the title history's, which the 19 May news post ("Chaos In The Cage to determine the new United States Champion") and the 27 May post ("over the past 36 hours") fit. Lovecraft's card of 24 May 2003 still reads "None in OSW" for titles; the team card of 20 June 2003 reads "OSW United States Champions".

reigns.how: Won the Contract versus Contract match for the OSW American Championship at Ascension: he drove Lovecraft into the corner with the Spear of Zameer, then pinned Powell after the Ivory Stampede; his own OSW contract was on the line against Lt. Mandela's. His roster card of 8 September 2003 lists "OSE American Championship" under Title History.
reigns.note: The end of the reign rests on Ivan Stanislav's card alone: no served show or news post carries the change on 24 August 2003 (the 21 August Overtime card does not mention the belt).

The show's own page announces it in advance — "XAVIER KANNON WILL DEFEND HIS CONTINENTAL TITLE AGAINST A…SCARY…MYSTERY OPPONENT?" — and bills him "the Commissioner of PCW and the PCW Continental champion......GOLD PATRON MERITORIOUS XAVIER KANNON!". NO I WAS NOT!" while the same show books "a Triple Threat Match to determine the Number One Contender to the PCW Continental Championship" and calls him "the last Continental Champion"; Turmoil 85 of 3 Jul (results/503.txt) has him say "MY Continental Title.... WHICH I HAVE NOT BEEN PINNED FOR goes to Legend Inc." The immediately preceding log row, Turmoil 80 of 21 May 2002, is a REPLAYED TAPE, not a title change: its own text opens "Sunday Sabotage:September 2, 2001- Boda vs The Chef vs Howard Porter" and the show frames it as a retrospective ("we're gonna show Boda's greatest moment in The Red Army. reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — Fusion 82, 9 Jul 2002 — the Fusion strand bills The End the standing PCW Cruiserweight Champion and has him defend and retain against Brandi ("The End vs Brandi for the PCW Cruiserweight Championship"; he "walks out with the Cruiserweight strap around his waist"; "The blind jobber retains his cruiserweight title for another night", PCW's own results page for Fusion 82, 9 Jul 2002), four days after Fusion 81 gave him only the number one contendership. Turmoil 85 of 3 Jul 2002 and Fusion 83 of 19 Jul 2002 both bill Charlie Loc the champion, and Fusion 83 is where the belt actually changes. No match on either strand returns it. Both show records stand; the reigns here follow the strand the belt's own recorded changes run through. Fusion 81 and Fusion 82 are the same pair of shows the Extreme and Tag Team passes found billing standing champions against the rest of the fed's record. Gold and Glory 2002, 30 Jun 2002 — the page's own contradiction, read end to end, is a REPLAYED CLIP and not a second reading. The show carries a "Cruiserweight Championship history video package" immediately before the match; inside that package is the finish of Turmoil 81 of 28 May 2002 — "Winner and new PCW Cruiserweight Champion: Juan Borro / Dave: I can't believe it! Juan Borro has captured the PCW Cruiserweight title once again!" — followed by weeks of build narrated in the past tense ("A week later...", "Just last Tuesday...", "That Friday..."). The night's own match follows it: "The following match is scheduled for one fall and is 3 way TLC show down for the PCW CRUISERWEIGHT TITLE", with Borro billed "the Current PCW CRUISERWEIGHT CHAMPION" going in, and it ends on Charlie Loc — "HE'S DONE IT~! WE HAVE A NEW CRUISER WEIGHT CHAMPION~!" and "CHARLIE IS FINALLY THE PCW CRUISER WEIGHT CHAMPION!" (PCW's own results page for Gold and Glory 2002, 30 Jun 2002). The fed's own title log is right, Turmoil 85 of 3 Jul corroborates it, and the contradicting line is the previous title change replayed. No conflict is filed (the replay-document model, CURATION v66). Fusion 81, 5 Jul 2002 — a NUMBER ONE CONTENDERSHIP match, not a title match. The show announces it twice in its own voice: "the next match is scheduled for one fall and is for the Number One Contendership to the Cruiserweight Title!" (PCW's own results page for Fusion 81, 5 Jul 2002, which also carries the whole match twice, the duplication its sibling pages carry). The fed's own log files it as a change from Charlie Loc to The End; Charlie Loc is billed "the PCW Cruiser Weight Champion" two days earlier on PCW's own results page for Turmoil 85, 3 Jul 2002 and again a fortnight later on PCW's own results page for Fusion 83, 19 Jul 2002, where he loses the belt for real. The stored champion-after is corrected. Turmoil 86, 9 Jul 2002 — another promotion's belt, filed under PCW's Cruiserweight Championship in the fed's own title log: the match's own text crowns "NEW PURE JUNIOR HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION, THE END!!" No correction row is filed, the standing shape for a row wanting a belt PCW's own title list does not hold (the RUSH Network Championship rows are the precedent).

The fed's own title log records no change, and Miss Moonlight is billed "the current Cruiserweight Champion" on the next show a week later (PCW's own results page for Fusion 121, 9 May 2003, where she retains) and every show after it. Aymin is billed champion nowhere. His reign is retired and hers runs unbroken. Turmoil 130, 19 Jun 2003 — SOCIETY never won the Cruiserweight Championship, he STOLE it. He walks out "wearing the PCW Cruiserweight Title around his neck", says "Many of you are wondering why I took this piece of property away from Miss Moonlight", and declares: "since I now own this belt, I HEREBY DECLARE MYSELF THE PCW CRUISERWEIGHT CHAMPION!!" The broadcast never accepts it — "He's destroyed TWO PCW officials, and stolen the PCW Cruiserweight Title!" — and calls Miss Moonlight the Cruiserweight Champion inside the same match (PCW's own results page for Turmoil 130, 19 Jun 2003). The finish is a disqualification besides. The card's "(c)" sits on Tessa Windsor-Green, PCW's Television Champion, who held this belt at no point. Turmoil 131, 25 Jun 2003 — the fed settles it in its own voice with Miss Moonlight refereeing SOCIETY's self-declared defence: "Jeff:...the PCW Cruiserweight Title's on the line, so let's get this match started! / Dave:...You know that Miss Moonlight's the champion." She demands the belt from SOCIETY and "begrudgingly, SOCIETY hands it over", raises it to the crowd and gives it to the timekeeper; the match is then thrown out ("THE RESULT OF THIS MATCH, WHEN MISS MOONLIGHT WAKES UP, IS A NO CONTEST!") (PCW's own results page for Turmoil 131, 25 Jun 2003). No reign is filed for SOCIETY. PCW closed for roughly six months between Turmoil 131 of 25 Jun 2003 and Turmoil 132 of 21 Dec 2003, and THIS BELT CROSSED THE GAP ON ITS CHAMPION. Turmoil 137 of 7 Feb 2004 stages her return with the belt still on her: "the PCW CRUISERWEIGHT TITLE AROUND HER WAIST!!" and "Dave: It's MISS MOONLIGHT!! THE LAST PCW CRUISERWEIGHT CHAMPION BEFORE THE COMPANY CLOSED!!", the same page billing her "the PCW Cruiserweight champion, Naomi Kawaii" and titling the segment "The Mega Soaring Arrows reveal Naomi Kawaii as the former PCW Cruiserweight Champion Miss Moonlight" (PCW's own results page for Turmoil 137, 7 Feb 2004). Turmoil 138 of 14 Feb 2004 says it again — the Cruiserweight title's own name plate reads MISS MOONLIGHT beside "the woman formerly known as Miss Moonlight", and the backstage interview corrects itself from "the reigning PCW Cruiserweight champion, Miss Moonlight—" to "reigning PCW Cruiserweight champion, NAOMI KAWAII" (PCW's own results page for Turmoil 138, 14 Feb 2004); she retains on that show, the belt's last surviving defence. The reign is one run under two billed names (Miss Moonlight, then Naomi Kawaii, per the fed's own roster); the holder is carried under the billing the reign began with.

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — Turmoil 43, 14 Aug 2001 — five days after Dawning 2001 declared the belt vacant, the Turmoil strand still bills Nikita Morozov the champion and has him retain: "WINNER and still PCW Rising Star Champion: Nikita Morozov" (PCW's own results page for Turmoil 43, 14 Aug 2001). Turmoil 44 of 22 Aug 2001 then agrees with Dawning and runs a tournament for the vacated belt. Both show records stand; the reigns here follow Dawning 2001 and Turmoil 44, which agree with each other and with the fed's own next crowning. Fusion 43, 20 Jul 2001 — the show's own text crowns Nikita Morozov ("Winner and NEW Rising Star Champion"), and Snow is called "the former Rising Star champ" later on the same page. The card bills Morozov "(c)" and the fed's own log stores him as champion on both sides; the page's own crowning governs. No correction is filed on the stored champion-before: the fed's record carries no Rising Star row between Turmoil 37 of 12 Jun 2001 and this match, so who held the belt going in is not established beyond Snow's own last billing. Sabotage 13, 22 Jul 2001 — a NUMBER ONE CONTENDER'S cage match, not a title match, and the champion was not in it. The show says so in its own voice — "BJ Mac could become the number one contender for the Rising Star Title right here!" (PCW's own results page for Sabotage 13, 22 Jul 2001) — Clay announces only "here is your winner…BJ Mac!", and PCW's own results page for Dawning 2001, 9 Aug 2001 then says "BJ Mac has the right to challenge for the Rising Star Title" and introduces "the PCW Rising Star Champion......NIKITA MOROZOV". BJ Mac never held the belt, and Nikita Morozov's reign runs unbroken through this match. Dawning 2001, 9 Aug 2001 — Nikita Morozov defended the belt against BJ Mac and kept it ("WINNER: Nikita Morozov, TIME: 9:28"), and the fed took it off him in the same breath: "Unfortunately for Morozov, this defense is said to be his last. Due to a rule violation, Morozov is no longer allowed to hold the Rising Star Title and it is now vacant" (PCW's own results page for Dawning 2001, 9 Aug 2001). PCW's own results page for Turmoil 44, 22 Aug 2001 confirms it from the other side — a tournament "for the vacated PCW Rising Star Title", with Morozov called "the now former Rising Star champion" who "retained the Rising Star title until he was forced to relinquish it".

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — Sabotage 28, 9 Dec 2001 — the Sabotage strand bills Gaijin the standing Rising Star Champion and crowns Orpheus Grant over him ("the Rising Star champion" inside the match; "Winner: Orpheus Grant"), two days after Fusion 62 of 7 Dec 2001 ended "Winner and NEW Rising Star Champion: El Diablo" and two days before Turmoil 60 bills "El Diablo (c)". No match on either strand returns the belt. The reigns here follow the Fusion/Turmoil strand. The same Sabotage 28 page also bills a third man, "the current PCW Rising Star Champion, “Big” Bubba McCoy … proudly clutching his belt". Sabotage 28, 9 Dec 2001 — Orpheus Grant won the match but the belt did not move on the Fusion/Turmoil strand; El Diablo is billed champion on Turmoil 60 two days later and retains on Sabotage 29 a fortnight after that. Turmoil 60, 11 Dec 2001 — a disqualification, and the champion kept the belt: the card reads "El Diablo (c) vs Big Bubba McCoy vs Gaijin" and the match ends "Winner via DQ: Gaijin" after El Diablo knocked Gaijin out with the ring bell ("What a load of bunk using a weapon to keep his title"). The fed's own log agrees — El Diablo before and after — and Sabotage 29 of 23 Dec 2001 ends "Winner and STILL PCW Rising Star Champion: El Diablo", with Sabotage 30 of 30 Dec and Sabotage 31 of 6 Jan 2002 billing him champion too. Turmoil 64, 8 Jan 2002 — a NUMBER ONE CONTENDER'S match, not a title match. The show announces it in its own voice: "This over the top rop battle royal will determine the # 1 contender for the Rising Star title", and the same show has El Diablo walk backstage "the Rising Star title around his waist". Hessian never held the belt; the stored champion-after is corrected. El Diablo held the belt through Sabotage 31 of 6 Jan 2002 (a four-way the referee ruled a non contest) and is shown with it backstage on Turmoil 64 of 8 Jan; the reign ends on the first of Shanghaied 2002's two Rising Star matches.

reigns.note: Turmoil 80 of 21 May 2002 is a RETROSPECTIVE, and the World Championship battle royal filed on it is a replayed tape. The show is titled "Boda's PCW legacy in memoriam", runs a career retrospective in clips throughout, and frames this one in its own voice — "When we come back, Boda's first World title victory at March Madness", "Let's go to the tape" — with the tape's own slate reading "PCW March Madness:March 3, 2002- Battle Royal for the PCW World Heavyweight Title" (PCW's own results page for Turmoil 80, 21 May 2002). The genuine title change is March Madness 2002 — Boda's 4–6 Mar 2002 reign, which the retrospective itself corroborates ("that is when Boda captured the Heavyweight title"). Row 904 is dropped from the chain (the replay-document model, CURATION v66; the row-873 / row-872 / row-903 precedent) with no correction row: the stored champions are correct for the match that actually happened, eleven weeks earlier. The next night's Supremacy 2002 card bills "Jason Snow (c)" and crowns Big Alan Steele over him. The tape's own slate dates March Madness 2002 to 3 March where his booking dates it to 4 March; the booking date governs. Turmoil 80's Continental half is likewise a replayed Sabotage 17 tape of Sep 2001.

reigns.note: Shanghaied IV, 23 Feb 2004 — the belt's last recorded night, and three things happen to it. Cal Roberts VACATES it himself in an in-ring promo ("So as of right now I officially vacate my World Championship title!"); the fed's own executives overrule him on the same page ("Hey Buzz you can't just give up a title you moron, it takes lots of paper work. You're still the champion and your match with Blitz is for the title"); and Inphino Blitz then beats him for it — "And the winner... and NEW PCW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION... THE BLACK DRAGON MASTER... INPHINOOOOOO BLITZ!!!" Minutes later Dick James and Alan Zoober take it off him in the aisle: "you, Inphino Blitz, just MIGHT get into the records books as the SHORTEST REIGNING PCW WORLD CHAMPION EVER!! Cause of right now, YOU'RE STRIPPED!!!", adding "no matter the winner... the belt was getting vacated IMMEDIATELY AFTER" (PCW's own results page for Shanghaied IV, 23 Feb 2004). The fed uses both its words in one segment — STRIPPED for the act and vacated for the result — and the reign's end is filed under the word for the act. Blitz then lays the belt down himself rather than fight for it. His reign is the shortest of the belt's recorded reigns. The fed's own title log records the outcome of the match as undetermined (its own champion-after value left blank); corrected below.

reigns.title: ptc-tag-team-tournament
reigns.label: Shane Stone & The Bum Boozler

won.source: User-attested: a contributor's own account of having wrestled and won it, corroborated on the alliance's own re-hosted forum — the champions' own tag-title defence of 28 September 2003 (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/tag-titles-match/266/1), a beaten opponent's own recollection of losing to them twice in it (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/next-tag-match/427/25), the same thread's own reply from one of the winners (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/next-tag-match/427/28), and a third poster's “I still owe you twice for the tag team tournament in the old PTC” (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/next-tag-match/427/23).

reigns.how: Won as the pairing the alliance billed “Homophobic” — one half of The Phenomenons with a partner from outside that team, never The Phenomenons themselves. The final is undated in what survives; the earliest surviving word of the win is the pair's own defence of the PTC World Tag Team Championship on 28 September 2003, where the ring announcer introduces “the current PTC World Tag Team Champions Homophobic”. A beaten opponent's own handler recounts the tournament in the alliance's own forum — “I was in the PTC TTT tournament with my friend Zero as Banned and Exiled. We lost to you… Later I teamed with Sin as a replacement for his partner and faced you in the next round of the tournament… So I lost to you twice in one tournament from two partner no shows” — and one of the winners answers him in the same thread: “we beat YOU twice… accept it.”

conflict.reading_a: The pairing billed “Homophobic” — Shane Stone and The Bum Boozler — won it: a contributor's own attested account, the pair billed as the alliance's reigning World Tag Team Champions on 28 September 2003, and a beaten opponent and a third poster both crediting that team with beating them twice in the one tournament.
conflict.reading_b: PTCpedia's own “Banned & Exiled~!” article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-banned-exiled.html) instead names the winners as The Phenomenons, and calls the event “the first and only Primetime Central Tag Team tournament”. The same article's account of the losing side is contradicted in detail by that side's own handler, who names a different first partner and a different sequence, and the alliance's own board carries a later tag-team tournament final of April 2004, so “first and only” is not supported either. Recorded as that article's own claim, not settled.

won.source: PURE's own Ikusa II script, Matsumoto Stadium, Nagano, 28 April 2002: "we have an exciting card including the crowning of the first ever PURE Champion, that being the Junior Heavyweight category with The End facing the HIT facing Kensuke Suzahara", ending with owner Alexander Miyagawa presenting the belt — "The first ever PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion... THE END!!!!!"

lost.source: PURE's own Ikusa V script, Sapporo Dome, Sapporo, 16 June 2002 — the champion's title on the line in a tag match, the commentary stating the stipulation ("We shouldn't forget that his Jr Heavyweight title is on the line in this match!" / "Right! Whoever pins him wins the belt!!"), Charlie Loc and The H.I.T. finishing The End with the double powerbomb into a blue thunder facecrusher the commentary calls the Double Neurotica, The H.I.T. covering for the three, and ring announcer Hanza Kibagame with the belt in hand: "Winner…and NEW PURE JUNIOR HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION…THE HARDCORE ISOSCELES TRAPEZOID!!!"

reigns.how: Beat The H.I.T. and Kensuke Suzahara in a three-way, making The H.I.T. tap to Never Again, to become PURE's first ever champion.
reigns.note: PURE's own roster card for The End calls him "First ever PURE titleholder" and "First ever two-time PURE titleholder"; the second reign is a row of its own. The belt left him at Ikusa V on 16 June 2002, in a tag match his own title was put on, and he gave his own account of it backstage the same night — "I am baffled myself on the loss…but more baffled on how I lost the belt." The fed's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history carries the same change at its entry #2 and the same crowning at its entry #1, where it has him beat "The HIT and Kensuke Suzahara in a triple threat match to win the belt at Ikusa II" and then dates the reign "(4/14/02 - 4/28/02)" — a span that runs against its own sentence, since Ikusa II is the show of 28 April 2002 and 14 April 2002 is Ikusa. Both stand.

reigns.title: pure-jr-heavyweight
reigns.label: The HIT

won.source: PURE's own Ikusa V script, Sapporo Dome, Sapporo, 16 June 2002 — the champion's title on the line in a tag match, the commentary stating the stipulation ("We shouldn't forget that his Jr Heavyweight title is on the line in this match!" / "Right! Whoever pins him wins the belt!!"), Charlie Loc and The H.I.T. finishing The End with the double powerbomb into a blue thunder facecrusher the commentary calls the Double Neurotica, The H.I.T. covering for the three, and ring announcer Hanza Kibagame with the belt in hand: "Winner…and NEW PURE JUNIOR HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION…THE HARDCORE ISOSCELES TRAPEZOID!!!" PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) numbers him its second champion, entry #2: "Pinned The End during a six man tag team match to win the title at Ikusa III". The bout the script carries is a six-man tag, and it is Ikusa V's; the fed's own two records name two different shows for the one change, and both stand.

lost.source: The record does not date the end of this reign. PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) gives the night and the manner at entry #3, where The End takes the belt back: "Pinned Inphino Blitz in a fatal four way match on Ikusa 6." No surviving PURE record holds or dates a show of that name. The change falls between 16 June 2002 and 28 July 2002, the night PCW's own Wrestle Vessel 2002 bills The End as the defending PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion.

reigns.how: Pinned The End after the Double Neurotica, in a tag match the fed put the champion's own title on — whoever pinned The End won the belt.
reigns.note: The fed's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history numbers him its second champion and names the win, in a six man tag team match, at a show it calls Ikusa III; the script that carries that bout is Ikusa V's, of 16 June 2002, and both stand. The fed's own earlier paperwork bills The End because The End was champion when it was written — the division rankings of 2 May 2002 and the Ikusa IV card of 4 June 2002 both predate the change — and its own champions page carries only the holder of the moment, in states that begin in January 2003. His own PURE roster card is the one document that reads against the reign: its title-history field gives "None as of yet" and its award field is blank. The show's own script and its own ring announcer carry the change, and The End gave his own account of it backstage the same night — "I am baffled myself on the loss…but more baffled on how I lost the belt." All of it stands as written. The reign ended when The End took the belt back in a fatal four-way, on a show the fed's own history calls Ikusa 6 and no surviving record dates.

reigns.title: pure-jr-heavyweight
reigns.label: Charlie Loc

won.source: PURE's own roster card for Charlie Loc bills him holder of the "PURE Jnr. Heavy Weight Title (Current)" and credits him as "First Man To Win a PURE Title Outside Of a PURE Ring"; the fed's own Axcess commentary says the same of him from the other side ("He won the Junior Heavyweight Title without even being on a PURE broadcast!"). The ring was PCW's. PCW's own Wrestle Vessel 2002 script, 28 July 2002 — a two-fall match for both the PURE Junior Heavyweight Championship and the PCW Cruiserweight Title, The End defending both against Charlie Loc and Alexander Miyagawa under his own stipulation that "The PURE Junior Heavyweight Championship shall be determined by pinfall or submission, while the PCW Cruiserweight Championship will be decided by climbing the ladder". Charlie Loc takes the first fall — "MIYA'S HEAD HITS THE CHAIR, AND LOC HOLDS FOR THE PIN! 1! 2! 3!", called on air as "Charlie Loc has managed to win the PURE Junior Heavyweight Title" — and leaves with the belt: "Loc seems happy with his Junior Heavyweight Title as he holds it aloft as he departs the ring." PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) dates the same change at entry #4: "Pinned The End at PCW Wrestle Vessel in the first fall of a double Crusierweight title match to become PURE Juniorheavyweight champion. (7/28/2002 - 10/13/2002)"

lost.source: PURE's own PURE v2.0 Ikusa 4 script, Ikusa Hall — "Jung Loc, going head to head with a bright young upstart in PURE, DJ Nygma, with Loc's PURE Jr. Heavyweight Title on the line", ending on a three count and the belt handed to the challenger; the fed's own Axcess replays the same match later. PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History") dates the reign "(7/28/2002 - 10/13/2002)" and the change itself: "#5 - El Romantico — Pinned Jung Loc on Ikusa 4 under the guise of DJ Nygma to become the new PURE Juniorheavyweight champion (10/13/2002)". The fed's own news of 2 October 2002 still bills Ikusa 4 as ahead and its news of 4 October 2002 reports it "ready to go"; the show's own commentary places it after PCW's Red October of 6 October 2002.

reigns.how: Took the first fall of a two-fall match in PCW's ring, one that carried the PURE Junior Heavyweight and PCW Cruiserweight titles at once; lost the belt to a masked DJ Nygma on PURE v2.0 Ikusa 4.
reigns.note: PURE's own commentary names him "Jung 'Charlie' Loc" and bills him "Jung Loc" on air, the same man the fed's own roster card bills Charlie Loc. He arrives on PURE v2.0 Ikusa 1 in August 2002 billed "PURE's current Jr.Heavyweight champion", the belt over his shoulder; the commentary on v2.0 Ikusa 2 calls him "the former PURE Jr Heavyweight champion" while the shows either side of it bill him as the holder, and both readings stand. The two federations' own records of the win disagree on whom he pinned for the belt and both stand: PURE's own title history has him pin The End, and PCW's own script for the match has him pin Alexander Miyagawa while The End, defending both belts, was still in it. The win was taken in another federation's ring, and links that federation's own show.

reigns.title: pure-jr-heavyweight
reigns.label: DJ Nygma

won.source: PURE's own PURE v2.0 Ikusa 4 script, Ikusa Hall — the challenger comes out of a Jr. Heavyweight battle royal earlier the same night, takes the belt on a three count, and the mask comes off: "DJ Nygma has just been revealed as none other than EL ROMANTICO!" The fed's own Axcess replays the match as "DJ Nygma vs. Jung Loc (c) - PURE JR.Weight Title Defense". PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History") dates it: "#5 - El Romantico — Pinned Jung Loc on Ikusa 4 under the guise of DJ Nygma to become the new PURE Juniorheavyweight champion (10/13/2002)", the same day it closes Charlie Loc's own reign. The fed's own news of 2 October 2002 still bills Ikusa 4 as ahead and its news of 4 October 2002 reports it "ready to go"; the show's own commentary places it after PCW's Red October of 6 October 2002.

lost.source: PURE's own Axcess: Jamar Wilson, holding the belt, says "the current PURE JR.Hevyweight champion is under PCW contract RIGHT NOW, in which I refer to El Romantico. That will be remedied when we crown a new champion here in PURE." The fed's own news row of 19 January 2003 then reports that "the PURE Jr.Weight title mini-tounry matches took place".

reigns.how: Won masked, as DJ Nygma, and unmasked in the ring the same night; the belt was decided again by tournament when PURE re-opened and its holder was under contract elsewhere.
reigns.note: PURE's own news row of 7 January 2003 calls him "the former PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion", quoting him by the El Romantico name. His own roster card's title-history line reads "none" in every layer of the deposit, against the fed's own champions page, which carries "Champion: El Romantico" in its January 2003 state, and against the Axcess script — recorded as a disagreement, not resolved. The reign is filed under the identity the unmasking revealed, with the masked billing on the label.

reigns.title: pure-jr-heavyweight
reigns.label: Radiant

won.source: Radiant's own PURE roster card carries the reign as a dated defence ledger: "First reign as PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion - 1/26/03 to 00/00/00" and "1. (1/26/03 @ Hakatanomori Football Stadium) Radiant beat Isao Asai (30:15) by pinfall (Belt won)." PURE's own news row of 26 January 2003 reports the same night: "titles were decided", "a 5-star JR.Weight title match". PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) closes on him, entry #6: "Became champion upon restart of PURE in January 2003."

reigns.how: Beat Isao Asai in 30:15 by pinfall at Hakatanomori Football Stadium, in the tournament PURE ran for the belt when it re-opened.
reigns.note: No script for the 26 January 2003 show survives in the record, so this reign's own winning event carries its date from the fed's own roster card and links no page. Three defences follow, on Radiant's own card and on the shows themselves: Isao Asai at Tosu Stadium on 9 February 2003 (13:55, a Moonsault), Isao Asai at the Tokyo Dome on 2 March 2003 (11:42, a Shining Wizard), and El Mesias at Budokan Hall on 9 March 2003. The fed's two records of that last one disagree and both are kept: the card reads "(15:00) when the Time Limit experied", the show's own script has the referee stop it "due to a DOUBLE COUNT OUT! Therefore, this match is a draw!" with Radiant still champion.

reigns.label: The End

won.source: PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders), entry #3: "Pinned Inphino Blitz in a fatal four way match on Ikusa 6." No surviving PURE record holds or dates a show of that name. PURE's own roster card for The End bills him "Two-Time PURE Junior Heavyweight Champion" and "First ever two-time PURE titleholder", and he says it in his own words on PCW's own broadcast of 28 July 2002: "The PURE Junior Heavyeweight Title was the first title awarded and I won it twice!"

lost.source: PCW's own Wrestle Vessel 2002 script, 28 July 2002 — a two-fall match for both the PURE Junior Heavyweight Championship and the PCW Cruiserweight Title, The End defending both against Charlie Loc and Alexander Miyagawa under his own stipulation that "The PURE Junior Heavyweight Championship shall be determined by pinfall or submission, while the PCW Cruiserweight Championship will be decided by climbing the ladder". Charlie Loc takes the first fall — "MIYA'S HEAD HITS THE CHAIR, AND LOC HOLDS FOR THE PIN! 1! 2! 3!", called on air as "Charlie Loc has managed to win the PURE Junior Heavyweight Title" — and leaves with the belt: "Loc seems happy with his Junior Heavyweight Title as he holds it aloft as he departs the ring." PURE's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history (newsdata board 57, row 0, subject "Complete History", the document the fed's own staff page renders) dates the same change at entry #4: "Pinned The End at PCW Wrestle Vessel in the first fall of a double Crusierweight title match to become PURE Juniorheavyweight champion. (7/28/2002 - 10/13/2002)"

reigns.how: Won it back in a fatal four-way, pinning Inphino Blitz on the show the fed's own title history calls Ikusa 6; lost it in PCW's ring at Wrestle Vessel 2002.
reigns.note: The second reign PURE's own roster card claims for him, placed by the fed's own complete Junior Heavyweight Championship history, which runs it as entry #3 between The H.I.T.'s reign and Charlie Loc's, and closed by PCW's own Wrestle Vessel 2002, where he defends the belt as champion and loses it. The night it began is named and so is the manner; the date is not recovered and is not guessed, and the record puts it between 16 June and 28 July 2002. No surviving record holds or dates a PURE show called Ikusa 6.

reigns.title: pure-tag-team
reigns.label: Inphino Blitz and Mang-A-Hero

won.source: PURE's own Ikusa V script, Sapporo Dome, 16 June 2002: "our boss, Alexander Miyagawa and Ebola III will be joining forces against the team of Inphino Blitz and Mang-a-Hero in a bout for the first awarding of the PURE Tag Team Titles", ending "Our winners and new PURE Tag Team Champions....INPHINO BLITZ AND MANG-A-HERO!"

end.source: PURE's own title-history page (newsdata board 78): "#2 - Titles retired. Retired belts upon the reopening of PURE." The fed's own show commentary says the same from the other side on the Tosu Stadium script: "We were the FIRST AND LAST PURE TAG TEAM CHAMPIONS!" / "That's only because Mina retired that spot for the Trinity!"

reigns.how: Beat Ebola III and Alexander Miyagawa, Mang-A-Hero pinning Miyagawa after the Dragon Drive Z, in the match booked for the first awarding of the belts.
reigns.note: The only reign the belts ever carried. The fed's own title-history page numbers it #1 and its own announcer calls the pair "new PURE Tag Team Champions", which reads as a title change but is not one: the match was billed on air as "a bout for the first awarding of the PURE Tag Team Titles" and "will determine the first PURE Tag Team Champions", so Ebola III and Alexander Miyagawa were challengers for a vacant belt, not holders of it.

reigns.title: pure-trinity-tag-team
reigns.label: Shaun Styles and the Sushi Crew

won.source: PURE's own title-history page (newsdata board 78): "#3 - Trinity Tag Team Championship declared. Sushi Crew / Shaun Styles become new champions over Black Dragons." The fed's own PURE World video package shows the same moment — "A picture of Shaun Styles beating the Black Dragons appears as he picks up one of the Trinity Tag Team Championships and holds it high." The belts were instated on Axcess and the pair are already billed champions in the Tosu Stadium script.

lost.source: PURE's own Budokan Ikusa script, 9 March 2003: "Well, we have new Trinty Champions, in the form of the Suburban Ninja Clan!"

reigns.how: Beat the Black Dragons for the belts PURE declared on its re-opening.
reigns.note: No script survives for the night this reign began: the fed's own title-history page, its own video package and its own later scripts all carry the win, and nothing else does, so the winning event carries a month and links no page. The pair were billed as a team of three throughout — Ryu Sotosucki and Otoshi Mishimoto of the Sushi Crew with Shaun Styles as their third, in the Sushi Crew's own words "albeit with Shaun Styles as our partner".

reigns.title: pure-trinity-tag-team
reigns.label: Suburban Ninja Clan

won.source: PURE's own Budokan Ikusa script, 9 March 2003 — Ninjas 20, 22 and 23 against "the PURE Trinity Tag Team Champions, they are Shaun Styles and the SUSHI Crew", ending on a choke hold and "we have new Trinty Champions, in the form of the Suburban Ninja Clan!" The fed's own champions page carries "Champions: Suburban Ninja Clan" in its last state.

reigns.how: Ninjas 20, 22 and 23 beat Shaun Styles and the Sushi Crew, Ninja 20 finishing Styles with a choke hold.
reigns.note: Eight days later the Clan issued an open challenge through PURE's own press office to any three-man team in the federations PURE shared a host with, offering to defend the belts on those feds' own shows: "The Clan will send ninjas to its challengers' shows and defend its Trinity Tag Team belts there." The surviving record carries no such defence.

reigns.title: pure-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jesse Ramey

won.source: PURE's own Final Destinies script, Tokyo Dome, 2 March 2003 — the tournament final, with the belt presented to Ramey on his knees; his own roster card reads "First Ever PURE World Heavyweight Title (March 2nd, 2003-????)", and the fed's own champions page carries "Champion: Jesse Ramey" in its last state.

reigns.how: Won the four-man tournament PURE ran to crown its first World Heavyweight Champion, beating Eddie Mandrake in the final by pinfall.
reigns.note: The belt was announced in 2002 and stood vacant until this night: PURE's own news row of 18 February 2003 has the fed's vice president say "all the titles will be on this line, including the vacant PURE Heavyweight Championship". Defended at Budokan Hall on 9 March 2003 against Jason Marah, and the surviving record carries no later change. The fed billed the belt as both the PURE World Heavyweight Title (its champions page, its own title-history page, Ramey's roster card) and the PURE Heavyweight Championship (the Final Destinies and Budokan scripts) in the same weeks.

reigns.title: pwc-wrestleonline-2003-tag-team
reigns.label: Penance

won.source: The fed's write-up of PWC TV of 8 February 2003.

lost.source: The fed's write-up of PWC TV of 5 April 2003; the fed's own title history lists the change.

reigns.note: Penance became the first PWC Tag Team Champion, gorilla-pressing Porky Bunson over the top rope for the final elimination in a battle royal after flooring him with a jumping sit-down piledriver. His partner refused the second belt, leaving Penance the sole champion. Defences on record. PWC TV, 15 February 2003: Penance retained the PWC Tag Team Championship in his first defence, pinning delivery boy Sammy Bello after dropping him with a tombstone piledriver onto his own tag partner, Chuck D'Andrea. PWC TV, 22 February 2003: Penance retained the PWC Tag Team Championship, pinning both members of 2GVC at once, dropping Chandler Tsonda with a sit-out piledriver onto the already-piledriven Jimmy Nguyen. PWC TV, 15 March 2003: Penance retained the PWC Tag Team Championship, chokeslamming Jim Axtell onto a folded steel chair for the pin after escaping Axtell's Axe to Grind. Axtell's own partner, Jimmy Nguyen, blinded him with cologne passed in by Chandler Tsonda, letting Penance recover to finish him. PWC TV, 22 March 2003: Penance retained the PWC Tag Team Championship, eliminating all three challenging teams in a gauntlet match: pinning Sammy Bello of Special Delivery with the Ideological Crucifixion, chokebombing Scourge of Total Violation, and finishing with a tombstone piledriver on Gunner Gojoh of the Deathmatch Samurai.

reigns.label: 2GVC

won.source: The fed's write-up of PWC TV of 5 April 2003; the fed's own title history lists the change.

lost.source: The fed's write-up of Last Man Standing 2003.

reigns.note: The Second Generation Viet Cong (Jimmy Nguyen and Chandler Tsonda) won the PWC Tag Team Championship from Penance in a Boiler Room Brawl, Tsonda diving into the ring first with both belts after Nguyen dragged Totakoxe Salvador back off the ring apron by the foot. Penance had abandoned the match to carry off Jim Axtell on Jacob Solomon's orders, leaving no one behind to stop 2GVC's dash. Defences on record. Capitol Punishment, 13 April 2003: 2GVC retained the PWC Tag Team Championship in a four-way defence, Chandler Tsonda pinning Ryo Kazaki of the Deathmatch Samurai with the Model Citizen off the top rope as Charlie Loc held Kazaki down. Jimmy Nguyen ran in to superkick Kazaki and turn the numbers back in 2GVC's favor after Tsonda had accidentally sprayed hairspray in referee Gil McGoosen's face. PWC TV, 26 April 2003: 2GVC retained the PWC Tag Team Championship, Chandler Tsonda pinning Colossus of the Roman Empire with the Model Citizen moonsault off the top rope. Jimmy Nguyen blindsided Romulus with a spinning calf kick just before he could break up the count.

reigns.title: pwc-wrestleonline-2003-tag-team
reigns.label: Chandler Tsonda

won.source: The fed's write-up of Last Man Standing 2003.

reigns.note: Chandler Tsonda became the sole holder of the PWC Tag Team Championship, the belts the show calls the "Alliance" titles, when Ron Starr released his injured partners, Jimmy Nguyen and Charlie Loc, after Tsonda ran them down with Loc's own car in the parking lot the night before. A defence is on record. Last Man Standing, 15 June 2003: Chandler Tsonda retained both PWC Tag Team Championship belts, billed as the Alliance belts, alone in a handicap match, pinning the Masked Mullet with the Model Citizen moonsault off the top rope. No match decides the hand-off: it happens off the cards, between the shows of 14 June and 15 June 2003. 2GVC's reign ends there with no loss on record.

reigns.title: pwc-wrestleonline-2003-television
reigns.label: Hoyt Williams

won.source: The fed's write-up of PWC TV of 3 May 2003.

reigns.note: Hoyt Williams became the first PWC Television Champion when Propaganda interrupted a Jake Keeton pinfall to chokeslam Keeton, then dropped Hoyt on top of him for the count. It was the fourth meeting between the two, after three earlier matches had left the title unclaimed. Defences on record. PWC TV, 10 May 2003: Hoyt Williams retained the PWC Television Championship by count-out, Gunner Gojoh leaving the ring to save his Deathmatch Samurai partner Ryo Kazaki from a beatdown by Total Violation shown on the arena screen. PWC TV, 24 May 2003: Hoyt Williams retained the PWC Television Championship, pinning Caleb McGlocklan after Propaganda knocked him out cold with a punch from the ring apron behind the referee's back.

reigns.title: pwc-wrestleonline-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jim Axtell

won.source: The fed's write-up of Capitol Punishment of 13 April 2003.

reigns.note: Jim Axtell became the first PWC World Heavyweight Champion, reversing Penance's Ideological Crucifixion into a sunset flip for the pin. Defences on record. PWC TV, 10 May 2003: Jim Axtell retained the PWC World Heavyweight Championship, making Jonathan Conspiracy submit to the Ax to Grind. PWC TV, 7 June 2003: Jim Axtell retained the PWC World Heavyweight Championship by disqualification, Magnum Wolf blindsiding him with a chair shot while Angelo Deville was caught in the Ax to Grind. Last Man Standing, 15 June 2003: Jim Axtell retained the PWC World Heavyweight Championship in a handicap match, locking the Ax to Grind on Penance for the tap-out after tricking him into crashing into his own manager, Jacob Solomon.

Trinidad, The Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid and El Diablo. A defence is on record. Adrenaline 2, 16 November 2003: Karina Wolfenden hooked The Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid's legs after pulling him in over the top rope with a Huricanrana from the apron and pinned him to retain the Eclipse Title.

reigns.title: rpw-rushpro-2003-eclipse

A defence is on record. Adrenaline 4, 30 November 2003: El Diablo hit Ilan Levin with the Brain Disorder as the time limit expired before the referee finished the three count, so the match was ruled a time limit draw and Levin kept the Eclipse Title.

reigns.title: rpw-rushpro-2003-eclipse
reigns.label: Karina Wolfenden

won.source: The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 7.

lost.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 10, which has Karina Wolfenden as champion, and Adrenaline 17, where Carys enters as the Eclipse champion with the belt; the change is on no card that is held.

reigns.note: Karina Wolfenden hit Ilan Levin with the Three Sixty Alien Drop and pinned him in a three way with Brianna Washington to win the Eclipse Title back. Defences on record. Adrenaline 9, 18 January 2004: Karina Wolfenden hit The Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid with the Whirlwind Romance, a tornado seatbelt DDT, onto a chair and pinned him to retain the Eclipse Title in the first match under the new Eclipse Rules. Adrenaline 10, 25 January 2004: Karina Wolfenden sprang off the ropes with a Huricanrana that drove Violence Jack's head onto a chair and pinned him with his legs locked to retain the Eclipse Title, after Magnum Wolf had hit Jack with a chair while she was tied in the ropes.

reigns.title: rpw-rushpro-2003-eclipse

Adrenaline 21, 18 April 2004: Carys covered Tessa Windsor and got the three after Chris Storm hit Tessa in the back with the Mid South belt as she came off the ropes, so Carys retained the Eclipse Title in a no disqualification match.

reigns.note: Gideon Poe hit El Diablo with the Cadaver Theory and pinned him to become the first RPW World Heavyweight Champion at Genesis, a show whose write-up has not been loaded. Defences on record. Adrenaline 10, 25 January 2004: Gideon Poe hit Peter Maxwell with the Cadaver Theory, then flew off the turnbuckle with the Suicide Anthem and pinned him, with Jason O'Neil counting as special guest referee, to retain the World Heavyweight Championship. Adrenaline 18, 28 March 2004: Gideon Poe kicked Nascosto Nerezza in the throat and covered him without hooking the leg to retain the World Heavyweight Championship. Adrenaline 20, 11 April 2004: Gideon Poe dropped to his knees with Christian Alexander Kannon over his shoulder for a backdrop piledriver and pinned him to retain the World Heavyweight Championship in a triple threat with Jason O'Neil.

reigns.title: rpw-rushpro-2003-heavyweight
reigns.label: Invincible Gabe

won.source: The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 21.

lost.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 24 and Adrenaline 25: the first has Invincible Gabe as champion going into The Kannon Effect, the second has Karina Wolfenden as the new champion from it; the pay-per-view's own card is not held.

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — Argyle's booking record dates Adrenaline 23 as 25 April 2004; the show's own page dates it 9 May 2004 from the fed's own news posts, and this history follows the page. Invincible Gabe won the World Heavyweight Championship in a six way when Christian Alexander Kannon restarted the match as sudden death, because Gideon Poe had tapped out to Magnum Wolf's Triangle Hold while Gabe's pin on Violence Jack was being counted, and Gabe hit Wolf with the Apocalyptic Chartbusting Last Dancing Stone Gabe Stunner and pinned him. A defence is on record. Adrenaline 23, 9 May 2004: Invincible Gabe retained the World Heavyweight Championship by count out after Gideon Poe left the ring to save Quinton Dufresne from Peter Maxwell's chair and was still on the ramp at the count of ten.

reigns.title: rpw-rushpro-2003-heavyweight
reigns.label: Karina Wolfenden

won.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 24 and Adrenaline 25: the first has Invincible Gabe as champion going into The Kannon Effect, the second has Karina Wolfenden as the new champion from it; the pay-per-view's own card is not held.

reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE — The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 32 has Karina Wolfenden say she overcame five of the roster's best and that Gideon Poe handed her the belt; the write-up of Adrenaline 25 has her take it from Gabe at The Kannon Effect after he lay down. The date window rests on the first account, and both are recorded. Argyle's booking record dates Adrenaline 30 as 4 July 2004; the show's own page dates it 11 July 2004 from the fed's own news posts, and this history follows the page. Argyle's booking record dates Adrenaline 32 as 18 July 2004; the show's own page dates it 25 July 2004 from the fed's own news posts, and this history follows the page. Karina Wolfenden took the World Heavyweight Championship from Invincible Gabe at The Kannon Effect, a pay-per-view whose card is not held; the write-up of the next show has Gabe say he lay down for her. Defences on record. Adrenaline 30, 11 July 2004: Magnum Wolf swatted Tessa Windsor off the top rope with a steel chair and the bell rang, so the match ended with no decision and Karina Wolfenden kept the World Heavyweight Championship. Adrenaline 32, 25 July 2004: Karina Wolfenden hit Brian Arson with a Pump Dropkick and caught him in a Small Package for the three after Christian Alexander Kannon had a replay show Magnum Wolf knocking her foot off the rope and the match continued, so she retained the World Heavyweight Championship.

Both readings are recorded. Chris Storm was the Mid South Champion by 21 March 2004; the write-ups say he won a tournament for the belt, which is on no card that is held. Defences on record. Adrenaline 20, 11 April 2004: Chris Storm hit Karina Wolfenden with the RyoPlex and pinned her to retain the Mid South Title. Adrenaline 21, 18 April 2004: Chris Storm hit Kohana with the Cherry Blossom, a Hangman's DDT from the second rope, and pinned him to retain the Mid South Title.

Second, Rising From the Ashes (13 Oct 2002; the fed's own pay-per-view script, served as a document): Sheila Tyrone announces "the RUSH Network Title", Livewire beats Joe Bananas with the Electricity ("Winner: Livewire", "LIVEWIRE KEEPS THE NETWORK TITLE!"), and the fed's own newsdesk has it in Bananas's own words, "Ah lost ta Livewire at Rising From the Ashes". The reign ended after the fed's own record: the fed's own title log carries no later Network change and its own title list (about October 2002) still names him champion, but the PCW card of Fusion 101 (20 Dec 2002) has Matt Hunt walk out with "his newly acquired Network Title", saying he won it "last week on Turmoil", and the commentary calls Livewire "past his prime" (reign r005); how Livewire lost it is on no served card.

MATTHIAS KUNTZ-HUNT!"). On Turmoil 108 (14 Jan 2003) he is introduced as "the RUSH Network Champion" against Ebola III, the Syndicate champion, in a match billed for neither belt. On the card of Adrenaline 5 (30 May 2002) he announces it himself: "I deserve not da 'Syndicate title' but my own! Datz why I'm officially renamin' da title to da \"Quo title\" fo' as long as my reign as champion!!", with a custom platinum belt unveiled on camera and a champion-declared stipulation, "from now on, diz title will only be defended in no disqualification matches". He repeats it on Adrenaline 10: "I am the QUO CHAMPION!!". This is not a second belt and not a rename by the federation: the announce team calls it degrading the Syndicate title, the fed's own title list keeps the name Syndicate Championship, the page heads its list "Syndicate Championship", and the next champion's own words are "how long it took for El Spiffy! to get the Quo-stink off of the belt". Statuz Quo retains his Syndicate Title") and Adrenaline 11 (25 Jul 2002, beat Caleb McGlocklan by pinfall). A fourth match is explicitly not a title match: on Adrenaline 10 Sheila Tyrone introduces "a non-title match", which Statuz Quo lost to William 'Biohazard' Perry. The page's "Longest Title Holder: Statuz Quo-87 days" agrees exactly with 23 May to 18 August.

So why don't you just keep this belt for now"), the real El Spiffy! was found tied up backstage, and Stimpo laid him out and took the belt again on Adrenaline 19. For HIS Spiffy-cate title"); the fed's own pay-per-view script, served as a document, has Sheila Tyrone announce "here is your winner, and STILL RUSH Wrestling Syndicate Champion, EL SPIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIFFYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY" and James Williams say he returned "JUST A DAY AFTER BEING HOSPITALIZED FOR A BACK INJURY" to defend it. The reign ended after the fed's own record, which carries no later Syndicate change and whose title list (about October 2002) still names him champion: the PCW card of Turmoil 102 (3 Dec 2002) has Stimpo "winning his first title, the Syndicate Title on Sunday Adrenaline defeating both Ebola III and Spiffy! in their triple threat match" (the Adrenaline of Sunday 1 Dec 2002, on no capture), and Decimation 2002's commentary says "Even when he lost his belt, Stimpo pinned Ebola in the triple threat to end it!" and that he held "the belt for 107 days"; 18 Aug to 1 Dec 2002 is 105 days; the commentary's count and the calendar differ, and no length is claimed.
