reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-generations
reigns.label: Ace Newton

won.source: The World is Watching, Thursday, Week 2, April 2008 (in-game).

reigns.how: The first champion, who won the belt by eliminating Robbie Retro last in a ten-man battle royal at The World is Watching and kept it against Gino Montero on Generation Supreme on Friday, Week 3, April 2008. He lost it to Robbie Retro on Supreme TV in Week 1 of June 2008.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-generations
reigns.label: Robbie Retro

won.source: Supreme TV, Tuesday, Week 1, June 2008 (in-game).

reigns.how: Won the belt from Ace Newton on Supreme TV in Week 1 of June 2008 with Murder on the Dance Floor and kept it against Paul Huntingdon on Supreme TV in Week 2 of June 2008. He kept it against Sean Deeley on Supreme TV in Week 1 of July 2008. He kept it against Ash Campbell on Supreme TV in Week 3 of July 2008 and lost it to Ace Newton in a Threefold Threat with Jay Chord on Supreme TV in Week 4.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-generations
reigns.label: Ace Newton

won.source: Supreme TV, Tuesday, Week 4, July 2008 (in-game).

reigns.how: Won the belt back from Robbie Retro in a Threefold Threat with Jay Chord on Supreme TV in Week 4 of July 2008, hitting Retro with a low blow and Chord with his finisher before pinning Retro with his feet on the ropes; in Week 1 of August 2008 the Four Kings and Playboy Jake Sawyer gave him a new belt, which Richard Eisen called the new official Generations Championship. He kept it against Kirk Jameson on Supreme TV in Week 3 of August 2008 and, in the SWF.com recaps of Generation Supreme, against El Leon and Swoop McCarthy; a match against Gino Montero for it is billed for Week 2 of September.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-legends
reigns.label: Chris Caufield

won.source: SWF Legends, Wednesday, Week 1, June 2008 (in-game).

reigns.how: The first champion, who won the four-way elimination match for the belt on the first SWF Legends, eliminating John McClean, then Runaway Train, and wore it to the ring in his non-title match with Eric Eisen on SWF Legends in Week 2 of June 2008. He kept it against Enygma on SWF Legends in June 2008, against Texas Pete, by count-out, on SWF Legends in Week 4 of June and against Enforcer Roberts on SWF Legends in Week 2 of July 2008. He lost it to Bloodstone at The Supreme Challenge 28, the referee stopping the match in the camel clutch while Caufield insisted he had not submitted.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-legends
reigns.label: Johnny Bloodstone

won.source: The Supreme Challenge 28, in-game Week 2 of July 2008 (post #300).

reigns.how: Won the belt from Chris Caufield at The Supreme Challenge 28 when the referee stopped the match as Bloodstone held the camel clutch, Caufield insisting he never submitted. He kept it against Brett Biggz on SWF Legends in Week 4 of July 2008 and against Pistol Pete Hall on SWF Legends in Week 1 of August 2008, and Robbie Retro says he has been put into a match with Bloodstone and Caufield for the belt at Welcome to the Jungle 2008. He kept it at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 in a Threefold Threat against Robbie Retro and Chris Caufield, pinning Caufield with an elbow from the top rope, and against Robbie Retro on SWF Legends in Week 4 of August 2008, when the referee stopped the match in the Bloodstone Mutilation.
reigns.note: The post for this SWF Legends show reads "Wednesday, Week 2, July 2008" in its own heading; the Fry Report preview posted before it ("Wednesday, Week 4, July 2008") and the shows either side of it place it in Week 4, and this record follows them.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-north-american
reigns.label: Steve Frehley

won.source: The World is Watching, Thursday, Week 2, April 2008 (in-game); the vacating is Supreme TV, Tuesday, Week 3, April 2008.

reigns.how: Won in a no-disqualification, no-count-out match against Rich Money at The World is Watching; Frehley then lays the belt down in the ring on Supreme TV, refusing to defend it, and Richard Eisen takes it away.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-north-american
reigns.label: Marc DuBois

won.source: Master of Puppets 2008, Thursday, Week 2, May 2008 (in-game).

reigns.how: Won the eight-man Grand Prix for the vacant title by beating Rocky Golden in the semi final and Eric Eisen in the final at Master of Puppets 2008; kept it against Thom Barrowman on Supreme TV in Week 3 of May, against Elmo Benson on the first SWF Legends and against Remo, by count-out, on Supreme TV in Week 2 of June 2008. He kept it in a three-way against Runaway Train and Antonio Marquez at Times of Trouble 2008, against Valiant on Supreme TV in Week 4 of June and, when Chris Morrisette won by disqualification for a belt shot, on Supreme TV in Week 1 of July 2008. He kept it at The Supreme Challenge 28 in a Threefold Threat against Zimmy Bumfhole and Antonio Marquez, when Darryl Devine's interference let him throw the referee in front of Marquez's shooting star press and pin Bumfhole, and is booked for another Threefold Threat at Welcome to the Jungle 2008. He kept it in the Threefold Threat at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 when Darryl Devine tapped to the Model Solution sleeper, beat Zimmy Bumfhole on Supreme TV in Week 4 of August 2008 and Scout of The New Wave in Week 1 of September, and is billed against Art Reed in Week 2.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-north-american
reigns.label: Rich Money

won.source: The diary opens with Rich Money as North American champion (Supreme TV, Tuesday, Week 1, March 2008); it does not date the win; dates are the diary's own in-game dates.

reigns.how: Rich Money's reign as the diary opens; the diary does not say when he won it. He keeps it against Eric Tyler, Randy Bumfhole and Christian Faith and loses it to Steve Frehley at The World is Watching.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-shooting-star
reigns.label: Darryl Devine

won.source: The World is Watching, Thursday, Week 2, April 2008 (in-game).

reigns.how: Won in a ladder match against Marc DuBois at The World is Watching, and kept against Mainstream Hernandez on Generation Supreme on Friday, Week 3, April 2008. He kept it in the three-way ladder match at Times of Trouble 2008 and lost it to Kid Toma on SWF Legends in June 2008, when Akima Brave and BJ O'Neill distracted the referee and Toma, Akima and Tana used a chair.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-shooting-star
reigns.label: Kid Toma

won.source: SWF Legends, in-game June 2008 (the post's own heading reads "Wednesday, Week 1, June 2008"; the Fry Report posts either side of it place the show in Week 3).

reigns.how: Won the belt from Darryl Devine on SWF Legends in June 2008 after Akima Brave and BJ O'Neill distracted the referee and Toma, Akima and Tana used a chair on the champion; kept it against Brett Biggz and American Elemental on SWF Legends in Week 4 of June and against Jacob Jett on SWF Legends in Week 2 of July 2008. He kept it against Remmy Skye on SWF Legends in Week 4 of July 2008, the night Eric Tyler handed him a redesigned belt; Bart Biggz earned a shot at the Welcome to the Jungle 2008 pay-per-view by beating Akima Brave by disqualification in Week 1 of August. He lost it to Acid in a Threefold Threat with Bart Biggz at Welcome to the Jungle 2008, Acid pinning him.
reigns.note: The post for this SWF Legends show reads "Wednesday, Week 2, July 2008" in its own heading; the Fry Report preview posted before it ("Wednesday, Week 4, July 2008") and the shows either side of it place it in Week 4, and this record follows them.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-shooting-star
reigns.label: Acid

won.source: Welcome to the Jungle 2008, in-game Week 2 of August 2008 (post #467).

reigns.how: Won the belt from Kid Toma in a Threefold Threat with Bart Biggz at Welcome to the Jungle 2008, on his first night in the SWF's big shows, pinning Toma after the Acid Rain Bomb swandive senton. He kept it against El Leon and Mainstream Hernandez on SWF Legends in Week 3 of August 2008, against Remmy Skye by submission in Week 4 and against John Greed and Mainstream Hernandez in Week 1 of September; Bart Biggz asks for a one-on-one match for it.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-shooting-star
reigns.label: Marc DuBois

won.source: The diary opens with Marc DuBois as Shooting Star champion (Supreme TV, Tuesday, Week 1, March 2008); it does not date the win; dates are the diary's own in-game dates.

reigns.how: Marc DuBois's reign as the diary opens, which the diary does not date; he keeps it in ladder matches against Enygma and Antonio Marquez and loses it to Darryl Devine at The World is Watching.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-sky-club-tag-team
reigns.label: High Concept

won.source: Welcome to the Jungle 2008, in-game Week 2 of August 2008 (post #467).

reigns.how: The first champions: Elmo Benson and Groucho Bling beat The Tokyo Underground at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 when Benson pinned Narato after the Game Over; the two teams had qualified for the final on SWF Legends in Week 2 of August 2008. They kept the belts against Double Deuce on SWF Legends in Week 4 of August, and lost a non-title match to Golden & Bloodstone in Week 1 of September.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-supreme
reigns.label: Christian Faith

won.source: The Supreme Challenge 28, in-game Week 2 of July 2008 (post #300).

reigns.how: The first champion, who beat Brandon James with the Test of Faith sleeper at The Supreme Challenge 28 and received the belt from Phil Vibert. He kept it in a Threefold Threat against Bloodstone and Eric Eisen on SWF Legends in Week 3 of July 2008, against Troy Tornado on SWF Legends in Week 4 of July and against Texas Pete on SWF Legends in Week 1 of August 2008, and is booked against Vengeance for Welcome to the Jungle 2008. He beat Vengeance at Welcome to the Jungle 2008, after which Vengeance put him through the timekeeper's table, beat Bryan Holmes on SWF Legends in Week 3 of August 2008, and kept the belt by disqualification in a Threefold Threat with Steve Frehley and Rocky Golden in Week 4; he is booked in a Threefold Threat with Brandon James and Steve Frehley for Under Control 2008.
reigns.note: The post for this SWF Legends show reads "Wednesday, Week 2, July 2008" in its own heading; the Fry Report preview posted before it ("Wednesday, Week 4, July 2008") and the shows either side of it place it in Week 4, and this record follows them.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jack Bruce

won.source: The diary's own later posts: "since winning the SWF World Heavyweight title back in August" (the Fry Report preview posted 7 October 2008) and "the first time since last August when Bruce won the belt" (in-game March 2008).

reigns.how: Jack Bruce's reign as the diary opens: the diary's later posts date it from last August, and Bruce says he took the belt from Runaway Train; he keeps it through Brandon James at Awesome Impact and Remo at The World is Watching. His later posts: Bruce beats Vengeance in a Supreme Cell match at Master of Puppets 2008, beats Eric Eisen at Times of Trouble 2008, beats Antonio Marquez and John McClean on Supreme TV in Week 3 of June and Jay Chord in Week 2 of July 2008, and is booked for Supreme Double Jeopardy at The Supreme Challenge 28. He beat Eric Tyler and Vengeance in the first Supreme Double Jeopardy match at The Supreme Challenge 28, then lost the belt to Rich Money in the second, ending a reign the SWF.com review puts at some eleven months.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Rich Money

won.source: The Supreme Challenge 28, in-game Week 2 of July 2008 (post #300).

reigns.how: Won the title from Jack Bruce in the second Supreme Double Jeopardy match at The Supreme Challenge 28: out of the first match after a disqualification loss to Randy Bumfhole, he came down the ramp in a suit and took it off piece by piece while Richard Eisen hesitated, and pinned Bruce after his finisher. He says the belt will be defended only on pay-per-view, makes Bruce and Randy Bumfhole each beat Remo for a shot, beats Valiant in a non-title match on Supreme TV in Week 4 of July 2008, replaces the belt with a black one set with diamonds, and is booked in a Threefold Threat with Bruce and Bumfhole at Welcome to the Jungle 2008. He kept it at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 in a Threefold Threat against Jack Bruce and Randy Bumfhole, pinning Bruce, and against Guide of The New Wave on Supreme TV in Week 3 of August 2008; on a video he turned down Bruce's challenge for Under Control 2008, and Pistol Pete Hall is billed against him for the belt on Supreme TV in Week 2 of September.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-world-tag-team
reigns.label: Sexual Aggression

won.source: The diary's set-up post ("The only title change was Sexual Aggression winning the tag titles in February") and its TEW.com monthly report for February 2008.

reigns.how: Sexual Aggression took the belts from The Amazing Bumfholes at Nothing to Lose in February 2008, then defends them on Supreme TV, at Awesome Impact and at The World is Watching. They lost the belts to Valiant & Giedroyc on the first SWF Legends in Week 1 of June 2008, after Joe Sexy walked out on Angry Gilmore.

reigns.title: swf-generation-supreme-world-tag-team
reigns.label: Valiant & Giedroyc

won.source: SWF Legends, Wednesday, Week 1, June 2008 (in-game).

reigns.how: Won the belts from Sexual Aggression on the first SWF Legends, when Joe Sexy walked out on Angry Gilmore mid-match and Giedroyc pinned Gilmore, and kept them against Last Chance on SWF Legends in Week 2 of June 2008. They kept them in the four-way at Times of Trouble 2008 when Giedroyc's stoppage win ended it, then against The Heartbreakers on Supreme TV in Week 1 of July and The Upper Class on Supreme TV in Week 2 of July 2008. They kept them at The Supreme Challenge 28 in a Threefold Threat against The New Wave and Badd Kompany, when Valiant pinned Joss Thompson, and are booked against Sin Inc for Welcome to the Jungle 2008. They kept them at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 against Sin Inc, when Giedroyc rolled up John McClean, against The Upper Class on Supreme TV in Week 3 of August 2008 and against The Heartbreakers in Week 1 of September; Richard Eisen names The New Wave the next challengers.

reigns.note: The retrospective states Marx "will be returning to SWIFT and will retain the title he earned" as of its own July 2011 date, so no loss is recorded.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Edd Stone

won.source: Total Mayhem 13, Sunday Week 4 May 2008 (in-game): 'Edd Stone defeated Sammy Bach for the All Action Championship'.

reigns.how: Won from Sammy Bach at Total Mayhem 13 with a top-rope Party's Over, the Syndicate's fourth belt. He defends it at Excessive Force in June 2008 in the Hangtime Match of his own devising, against Sammy Bach and Acid, and keeps it. He keeps it through July 2008, beating Hell Monkey at Summer Showdown with the Party's Over. He keeps it through August 2008: Art Reed, the fans' choice, beats him at Hotter Than Hell only by count out. He keeps it through September 2008, beating the Cannonball Kid on Badge of Honor and Art Reed again at Destructive Energy. He loses it to Frankie Perez at Crunch Time in October 2008, when Perez catches him with a mule kick to the head and applies the P-Clutch.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Frankie Perez

won.source: Crunch Time, Sunday Week 4 October 2008 (in-game): 'Frankie Perez defeated Edd Stone'.

reigns.how: Won from Edd Stone at Crunch Time with the P-Clutch, after a mule kick to the head sends Stone spinning and Perez drags him back to the centre of the ring by the hair; the diary calls it his first TCW gold, won in around nine months with the company. He keeps it through November 2008, losing a non-title match to Rick Law on Badge of Honor; at A Little South Of Sanity, in his first defence, he beats Art Reed, Greg Keith and Freddy Huggins, working over Keith's injured arm and clamping on the P-Clutch for the submission. He keeps it through December 2008: at Psycho Circus, with Phil Vibert at his side, he beats Hell Monkey with the P-Clutch after Hell Monkey's Tumbling Monkey misses.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-all-action-championship
reigns.label: Sammy Bach

won.source: The diary's roster entry of 20 February 2008 calls him 'a champion, the All-Action guy'; it does not date his win.

reigns.how: Champion when the diary opens; keeps it against Johnny Bloodstone at Where Angels Fear To Tread (a disqualification) and loses it to Edd Stone at Total Mayhem 13.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-hard-hitting-championship
reigns.label: Sam Keith

won.source: Excessive Force, Sunday Week 4 June 2008 (in-game): 'Sam Keith defeated Eddie Peak, Ricky Dale Johnson, and Tyson Baine'.

reigns.how: The first champion: won the four-way No Holds Barred match at Excessive Force over Eddie Peak, Ricky Dale Johnson and Tyson Baine, thumbing Baine in the eye, kicking him low and making him tap to the Proton Lock with the ropes for leverage. He keeps it through July 2008, winning by disqualification over Tyson Baine on Total Wrestling and beating Ricky Dale Johnson at Summer Showdown with the Proton Lock. He keeps it through August 2008, beating Sammy Bach on Total Wrestling and Tommy Cornell in a No Holds Barred match at Hotter Than Hell with the Proton Lock. He keeps it through September 2008, drawing with Chris Rockwell on Total Wrestling and beating Jeremy Stone in a No Holds Barred match at Destructive Energy with the Proton Lock. He keeps it through November 2008, beating JD Morgan with the Proton Lock and being hit with a chair by Sammy Bach; at A Little South Of Sanity he beats Bach with the NeutronPlex. He keeps it through December 2008: at Psycho Circus, in a No Holds Barred match with Sammy Bach, he is not beaten; Bach wins by disqualification when Texas Pete hits him with a chair, which the diary does not treat as a title change.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-international-championship
reigns.label: Koshiro Ino

won.source: Total Mayhem 13, Sunday Week 4 May 2008 (in-game): 'Koshiro Ino defeated Wolf Hawkins for the International Championship'.

reigns.how: Won from Wolf Hawkins in a no-disqualification match at Total Mayhem 13 with the Kobra's Bite. He keeps it through June 2008: he beats Sam Keith on Total Wrestling in Week 2, and at Excessive Force he loses to Chris Rockwell by disqualification, which the diary's next preview (p249) treats as no change, billing Ino as champion. He keeps it through July 2008: the diary's result line has Tommy Cornell beating him on Total Wrestling by disqualification after Sam Keith's chairshot, which leaves the title with Ino (the next preview bills him as champion), and at Summer Showdown he beats Sammy Bach with the Kobra's Bite. He loses it to John Anderson at Hotter Than Hell in August 2008, when Anderson boots him in the gut and lands the Ammo Dump onto his injured head.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-international-championship
reigns.label: John Anderson

won.source: Hotter Than Hell, Sunday Week 4 August 2008 (in-game): 'John Anderson defeated Koshiro Ino', 'giving TCW a new International Championship'.

reigns.how: Won from Koshiro Ino at Hotter Than Hell with the Ammo Dump onto Ino's injured head, after Ino's head hit the ringpost, Ino taking too long to cover after Wolf Hawkins hit Anderson with the Full Moon Rising on his behalf; the diary calls it 'a new International Championship', and the Syndicate's Tommy Cornell growls that Anderson remembered how to wrestle once they let him go. He keeps it through September 2008, beaten only by count out by Wolf Hawkins, then beating Frankie Perez, Acid and, at Destructive Energy, Eric Tyler with the Ammo Dump. He keeps it through October 2008, drawing with Sean Deeley and beating Jack Marlowe with the Ammo Dump; at Crunch Time, answering his own open challenge, he is beaten by Deeley by count-out, which the diary does not treat as a title change. He keeps it through November 2008, beating Texas Pete with the Ammo Dump after Wolf Hawkins' interference; at A Little South Of Sanity he beats Pete and Hawkins in a three-way match, pinning Hawkins with the Ammo Dump. He keeps it through December 2008, beating American Buffalo with the Ammo Dump, drawing with Wolf Hawkins at the time limit and, at Psycho Circus, beating Hawkins clean with the Ammo Dump after fifteen minutes.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-international-championship
reigns.label: Wolf Hawkins

won.source: The diary's roster entry of 18 February 2008 calls him 'Currently the International champion'; it does not date his win.

reigns.how: Champion when the diary opens; keeps it at Where Angels Fear To Tread through Sam Keith's interference and loses it to Koshiro Ino at Total Mayhem 13.
reigns.note: At Where Angels Fear To Tread the diary's result line reads 'Koshiro Ino defeated Wolf Hawkins', but its match report has Hawkins pinning Ino and keeping the title, and the May shows bill Hawkins as champion until Total Mayhem 13.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Machines

won.source: The diary's Total Mayhem 13 preview (Sunday Week 4 May 2008) calls the title 'now celebrating a full year in the possession of the Machines', and Troy Tornado tells the Young Guns 'The Machines? They won those belts a year ago'; the month is that year back from May 2008.

reigns.how: Champions when the diary opens; retain against Painful Procedure at Where Angels Fear To Tread and against the Young Guns at Total Mayhem 13. They lose the belts to the New Wave at Excessive Force in June 2008.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The New Wave

won.source: Excessive Force, Sunday Week 4 June 2008 (in-game): 'The New Wave defeated The Machines'.

reigns.how: Won from the Machines at Excessive Force when Scout made John Anderson submit to the Special Force, with the Young Guns at ringside to stop Syndicate backup: Troy Tornado had put the New Wave in the Young Guns' place for the match in return for the Young Guns' first shot at the belts after they won them. They keep the belts through July 2008, beating the Young Guns at Summer Showdown with the Special Force. They keep the belts through August 2008, beating the Easy Riders and the British Lions on television and the School of Tradition at Hotter Than Hell. They keep the belts through September 2008, beating the Keith Brothers, the Enforcers and, at Destructive Energy, the School of Tradition. They keep the belts through October 2008, drawing with the Stone Brothers and beating Acid Dragon and the British Lions; at Crunch Time they beat the Easy Riders only by disqualification. They keep the belts through November 2008, beating the Elite Express, the British Lions and, in non-title matches, American Buffalo & JD Morgan, and going to a no contest with the Keith Brothers; at A Little South Of Sanity they beat the Easy Riders and the Stone Brothers in a three-team elimination match, Scout's Special Force finishing the Stones. They lose the belts to the Easy Riders at Psycho Circus in December 2008 in a hardcore match, Scout choked against the turnbuckle with a chain and Guide finished with the Emergency Stop onto a steel chair.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Easy Riders

won.source: Psycho Circus, Sunday Week 4 December 2008 (in-game): 'Easy Riders defeated the New Wave'.

reigns.how: Won from the New Wave at Psycho Circus in a hardcore match, Billy Fonda and Peter Hopper beating down Scout, anchoring him to the turnbuckle with a chain that Carl Batch holds round his neck, and finishing Guide with the Emergency Stop onto a steel chair; the diary notes that the New Wave's long reign has ended and that it is not sure the Easy Riders will endure as long.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-world-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Troy Tornado

won.source: Excessive Force, Sunday Week 4 June 2008 (in-game): 'Troy Tornado defeated Tommy Cornell', 'Suddenly, TCW has a new World Heavyweight Champion.'

reigns.how: Won from Tommy Cornell at Excessive Force, coming off a failed top-rope attack with the Star Maker, after Painful Procedure ringed the match to cut off Syndicate help; Edd Stone's missile dropkick from the Hangtime structure and a Savate Kick from Steve Gumble on Cornell came first. He keeps it through July 2008, beating Chris Rockwell and Wolf Hawkins in a three-way match at Summer Showdown with the Star Maker. He keeps it through August 2008, beating Brent Hill and Wolf Hawkins in a three-way match at Hotter Than Hell. He is still champion at the end of September 2008; at Destructive Energy, in a three-way match with Johnny Bloodstone and Tommy Cornell, he and Bloodstone together make Cornell submit, and Mayhem Midden says he must take the result to the Board. He keeps it through October 2008, carrying a new custom belt as the Standing Champion, beating Sammy Bach & Wolf Hawkins with Koshiro Ino and drawing with Sam Keith against Jeremy Stone & Tommy Cornell; at Crunch Time he beats Jeremy Stone and Remo Richardson in a three-way match with the Star Maker. He keeps it through November 2008: on Total Wrestling in the first week the Board's edict recognises his belt and Johnny Bloodstone's and orders the two unified at Malice in Wonderland in January; he beats Jeremy Stone with the Star Maker, beats Tommy Cornell & Tyson Baine with Rick Law and loses a six-man match with John Anderson and Johnny Bloodstone to Chris Rockwell, Tommy Cornell & Wolf Hawkins; at A Little South Of Sanity, with the belt not at stake, he beats Tommy Cornell with the Star Maker. He keeps it through December 2008, drawing with Eric Tyler in twenty minutes, fighting Tommy Cornell to a no contest when Jack Bruce returns and, at Psycho Circus, beating Eddie Peak and Jeremy Stone in a three-way match with the Star Maker after Cornell has attacked him and Peak with the retired TCW belt.

reigns.title: tcw-a-quiet-retirement-world-heavyweight-championship
reigns.label: Johnny Bloodstone

won.source: Crunch Time prediction key, Sunday Week 4 October 2008 (in-game): 'TCW World Heavyweight Championship (Canadian Belt)* Johnny Bloodstone (c)'; his claim comes from Destructive Energy in September 2008, and the diary shows the Board recognising his belt on Total Wrestling in the first week of November 2008.

reigns.how: Holder of the second World Heavyweight Championship belt the diary shows from October 2008, the Canadian Belt, after he and Troy Tornado together made Tommy Cornell submit at Destructive Energy and the Board left both men with a claim; the prediction key bills him '(c)'. He keeps it at Crunch Time, beating Brent Hill with the Bloodstone Mutilation, and the diary says the belts will be reunited sooner or later. He keeps it through November 2008: on Total Wrestling in the first week the Board's edict recognises his belt and Troy Tornado's and orders the two unified at Malice in Wonderland in January; he beats Sean Deeley on Badge of Honor, beats the Elite Express with Sam Keith and loses a six-man match with John Anderson and Troy Tornado to Chris Rockwell, Tommy Cornell & Wolf Hawkins; at A Little South Of Sanity he beats Chris Rockwell after half an hour, pinning him in an improvised pin attempt. He keeps it through December 2008, beating Edd Stone with the Bloodstone Mutilation on Total Wrestling and Merle O'Curle in a non-title match on Badge of Honor; the diary's Psycho Circus preview treats the match that decides who faces him at Malice in Wonderland as a title unification match.

This holder was named the federation's first ATLANTIC Champion on 28 December 1991; when he took this belt instead is not something any served document says. Four days after the relaunch call the same president wrote that all the champions were returning "with the exception of 2" — which two is not on record, so no reign here is ended on that sentence. THE HELD-BUT-UNSERVED RECORD CARRIES THIS REIGN RUNNING, THOUGH NOT ITS START (2026-09-02). The WeWF's own broadcasts of 15, 19 and 25 February 1992 have this holder as Intercontinental Champion at 10-0-0, beating Lord Plunder to retain, and beating Rage to retain, ending that week at 14-1-0. So the reign is continuous from at least mid-February to the relaunch call's recognition in May. Its beginning is still nowhere in the record, served or unserved.

reigns.title: uewf-ladies-world
reigns.label: Laurie Liberty

won.source: the Summit of E-Wrestling's own broadcast of 28 December 1991 (promotions/summit-of-e-wrestling/archive/summit-of-e-wrestling-day-2-1991-12-28.html): "The Winner and NEW UeWF Ladies Champion...... Laurie......LIB.....ERTY!!!!!!"

reigns.how: Won an eight-woman battle royal staged at the Summit of E-Wrestling to crown the federation's own first Ladies Champion: two women started and the other six entered at one-minute intervals, with the first and second ranked having had first pick of numbers five to eight, and elimination over the top rope only. Laurie Liberty drew last, was thrown over the top rope onto the apron and came back in through her opponent's legs, and won it by playing possum in the Angel of Death's grip and scooping her out. FOUND BY THE SUMMIT ACCESSION, 2026-09-02; the belt's own row had said no holder survived. No end to this reign is on the record: the federation's own relaunch call of 14 May 1992 closes the women's division rather than naming a champion, so the reign is left open and the division's closure is carried on the title row instead. THIS REIGN ENDED IN FEBRUARY 1992, AND THE ROW'S OWN "left open" IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN ERASED (2026-09-02). The WeWF's own This Week in Wrestling of 19 February 1992 — held in the Google Groups dumps, unserved — cuts to a clip of this federation's ladies title match and ends it on "JAckson covers......ONE!....TWO.....THREEEE!!!! We've got a new champion"; the following week's edition has "Sarah Jackson kept her Women's belt, when Rhonda Rhodes interfered saving Ms. Jackson from a pinfall at the hands of Laurie Liberty." Sarah Jackson took this belt from this holder in the third week of February 1992. No end date is written onto this row and no second reign is minted, because the documents belong to another wing and are not served; what is written is that the record is no longer silent, only unserved.
reigns.note: THE ROW SAID “the reign is left open” AND IT IS NOT. Sarah Jackson beat this holder for the belt on 19 February 1992, in a finish the WeWF's own newsdesk rolled as tape, and kept it against her six days later.

reigns.title: uewf-pacific
reigns.label: Lord Plunder

won.source: the Summit of E-Wrestling's own broadcast of 28 December 1991 (promotions/summit-of-e-wrestling/archive/summit-of-e-wrestling-day-2-1991-12-28.html), whose ring announcer sets the terms before the bell: "The Winner will advance to face in the Championship round and the loser will be be awarded the Pacific Championship Title."

reigns.how: Awarded on 28 December 1991 for losing the second of the federation's own two World Championship semi-finals, staged at the Summit of E-Wrestling and announced in advance as crowning a champion either way. Lucifer beat Lord Plunder with the HellRaiser, after throwing a packet of dust in his eyes, and after a man the announcers took for a blind spectator had climbed onto the apron and drawn the referee away — the broadcast never says who he was, only that his tights read "Totally Awesome Dude"; the Pacific Championship went to the loser. The federation's own relaunch call of 14 May 1992 still recognises this holder as its Pacific Champion, so the reign runs from the Summit to at least that date. DATED BY THE SUMMIT ACCESSION, 2026-09-02, which supersedes this row's earlier "no served document carries a match or a date for the start of this reign" — one now does. Four days after the relaunch call the same president wrote that all the champions were returning "with the exception of 2" — which two is not on record, so no reign here is ended on that sentence. THIS REIGN IS NOT CONTINUOUS, AND THE HELD RECORD SAYS SO (2026-09-02). The sentence above has this reign running from the Summit to at least 14 May 1992. It did not. The WeWF's own broadcasts of 15 and 19 February 1992 — held, unserved — have T'ien "The Master" Lung as this federation's Pacific Champion, at 12-1-1 and defending successfully against the Shropshire Slasher, with this holder first among the contenders; the broadcast of 25 February then has this holder win the belt back, "Lord Pluder beat Pacific Champion T'ien 'The Master' Lung by hitting him with an internation object," and prints "Pacific Champion: Lord Plunder (12-4-0)". So the reign dated here to 28 December 1991 ended before mid-February 1992, and the holder the relaunch call recognises in May is in a SECOND reign that begins in the last week of February. The row is not renumbered and no second reign is minted, because the documents that carry it belong to another wing and are not served; the correction is written here so nothing in this ledger reads as settled when it is not.
reigns.note: THIS REIGN DID NOT RUN UNBROKEN TO MAY 1992 AND THE ROW SAID IT DID. T'ien “the Master” Lung holds the belt in the WeWF newsdesk's own standings for this federation on 30 January, 15 February and 19 February 1992; this holder wins it back on 25 February, and that second reign is the one the relaunch call recognises. How this first reign ended is not carried by any held document — a gap, not a claim.

reigns.title: uewf-pacific
reigns.label: Lord Plunder (second reign)

won.source: the WeWF's own newsdesk of 25 February 1992: “Lord Pluder beat Pacific Champion T'ien ‘The Master’ Lung by hitting him with an internation object!” — and its standings that week read “Pacific Champion: Lord Plunder (12-4-0)” (promotions/wewf/archive/twiw-1992-02-25.html) served under the WeWF wing, accession lot 0144; under the tier rule the document belongs to that wing and the fact belongs here.

reigns.how: Beat T'ien “the Master” Lung with an international object.
reigns.note: This is the reign the federation's own relaunch call of 14 May 1992 recognises, not the one that began at the Summit on 28 December 1991.

reigns.title: uewf-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Lord Plunder

won.source: the WeWF's own newsdesk of 30 January 1992, whose standings for this federation read “World Champion: Lord Plunder (11-2-0)” (promotions/wewf/archive/twiw-1992-01-30.html) served under the WeWF wing, accession lot 0144; under the tier rule the document belongs to that wing and the fact belongs here. The date recorded is that broadcast's own; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: How he won it is not on the record as a match, but the same broadcast's rumour mill says how it happened: “The recent ‘administrative errors’ in the UeWF which allowed Lord Plunder to obtain the World Championship were a direct result of the bribing of the UeWFs chief officer - Harvey Wallbanger.”
reigns.note: Mr. B is champion in the same newsdesk's standings of 15 February 1992, so this reign ends on or before that date; the change itself is not carried by any held document. A gap, not a claim.

reigns.title: uewf-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Mr. B

won.source: the WeWF's own newsdesk of 15 February 1992, whose standings for this federation read “World Champion: Mr.B (11-2-1)” (promotions/wewf/archive/twiw-1992-02-15.html) served under the WeWF wing, accession lot 0144; under the tier rule the document belongs to that wing and the fact belongs here. Precision circa, meaning won on or before that broadcast.

reigns.how: Retained on 19 February by handing Admiral Ax the first loss of his career; lost the belt to the Ultimate Lanny six days later, to a superplex to the middle of the ring.
reigns.note: The newsdesk of 19 February 1992 carries the defense in its own late-breaking results: “Mr. B handed Admiral Ax the first loss of his career to retain the UeWF World Championship.”

reigns.title: uewf-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The Ultimate Lanny

won.source: the WeWF's own newsdesk of 25 February 1992, which stages the title change move for move: “Lanny's setting Mr.B up in the corner....SUPERPLEX to the middle of the ring, and the cover......” / “ONE! TWO!!.........THREEEEE!!!!!! We've got a new World Champion!!!!!” (promotions/wewf/archive/twiw-1992-02-25.html) served under the WeWF wing, accession lot 0144; under the tier rule the document belongs to that wing and the fact belongs here.

reigns.how: Beat Mr. B with a superplex to the middle of the ring, in a match the newsdesk called on tape.
reigns.note: THE DATE THIS ROW SAID NO SERVED DOCUMENT CARRIED IS NOW SERVED AND IS NOW WRITTEN ON. It has. The newsdesk's own standings that week read “World Champion: The Ultimate Lanny (15-3-1)”.

reigns.title: uewf-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Dangerous Emotions

won.source: the WeWF's own newsdesk of 30 January 1992, whose tag standings for this federation read “World Champions: Dangerous Emotions (12-2-0)” (promotions/wewf/archive/twiw-1992-01-30.html) served under the WeWF wing, accession lot 0144; under the tier rule the document belongs to that wing and the fact belongs here. Precision circa, meaning won on or before that broadcast.

reigns.how: Recognised as champion at the federation's own relaunch of 14 May 1992, which reinstates "the wrestlers who were champions before the UeWF's hiatus." No served document carries a match or a date for the start of this reign; the federation's own first title tournaments were staged at the Summit of E-Wrestling in December 1991, and the Summit accession of 2026-09-02 NARROWS THIS REIGN WITHOUT DATING IT: these holders reached the final of that inaugural tag-team tournament, beating Carnage on 30 December 1991, and the final itself — against the Armed Forces — was advertised for a fifth night no held document carries. Whether this reign began in that final or later is still not something any served document says. Four days after the relaunch call the same president wrote that all the champions were returning "with the exception of 2" — which two is not on record, so no reign here is ended on that sentence. THE HELD-BUT-UNSERVED RECORD CARRIES THIS BELT IN FEBRUARY 1992 AND CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT IT (2026-09-02). On 15 February the Dangerous Emotions' own manager calls them "the first UeWF tag-team champions"; on 19 February the newsdesk has them lose by disqualification to the Armed Forces and keep the belts; on 25 February it has the Armed Forces keep the belts by losing by disqualification to the Dangerous Emotions. One of the two is a transposition or a title change nobody reported. Recorded, not resolved, and nothing minted: all three documents are the WeWF's own and none is served.
reigns.note: THAT THIS IS THE FIRST REIGN ON THIS BELT IS NOW SETTLED BY THE TEAM'S OWN MANAGER, on camera at the Boston Garden on 15 February 1992: “Now that my Emotions are the first UeWF tag-team champions, I want you to know that they will be the ONLY tag-team champions.” They retain by disqualification on 19 February and win by disqualification on 25 February.

reigns.title: ufws-all-jobber
reigns.label: Baron Von Klaw
reigns.how: The first championship the federation ever awarded: Von Klaw took the Klaw hold on Sargent Glasnost and covered him at 4:44 in the All-Jobber tournament final, which was called before either other final. Lost it five weeks later when the Wolfman ducked his international object, took it and knocked him out with it.

reigns.title: ufws-all-jobber
reigns.label: The Wolfman
reigns.how: Won it with Von Klaw's own weapon, in the match the results desk says turned him into a fan favourite. Defended it three times in a fortnight and lost it to Bobby Windsor in 58 seconds.

reigns.title: ufws-all-jobber
reigns.label: Bobby “The Cavalier” Windsor
reigns.how: Won it in 58 seconds and defended it four times, twice against Baron Von Klaw's stablemates, before the Aztec Mummy took it with the Mummy's Claw at 1:18.

reigns.title: ufws-all-jobber
reigns.label: Bobby “The Cavalier” Windsor
reigns.how: A second reign, won inside the unheld Report #11 and defended against the Aztec Mummy in three consecutive issues — four weeks running against the same challenger, an oddity the broadcast itself complained about. Lost it to Baron Von Klaw, who kept the Klaw hold on until Windsor bled and had to be carried out. Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

reigns.title: ufws-all-jobber
reigns.label: The Aztec Mummy
reigns.how: A one-week reign held alongside the North American title — the only double championship in the federation's record. Lost the belt back to Bobby Windsor inside the unheld Report #11: Report #12's own results desk has Windsor “defending the All-Jobber title with success against the former champion, The Aztec Mummy.” Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

reigns.title: ufws-all-jobber
reigns.label: Baron Von Klaw
reigns.how: A second reign, eleven days long, ended by Sargent Glasnost's Japanese armlock in the Seattle card reported in the last surviving issue.

reigns.title: ufws-all-jobber
reigns.label: Sargent Glasnost
reigns.how: Won with the Japanese armlock over Baron Von Klaw, and holds the belt where the record ends.

reigns.title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
reigns.label: Death
reigns.how: Awarded the title as the losing finalist of the opening night's World title tournament, by that tournament's own announced rule. Lost it to Ricky Dangerous at 7:56.

reigns.title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
reigns.label: Ricky Dangerous
reigns.how: Pinned Death at 7:56. Lost the belt in a steel cage when Mr. Mercury dived off the top of it onto him at 9:22.

reigns.title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
reigns.label: Mr. Mercury
reigns.how: Won it in the cage rematch the federation's own president had ordered after a disqualification finish. Lost it to Cowboy Kevin Puckett's spinning toehold at 16:41.

reigns.title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
reigns.label: “Cowboy” Kevin Puckett
reigns.how: Made Mr. Mercury submit at 16:41; lost it back to him nine days later in 2:58.

reigns.title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
reigns.label: Mr. Mercury
reigns.how: A second reign, won in 2:58. It ended at the Summit of E-Wrestling of 10-12 July 1991 (its own wing, id `summit-of-e-wrestling`): Report #10 of 18 July opens on “last week's Summit, where we crowned a new North American champion,” and the Aztec Mummy is champion from that issue on. The match itself belongs to the Summit's own scripts, not to this wing, and is not structured here.

reigns.title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
reigns.label: The Aztec Mummy
reigns.how: Won the belt at the Summit of E-Wrestling (its own wing, id `summit-of-e-wrestling`) and defended it in Report #10 against Johnny Vicious; for one week in July he held this title and the All-Jobber belt at the same time, the only wrestler in the federation's record to hold two. Lost it inside the unheld Report #11 to Brewster Cogburn, whom Report #12 introduces with his “brand new North American title.” Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

reigns.title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
reigns.label: Brewster Cogburn
reigns.how: Won inside the unheld Report #11; the change is named in Report #12's own preview. Defended it against the Unknown Masked Wrestler, Jimmy Vendetta and Lightning Bolt, and lost it to Billy Thunder in the last issue that survives. Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

reigns.title: ufws-north-american-heavyweight
reigns.label: Billy Thunder

reigns.title: ufws-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Billy Thunder
reigns.how: Pinned Ford Firepower at 4:29 in his third match. Lost the belt to Running Eagle Feather inside the unheld Report #11: Report #12 of 29 July 1991 says outright that “Billy Thunder will have a chance to regain the World belt that he dropped to Running Eagle Fetaher last week.” Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

reigns.title: ufws-world-heavyweight

Report #11 does not survive. Report #10 of 18 July 1991 and Report #12 of 29 July 1991 bracket the change between them and Report #12 names its outcome outright, so the reign is chained across the gap at month precision rather than left broken.

Recorded here under the header's own credited champion (Disturbed Youth), on two pieces of corroborating evidence inside the same document: the same entry's own "it was Youth's first World Title win" line, and the very next (18th) reign's own text, which has Shane Stud regaining the title specifically from "his Sex and Violence friend and partner Disturbed Youth" — confirming Youth, not Kelly, held it entering that match. reigns.title: united-states-stewart-wf-1999
reigns.label: "Laid Back" Lawrence Christian

won.source: Defeated "Pure Heart" Matt Blazer by referee stoppage after a figure-four leglock, for the vacant championship.

reigns.note: The first champion in the title's history.

won.source: Recorded as the first champion in Bulletin #69; the sheet does not name an opponent. The lineage is unknown after this.

reigns.title: upw-north-american
reigns.label: "Legionarius" Antonio De Luca

won.source: promotions/upw/archive/north-american-title-history.html

reigns.how: Defeated Glenn Chambers in the final of a single-night, eight-man tournament to fill the title, vacant since TTW's own November 2015 closure.
reigns.note: SOURCES DISAGREE ON THE DATE BY FOUR DAYS: the title-history ledger dates this win 14 February 2017, while the served show recording the whole tournament (front-to-back, same night) is dated 18 February 2017 by Past Events' own sequence rather than an in-text date. Both readings are recorded; the reign is linked to the served show as the same event.

reigns.title: upw-television
reigns.label: "El Patron" Felix Sandoval

won.source: promotions/upw/archive/television-title-history.html; matches the show's own content (a ladder match for the vacant title).

reigns.how: Won a ladder match over Brandon Franklin, Chad Allen, Tripp Skylark, Damian Payne, and Harrison Daniels III by retrieving the hanging title belt, filling the title vacant since TTW's own closure.

reigns.title: upw-television
reigns.label: "Hardcore Icon" Brandon Franklin

won.source: promotions/upw/archive/television-title-history.html

reigns.how: Defeated Felix Sandoval at Survival, avenging a controversial time-limit-draw loss to Sandoval on 17 January 2017.
reigns.note: The count reached three as the twenty-minute time limit sounded; the referee consulted the timekeeper and the replay and the ring announcer named Franklin the winner and new champion, per the Survival main card.

reigns.title: upw-television
reigns.label: Windham Brody

won.source: promotions/upw/archive/television-title-history.html; matches the show's own content (Brody's first defense as challenger, with the Dominion interfering).

reigns.how: Defeated Brandon Franklin by pinfall in Franklin's first defense, with Franklin's own Dominion rivals (Tyson Bishop, Lance Donovan, Antonio De Luca) interfering at ringside throughout.

reigns.title: upw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Aaron "All Day" Lewis

won.source: promotions/upw/archive/world-heavyweight-title-history.html; matches the show's own content (a Fatal Four-Way crowning a new champion).

reigns.how: Defeated Dylan Cardinal, Liam Donegal, and Chase Williams in a Fatal Four-Way at UPW's own fifth Showdown to become its first World Heavyweight Champion since TTW's own closure.

reigns.title: upw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Derek Rage

won.source: promotions/upw/archive/world-heavyweight-title-history.html

reigns.how: Defeated Aaron Lewis by pinfall at Survival, UPW's own first pay-per-view.
reigns.note: Rage covered Lewis after a Hammer of God from the top-rope position, per the Survival main card.

reigns.title: upw-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Warriors

won.source: promotions/upw/archive/world-tag-team-title-history.html; matches the show's own content (a best-two-of-three-falls match crowning UPW's first tag champions).

reigns.how: Defeated the Hype two falls to one, Kel Robertson pinning Danny Nash for the deciding fall, on UPW's own debut Showdown to become its first World Tag Team Champions since TTW's own closure.

reigns.title: upw-world-tag-team
reigns.label: Soldiers of the Sun

won.source: promotions/upw/archive/world-tag-team-title-history.html

reigns.how: Defeated the Warriors (champions), the Dominion, and the O'Malley Brothers in a Fatal Four-Way at Survival.
reigns.note: Ricky Courage pinned Anthony O'Malley with a bridging cover after he and Titan Juarez hit the Sunplex, per the Survival main card.

reigns.title: uscw-heavyweight-title
reigns.label: Viper

won.source: Won the Heavyweight Title tournament final over Jacob Yoder at Battle Bowl: May Day '98 after Sinister attacked the count-keeper.

reigns.note: end_how omitted: still champion at the held record's end.

won.source: Pinned a run-in-felled Kid Sharpe at Battle Bowl: May Day '98.

reigns.title: uscw-north-american-title
reigns.label: David Dobouis

won.source: Beat undefeated champion Scott Dakota at Midweek Madness with the Bad Mojo.

reigns.note: end_how omitted: still champion at the held record's end.

won.source: Seagram pinned Dana Czech of Total Destruction at Battle Bowl: May Day '98.
Won the fed's own first Weapons and Cage match at Battle Bowl: May Day '98.

lost.note: Lost the title before Midweek Madness (17 July 1998) to Tony Dylan, whose own reign is not otherwise documented in the held record.

reigns.title: uscw-television-title
reigns.label: Mike Adams

won.source: Submitted Tony Dylan at Midweek Madness.

reigns.note: end_how omitted: still champion at the held record's end.

reigns.title: usew-light-heavyweight
reigns.label: Swashbuckler Jack Hornblower

won.source: Billed as the USeW Light-Heavyweight Champion on the federation's own Last Stand Control Center of 14 May 1995, having kept the belt at the Holiday Rush after a branding-iron attack.

reigns.note: Booked to defend it in a Texas Death Match against the man who attacked him; the card is not held.

reigns.title: usew-light-heavyweight
reigns.label: Doug Carr

won.source: Billed as the current USeW Light Heavyweight Champion on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996.

reigns.note: Retained against “Suicidal” Sean Altman at Leprecharnage in 9:24. Simon Sanders is separately billed on the same card's own aftermath as a former Light Heavyweight Champion — a reign this collection cannot date.

reigns.title: usew-north-american
reigns.label: Comanche War Dog

won.source: Billed on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996, as the former USeW North American Champion, stripped of the title three weeks earlier.

reigns.how: Stripped by the federation, which abolished the championship in the same announcement.

end.source: Leprecharnage's own recap: “Three weeks ago, Comanche War Dog was stripped of the North American Title for a few reasons.”

reigns.title: usew-united-states-heavyweight
reigns.label: the Nightcreeper

won.source: Billed on the federation's own Last Stand Control Center of 14 May 1995 as “the newly-crowned United States Heavyweight Champion.”

reigns.note: The card that would have followed is not held, and no other document of this championship survives.

reigns.title: usew-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: the 600 Pound Gorilla

won.source: Billed as the reigning World Heavyweight Champion on the federation's own Last Stand Control Center of 14 May 1995, which records that he took the belt from Rick O'Malley at the Holiday Rush.

reigns.note: Rick O'Malley is named in the same document as a former World Champion — the reign this one ended. The chain forward from here does not survive: El Maestro is billed on the 8 April 1996 Blow-Out as a former World Heavyweight Champion, and no document holds the changes between May 1995 and March 1996.

reigns.title: usew-world-heavyweight

won.source: Billed as the reigning USeW World Heavyweight Champion on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996; his own reign is described there as already established.

reigns.how: Pinned by “Mr. Machismo” Hank Thompson at Leprecharnage, after Freddy Flame slid a chair into the ring and Thompson powerbombed him onto it.
reigns.note: Won on a card this collection does not hold; no start date survives.

reigns.title: usew-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: “Mr. Machismo” Hank Thompson

won.source: Leprecharnage, served under this wing: “the winner of this contest . . . by pinfall and New USeW Heavyweight Champion . . . 'Mr. Machismo' HANK THOMPSON.”

reigns.how: Pinned by 187 at 17:07 on the Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996, hiptossed out of his own abdominal stretch into a cover.

reigns.title: usew-world-heavyweight

won.source: The Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996, served under this wing: “Your winner and NEW 2 time USeW World Heavyweight Champion........187!”

reigns.note: Still champion on 22 April 1996, the last card of this federation's own that this collection holds.

reigns.title: usew-world-tag-team
reigns.label: the Machismos

won.source: Billed as the current World Tag Team Champions on the federation's own Last Stand Control Center of 14 May 1995, with a title defence against the number one contenders already signed.

reigns.note: The Iconoclasts are named in the same document as former World Tag Champions — an earlier reign this collection cannot date.

reigns.title: usew-world-tag-team
reigns.label: the White Knights

won.source: Billed as the reigning and undefeated USeW World Tag Team Champions on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996.

reigns.note: Retained against the Equalizers at Leprecharnage in 3:36, the shortest World Tag Team title match in this federation's own held record.

reigns.title: usew-world-television
reigns.label: Justice D. Nyde

won.source: Billed as the current USeW World Television Champion on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996.

reigns.how: Pinned by Jack Diamond at 34:44 at Leprecharnage, with the Diamond Senton.
reigns.note: The federation's own account of the four-way match that created this championship names both Haplo and Nyde as its champion in one sentence and then says Haplo retained; that contradiction is recorded on the title's own row and no earlier reign is written from it.

reigns.title: usew-world-television
reigns.label: Jack Diamond

won.source: Leprecharnage: “The winner of this contest . . . and NEW USeW WORLD TELEVISION CHAMPION . . . JACK DIAMOND.”

reigns.how: Pinned by El Maestro at 3:18 on the Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996, with a Northern lights suplex.

reigns.title: usew-world-television
reigns.label: El Maestro

won.source: The Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996: “We have a new Television champion!”

reigns.how: Pinned by Simon Sanders at 5:21 on the Monday Night Blow-Out of 22 April 1996, with the Boogie-Woogie Jam-Slam.

won.source: The Monday Night Blow-Out of 22 April 1996: “the winner of this contest . . . and NEW USeW TELEVISION CHAMPION . . . SILKY SMOOTH SIMON SANDERS.”

reigns.title: usew-world-television-tag-team
reigns.label: BlackJack

won.source: Billed as the USeW World Television Tag Team Champions on Leprecharnage, 17 March 1996, and described there as having held the belts “for a little while now” with several defences already made.

reigns.how: Lost the titles to Doom and Disaster at 29:15 on the Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996.
reigns.note: Kept the belts at Leprecharnage by losing the match: their own manager hit a challenger with a title belt in front of the referee and the team was disqualified.

reigns.title: usew-world-television-tag-team
reigns.label: Doom and Disaster

won.source: The Monday Night Blow-Out of 8 April 1996: “Winners: Doom and Disaster +6 (Blackjack -3).”

reigns.note: Kept the titles on 22 April 1996 the same way the previous champions had: disqualified against La Famiglia at 7:43 after using a belt, and still champions.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
reigns.label: Citizen X

won.source: USPW American Wrestling, Wednesday, Week 2, January 2007 (in-game).

reigns.how: Won from Jim Force with a golf club on the second show of the diary; kept against Force twice, Frankie Perez, Captain USA and Bulldozer Brandon Smith, the last billed as the fifth defense. It ends on the third show of March 2007, when Steve Flash beats him with the Flash Bang.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
reigns.label: Steve Flash

won.source: USPW All American Wrestling, Saturday, Week 3, March 2007 (in-game), billed "NEW USPW National Champion: Steve Flash".

reigns.how: Won from Citizen X with the Flash Bang on the third show of March 2007; kept against Fumihiro Ota, Corporal Doom, William Hayes by disqualification, and Ota and Hayes together in the April shows, and still champion at the end of this range. It ends at the first Family Night, Friday of Week 1, June 2007, when William Hayes beats him in a two out of three falls match.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
reigns.label: William Hayes

won.source: USPW Family Night, Friday, Week 1, June 2007 (in-game), billed "Winner and new Champion: William Hayes".

reigns.how: Won from Steve Flash in a two out of three falls match at the first Family Night, Friday of Week 1, June 2007, with the Slick Trick; kept in June against Art Reed, Freddie Datsun, Muffin and Wanda Fish, and still champion at the end of this range. In July 2007 he keeps it against Jacob Jett on the Monday of Week 3; the same week he wins the fatal four-way for the number one contendership, and he loses the World Championship match to Umaga on the Thursday of Week 4; in August he keeps the belt against Wanda Fish on the Monday of Week 2, and is still champion at the end of this range. In August 2007 he keeps the belt against Bulldozer Brandon Smith on the Monday of Week 3 and against Art Reed at the Family Night of Friday, Week 3; in September he keeps it against Rudy Velasquez on the Monday of Week 1, and he is still champion at the end of this range, with Wanda Fish set to challenge him at Blaze of Glory. It ends at Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007, when Triple D hits Wanda Fish with the belt in the ring and she wins the title by disqualification; Hayes is fired in October 2007.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
reigns.label: Wanda Fish

won.source: USPW Blaze of Glory, Saturday, Week 2, September 2007 (in-game), recapped "Wanda Fish defeated William Hayes by DQ to win the USPW National title".

reigns.how: Won from William Hayes at Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007, after Danny Jillefski changes the rules so that the title can change hands on a disqualification: with Hayes and Fish facing each other in the ring, Triple D takes the belt from the timekeeper, hits Fish in the head with it and drops it on her, and the timekeeper announces her as the new champion; Jacob Jett's offer that she join Divinity and the sneak attacks that follow do not take it from her, and she is still champion at the end of this range, with Jett set to challenge her at A Haunting in America. She keeps the belt against Jacob Jett at A Haunting in America on Saturday of Week 2, October 2007, with the Dish of the Day; she is still champion at the end of this range, with Jett and Art Reed booked into a three-way against her for Pilgrimage. She keeps the belt at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, pinning Art Reed with the Dish of the Day in the three-way with Reed and Jacob Jett, who fight each other; she is still champion at the end of this range. Jillefski books Phlex as her challenger for Winter Epiphany on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 1, December 2007, after she and Phlex become a couple; Giant Oak and The Flash warn her Phlex is using her, and she beats The Flash in 12:54 on the Thursday of Week 3; she is still champion at the end of this range.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-national-championship
reigns.label: Jim Force

won.source: The second show of the diary (Wednesday, Week 2, January 2007) bills Citizen X's win "for the USPW National title"; it does not date Force's win.

reigns.how: Jim Force's reign, which the diary does not date; it surfaces when he loses the belt to Citizen X on the second show of the diary.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-unappreciated-championship
reigns.label: Bulldozer Brandon Smith

won.source: USPW Blaze of Glory, Saturday, Week 2, September 2007 (in-game), billed "USPW Unappreciated Championship Match", "Winner: Bulldozer Brandon Smith in 9:08".

reigns.how: Won in the four-way at Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007: he promises Thomas Morgan his back, drops him with a Backdrop Driver, drops Insane Machine with an Inverted Piledriver and pins Brett Hall; still champion at the end of this range. He draws with Brett Hall by double disqualification on the Monday of Week 3, September 2007, and beats Brendan Idol with a Backdrop Driver on the Monday of Week 1, October; he is still champion at the end of this range, with Hall set to challenge him at A Haunting in America. In October 2007 he keeps the belt against Brendan Idol and Insane Machine on the Monday of Week 2 and against Brett Hall in a street fight at A Haunting in America on Saturday of Week 2; he is still champion at the end of this range, with Idol, who beats Hall by disqualification on the Monday of Week 3, set to challenge him at Pilgrimage. He keeps the belt against Brendan Idol at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, with a Backdrop Driver after Idol's springboard crossbody; he is still champion at the end of this range. He keeps the belt against Mean Jean Cattley on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 3, November 2007 in 7:41 with the Dozer Driver; in December 2007 the Mantis, a masked newcomer, steals the belt from his shoulder in the halls and challenges him for it at Winter Epiphany, and the Mantis's messenger The Trademark is knocked out by his chain-wrapped fist; he is still champion at the end of this range.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-championship
reigns.label: Freddie Datsun

won.source: USPW Stars, Stripes and Slams, "Saturday, Week 4, 2007" (in-game; the show's header omits the month, and it follows Tuesday, Week 4, January 2007, after which the narrator has "a big event to book for this Saturday").

reigns.how: Won from Bruce the Giant at Stars, Stripes and Slams with the Patriot Press; kept against William Hayes in February and against Peter Valentine and Umaga (by disqualification) in March, with a stretcher exit in between. It ends on the third show of March 2007, when Umaga beats him in a steel cage match.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-championship
reigns.label: Umaga

won.source: USPW All American Wrestling, Saturday, Week 3, March 2007 (in-game), billed "New USPW World Champion: Umaga".

reigns.how: Won from Freddie Datsun in a steel cage match on the third show of March 2007 with a Savage Charge; kept against Datsun, Trent Shaffer, Muffin and Datsun again through May, and still champion at the end of this range, with Triple D set to challenge at the first Family Night. On the fourth Saturday of May 2007 he beats Muffin again; in June 2007 he keeps it against Triple D at the first Family Night, Freddie Datsun on the Saturday of Week 2 and Triple D again on the fourth Family Night, and is still champion at the end of the diary's June 2007 posts. In July 2007 he keeps it against William Hayes at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 4; it ends at the Family Night of Friday, Week 1, August 2007, when Darryl Devine beats him in a steel cage match.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-championship
reigns.label: Darryl Devine

won.source: USPW Family Night, Friday, Week 1, August 2007 (in-game), billed "Winner and NEW Champion: Triple D".

reigns.how: Won from Umaga in a steel cage match at the Family Night of Friday, Week 1, August 2007, by dropping from the top of the cage to the floor while Umaga is still on the steel steps; still champion at the end of this range. He keeps it against Bruce the Giant at the Family Night of Friday, Week 2, August 2007, against William Hayes at Summer of Love, against Freddie Datsun at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 1, September and against Jim Force at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 2; he is still champion at the end of this range, with Muffin set to challenge him at Blaze of Glory. At Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007, he beats Muffin in a match the narrator rates an A, after the referee counts her pin and Seduction tells him Devine's foot was on the rope, and Danny Jillefski has the match restarted; on the Monday of Week 4 he leaves her bloodied in a cage match, an angle with no result; he is still champion at the end of this range, set to defend against Sam Strong at A Haunting in America. In October 2007 he beats Frankie Perez on the Monday of Week 2 with the Hotshots' help, beats Bruce the Giant on the Thursday when Seduction counts the pin, and keeps the belt against Sam Strong, back from retirement, at A Haunting in America on Saturday of Week 2 by pulling the tights, then against Davey Wayne on the Monday of Week 3; on the Thursday of Week 3 Freddie Datsun wins the number one contendership and walks off with the belt in a brawl without the title changing hands, and Devine is still champion at the end of this range, set to defend against Datsun at Pilgrimage on 22 November 2007. In November 2007 he keeps the belt against Umaga on the Monday of Week 1, in a match the narrator rates an A*, after Danny Jillefski, Big Cat Brandon and a low blow turn it and while the Masked Man's video threatens Seduction and Muffin, and against Freddie Datsun at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November, when the Masked Man hits Datsun with the Slick Trick and Jillefski, in a referee's shirt, counts the pin; he is still champion at the end of this range. Through the Monday of Week 4, December 2007 no title match is booked: he beats Casey Valentine, Fumihiro Ota, Human Arsenal, Rick Law, Wolf Hawkins and Reaper in non-title and singles matches, learns that the Masked Man is Jack Giedroyc, and the card for Winter Epiphany lists Giedroyc against him for the World Championship; he is still champion at the end of this range.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-championship
reigns.label: Bruce the Giant

won.source: The diary's first show (Wednesday, Week 1, January 2007) has him as champion; it does not date the win; dates are the diary's own in-game dates.

reigns.how: Bruce the Giant's reign as the diary opens; the diary does not say when he won it. He loses the belt to Freddie Datsun at Stars, Stripes and Slams.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Dudez!!!1!

won.source: USPW American Wrestling, Tuesday, Week 3, January 2007 (in-game).

reigns.how: Won from The Towers of Power by Trent Shaffer and Mainstream Hernandez, then lost a week later when Frankie Perez hit Hernandez with a boot.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Canadian Crusties

won.source: USPW American Wrestling, Tuesday, Week 4, January 2007 (in-game).

reigns.how: Won from The Dudez!!!1! after Frankie Perez hit Mainstream Hernandez, then kept against the Lords of War on the first March show. It ends on the third show of March 2007, when The Dudez!!!1! win a three-way match with Maxmillion Productions.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Dudez!!!1!

won.source: USPW All American Wrestling, Saturday, Week 3, March 2007 (in-game), billed "NEW USPW World Tag Team Champions: The Dudez!!!1!!!".

reigns.how: Won in a three-way match with Maxmillion Productions from The Canadian Crusties, who were not showing up for work; kept against The Demons of Rage and Veteran Mentality in April, and still champions at the end of this range, with a defense against the Demons of Rage set for the diary's first Family Night. In June 2007 they keep the belts against The Demons of Rage at the first Family Night, Demon Anger's last match, and against Veteran Mentality at the fourth; after that match Trent Shaffer attacks the champions with a steel chair and carries the belts off, and on the Saturday that follows he wears them and claims to be the champion with a partner he does not name, but the diary records no match and no change of champions. In July 2007 Trent Shaffer's long-promised partner turns out to be Chance Fortune; the pair, billed as the dudes, challenge for the belts: The Dudez!!!1! beat them at the Family Night of Thursday, Week 3 and take the belts back, and beat them again on the Monday of Week 2, August 2007, and they are still champions at the end of this range. It ends at Summer of Love, Saturday of Week 3, August 2007, when Team Seduction beat them and win the belts.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Team Seduction

won.source: USPW Summer of Love!, Saturday, Week 3, August 2007 (in-game), recapped "Team Seduction defeated The Dudez!!!1!!! to win the USPW World Tag Team titles".

reigns.how: Won from The Dudez!!!1! at Summer of Love, Saturday of Week 3, August 2007, when Human Arsenal pins Mainstream Hernandez with an Ammo Dump after Fumihiro Ota's Ninja Strike, with Seduction at ringside; The Dudez!!!1! use their rematch clause, which Seduction turns into a ladder match for Blaze of Glory, and Team Seduction are still champions at the end of this range. They keep the belts against The Dudez!!!1! in a ladder match at Blaze of Glory, Saturday of Week 2, September 2007, when Seduction distracts Frankie Perez and Human Arsenal pulls the belts down; Seduction names Veteran Mentality the #1 contenders on the Monday of Week 4, and Team Seduction are still champions at the end of this range. In October 2007 they beat Veteran Mentality (with Steve Flash on the Thursday of Week 1, with Wanda Fish on the Monday of Week 2) and keep the belts against Veteran Mentality at A Haunting in America, Saturday of Week 2, after attacking the pair before the match; Team Seduction are still champions at the end of this range. They lose the belts to The Valentines at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, when Triple D, shut out of Divinity's plans, hits Human Arsenal with a Divine Dream Drop and lays Peter Valentine across him for the pin.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Valentines

won.source: USPW Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007 (in-game), billed "USPW Tag Team Championship Match- The Valentines vs. Team Seduction (c)" and recapped "The Valentines defeated Team Seduction to win the USPW Tag Team titles".

reigns.how: Won from Team Seduction at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, when Triple D, shut out of Divinity's plans, slides into the ring while Seduction distracts the referee, hits Human Arsenal and then Peter Valentine with Divine Dream Drops and lays Valentine across Arsenal, and the referee counts the pin; Danny Jillefski, who cannot reverse the decision, gives them a match on the spot against Divinity's "newest members", The Hotshots, and they lose the belts to them in 1:56.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Hotshots

won.source: USPW Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007 (in-game), recapped "The Hotshots defeated The Valentines to win the USPW Tag Team titles".

reigns.how: Won from The Valentines minutes after the Valentines won them, at Pilgrimage, Saturday, 22 November 2007, with a Vessey Plex on Casey and a Fisherman's Suplex on Peter, in 1:56, when Danny Jillefski makes the pair Divinity's newest members and Seduction welcomes them; they keep the belts against The Valentines on the Monday of Week 3, with a VesseyPlex II, and are still champions at the end of this range. They keep the belts against Veteran Mentality on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 4, November 2007, when Davey Wayne pins Jim Force with the Fisherman's Suplex in 13:54, and against The Dudez!!!1!!! on the Family Night of Thursday, Week 1, December 2007 by count-out in 20:22 when Force, Oxford and Mr. Snuggleforce chase the Dudez off; the card for Winter Epiphany lists Maxmillion Productions against them; they are still champions at the end of this range.

reigns.title: uspw-65-and-older-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Towers of Power

won.source: USPW American Wrestling, Tuesday, Week 3, January 2007 (in-game), bills the match as "to win the USPW World Tag Team titles"; it does not date the Towers' win.

reigns.how: The Towers of Power's reign, which the diary does not date; it surfaces when they lose the belts to The Dudez!!!1! on the third show.

reigns.title: ustv-swl-1997b
reigns.label: Night

won.source: The fed's own Friday Night Raw (17 October 1997): Night pinned Manhunter with the Nightfall powerbomb.

reigns.note: No later document in this record shows a further change.

reigns.title: ustv-swl-1997b
reigns.label: Gravedigger

won.source: The fed's own King of the Mats pay-per-view (24 May 1998): Gravedigger won the title from Mass Destruction with a low blow and a chokeslam.

reigns.note: No later document in this record shows a further change.

won.source: Already billed champion entering the promotion's earliest surviving card (17 October 1997); no document in this record shows the win itself.

reigns.title: ustv-swl-1997b
reigns.label: "Hardcore" Harley Robinson

won.source: The fed's own Monday Madness broadcast (1 December 1997), where Harley Robinson enters already champion, some time after Night's own reign (won 17 October 1997, already a reign of record on this title).

reigns.note: Retained against Big Rob Styles on Monday Madness with interference from his own corner. Lost the title off-page some time before the fed's own Ring Masters broadcast (22 March 1998), where Kraze (formerly Biggy) is billed champion.

reigns.title: ustv-swl-1997b
reigns.label: Kraze

won.source: The fed's own Ring Masters broadcast (22 March 1998), where Kraze (formerly Biggy) enters already champion.

reigns.note: Lost the title off-page some time before the fed's own King of the Mats pay-per-view (24 May 1998), where Mass Destruction is billed champion.

reigns.title: ustv-swl-1997b

reigns.title: ustv-swl-1997b
reigns.label: Dynamite Dana

reigns.note: The promotion's earliest recorded United States Television Title change, predating this record's own earliest surviving card (17 October 1997), where Manhunter already holds the belt; no document shows how or when the title passed from Dynamite Dana to Manhunter.

reigns.title: uswf-1998-heavyweight
reigns.label: Mark Williams

won.source: The fed's own Championship Triangle Match broadcast: the ring announcer crowns 'Mark Williams' while the referee raises Chris Williams's hand, after Chris performed the deciding pinfall in his brother's stead.

lost.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem): Bill Vaughn pins Mark Williams for the title.

reigns.how: Chris Williams, introduced moments earlier as Mark's identical twin, secretly took his brother's place mid-match and scored the pinfall on Steve Shine; the ring announcer credited Mark Williams regardless.
reigns.note: The broadcast itself never resolves whether Mark or Chris actually wrestled the deciding fall; the record credits the belt to Mark Williams per the in-fiction announcement, with Chris Williams named as the reign's other holder.

reigns.title: uswf-1998-heavyweight
reigns.label: "Critical" Bill Vaughn

won.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem) recap: a mystery masked man interferes on Vaughn's behalf before he pins Mark Williams.

reigns.how: Pinned champion Mark Williams with his own finisher, the Critical Mass, after an unidentified masked interloper attacked Chris Williams at ringside.
reigns.note: Still champion when this record ends; no further USWF Championship documents survive.

reigns.title: uswf-1998-tagteam
reigns.label: Rail Road Express

won.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem): Freight pins Mars for the fed's first Tag Team Championship after a ringside brawl involving a surprise ally, Subway.

reigns.how: Defeated The Gods (Mars and Apollo) with their finisher, the Runaway Train, in the fed's own first Tag Team Championship match; the surprise involvement of a third wrestler, Subway, immediately afterward formed the stable Revolution Zero.
reigns.note: The fed's own first and, per the surviving record, only Tag Team Championship reign; still champions when this record ends.

reigns.title: uswf-1998-television
reigns.label: John McKenzie

won.source: The fed's own TV Title Battle Royal broadcast: McKenzie is the last man standing among the ring's 27 entrants.

lost.source: The same broadcast: moments after being crowned, McKenzie is ambushed by Steve Shine, who had hidden under the ring for the entire match.

reigns.how: Won a 27-man battle royal in his own debut match.
reigns.note: Held the belt for only minutes before Shine's post-match ambush.

reigns.title: uswf-1998-television
reigns.label: "Hollywood" Steve Shine

won.source: The fed's own TV Title Battle Royal broadcast: Shine, who was never eliminated because he hid under the ring, ambushes new champion John McKenzie with his finisher and is declared the winner by the ring announcer.

lost.source: The fed's own first pay-per-view (MAYhem): McKenzie pins Shine to reclaim the title.

reigns.how: Never entered the battle royal proper; hid under the ring for its entire duration, then clotheslined and eliminated newly-crowned champion John McKenzie after the bell.
reigns.note: The announcer's own declaration awarded Shine the title despite his never having been an active, non-eliminated combatant in the battle royal itself.

reigns.how: Pinned champion Steve Shine with his finisher, the Detonation, after Shine's own manager Krystal Powers's interference was turned against him.
