reigns.note: Recorded as a reign of record from the promotion's own billing; no surviving document in the held record states the match in which the titles changed hands from the Sons of Cacophony. Challenged by Erik Grimsson to a Descent Into Hell defense at Gold Rush on 23 July 2005, after he kidnapped and chained up Caliban inside the structure itself. The reign ended when Serge Annis turned on and ended the career of his own tag partner Caliban at an unread Gold Rush, per the promotion's own commentary on UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 18 March 2006.

lost.source: UWF Saturday Night Rampage, 18 March 2006: Serge Annis, appearing without tag partner Caliban and described by ringside commentary as having ended Caliban's own career at an unread Gold Rush, no longer carries the title; the Sons of Cacophony are billed as reigning champions the same night. No surviving document in the held record states how the titles changed hands.

reigns.note: Recorded as a reign of record from the promotion's own billing; no surviving document in the held record states the match in which the Sons of Cacophony regained the titles from the Hands of Death. A second reign for Erik and Chad Grimsson, who first held these titles in 2005.

reigns.title: uwf-television
reigns.label: James von Doom

won.source: The Clash: London Calling card (promotions/uwf/archive/the-clash-2005.html) lists a Television Title Jubilee, Silvio Rochelli (c) against a field that includes James von Doom; the fed's own North American history dates the Clash PPV to 6 March 2005 (promotions/uwf/archive/nahistory.html). The winner is named by his own posts: "Winning the UWF Television Championship on the Clash PPV" (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/your-characters-defining-moment/13052/18); "winning the 13-man Television Championship Jubilee in his UWF debut" (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/tell-us-about-your-character/15449/2); "Beat 13 wrestlers to win the UWF Television Championship in his UWF debut at the Clash" (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/ptc-wrestler-of-the-year-2005-stage-1-enclosed/16156/8).

lost.source: Not dated by any surviving card: Red Rock is champion by 2 Jun 2005 (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/preview-uwfs-sunday-supremacy/14081/1); the FANdamonium DOS voting page of 28 Apr lists the champion only as "TV Champ" (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/uwf-fandamonium-dos-voting-open/13714/1). The export names no holder between this reign and Red Rock's.

lost.source: The Wednesday Night Universal card dated 7 Sep 2005 books "Champion vs. "Career Killer" James Mason" for the title (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/uwf-presents-sas-wnu-cards-feedback-and-predictions/15182/1); Red Rock is "STILL the TV Champ" on the SAS of 4 Sep (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/feedback-uwf-presents-sunday-afternoon-supremacy/15235/1); the Regal Rumble report of 20 Sep says "James Mason defended his newly won UWF TV Championship for the first time" (https://forum.ewmuseum.org/t/feedback-uwf-presents-regal-rumble/15373/1).

reigns.note: Attacked Valenkov, Ric Beauty and Rob Beauty with Lucy after his own earlier tag match, then won the title from Valenkov in the closing battle royal the same night. Retained the title by count-out against Flash on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004) after leaving the ring with the belt rather than answering the referee's count, which eliminated him from the Dog Days tournament; a further challenge from Daniel Sinz on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004) ended with both men walking away from the ring before a decision, the title again not changing hands. Majority owner Kingston Cash declares the championship no longer recognized by the promotion on Wrestle Style V.1 (16 August 2004) and tries to confiscate the belt; Blair refuses and strikes Cash down, keeping the belt in his own possession with no successor named. Still clutching the same belt, Blair loses to a returning Classy Joey Boy by disqualification in the VWF Heavyweight Title tournament's opening round on Wrestle Style V.3 (3 September 2004) after attacking the referee rather than give it up. Eliminated early from a VWF 24 Hour Championship battle royal on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004) after fleeing to the back with the belt; Adam Jennings wins the battle royal and is announced champion by the ring announcer, but Kingston Cash refuses to recognize the change unless Jennings physically takes the belt from Blair. Blair fails to appear for a signed follow-up against Jennings on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004), ruled a no contest; Cash instead sends his own new bodyguard G-Gangsta after Jennings, no bell rung. Blair again fails to appear for a defense against Fast Eddie Cutlass on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), another no contest, and runs in with Lucy to chair Jennings after Jennings beats Gangsta later the same show; Cash books Blair against Jennings in an I Quit match for the title at Vegas Violence. Loses the title to Adam Jennings in an I Quit match at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), knocked into the referee before physically knocking Jennings around while refusing to let go of the belt himself; finally says the words after a powerslam over the top rope with both men still gripping the title, then speared, sedated and stretchered out.

Continues to be billed champion on Dog Days 2 (22 June 2004), scratched from his own three-way match by majority owner Kingston Cash before the bell; returns to competition, without the title on the line, in an eight-man singles scramble on Dog Day Three (1 July 2004). Retains the title in a clean pin over Daniel Sinz on Dog Day Four (9 July 2004). The Heavyweight Championship main event on Wrestle Style V.1 (16 August 2004) ends without a finish when a returning Classy Joey Boy interferes; Kingston Cash announces a random-draw title tournament running each week until Vegas Violence, with the champion defending every time he is drawn and the title changing hands on count-outs and disqualifications during it. Retains cleanly over a returning Billy Bones, a shell of his former self after months in an alcoholic rehabilitation facility, in the tournament's opening round on Wrestle Style V.3 (3 September 2004). Wrestles The Predator Kevin Simmons to a time-limit draw in the tournament's second round on Wrestle Style V.4 (10 September 2004); majority owner Kingston Cash rules the count-out and disqualification stipulation does not cover draws, and both men advance. Retains in a fatal four-way on Wrestle Style V.5 (17 September 2004) over Classy Joey Boy, Sebastian and The Assassin Marcus O'Malley (self-eliminated to save a kidnapped Mark McQueen), pinning Sebastian with the Sammael after Sebastian tricks Classy Joey Boy into a sledgehammer disqualification; the win sets a Vegas Violence main event against tournament runner-up The Equalizer. Signs the contract for that match on Wrestle Style V.6 (29 September 2004), where a video appearance by Jason Storm inserts him into the match as a third man and the champion declares he no longer cares about the title, only about denying The Equalizer. Loses the title to The Equalizer in a three-way also involving Jason Storm at Vegas Violence IV (12 October 2004), pinned after a chair shot from guest referee Flash; Orion's own interference in the match, and a referee dispute between guest referees Classy Joey Boy and Flash, both factor into the finish.

On The Gauntlet 2005 (11 April 2005), Team Brittania defends the titles, billed with a question mark over their own legitimacy, against a returning Henry Fish (billed Scott Starring) and an unidentified stand-in wrestling as the absent Van Wild, winning by pinfall; the team's own hired ring announcer, not the broadcast's regular ring announcer, declares them champions afterward. The same night the previous champions, Mark McQueen and Thunder Valenkov, billed "the unlikely tag team champions," lose their own tag match to Hot Property when Valenkov turns on McQueen; the VWF's incoming ownership still has not ruled on the championship's own disputed status.

reigns.how: Pinfall, a Thunder Bomb, for the title left vacant by Adam Jennings's own suspension, at the end of a mid-year tournament (a Second Chance Battle Royal and four quarterfinals narrowing to a Final Four, then a Vegas Violence final).
reigns.note: Valenkov's second documented VXW 24 Hour Championship win (this broadcast introduces him as 'the three time former 24 Hour Champion,' a claim the held record's documented history does not fully account for). Omega's own manager Richard Masterson secretly conspired with Valenkov's manager Chris Wheeling, saying something to Omega mid-match that left him open to the Thunder Bomb; Valenkov refused Wheeling's demand to attack the beaten Omega afterward. Manager Chris Wheeling wore the belt himself in a mock celebration and continued to lead Valenkov to the ring wearing it through Sin City Fights October 16 and October 24, without a title defense on either broadcast. Still without a defense, Wheeling gave Valenkov a night off from wearing the belt to the ring on Sin City Fights November 18 in order to wrestle a non-title match himself in Valenkov's place, then had Valenkov stand ringside without it again on Sin City Fights November 27. Contested again in a three-way match against Television Champion Cobra and challenger Miles McKinley at New Year's Eve of Destruction 2006, under special rules barring Valenkov from losing the title to McKinley; the match ended without a decision when the referee called for the bell amid a mass brawl, Valenkov still champion.

Lost the title to the O'Malley Brothers on Ghost Town Blues in a Tables Ladders and Chairs match, Anthony O'Malley unhooking the belts while Stevie Knight fell from the other ladder.

won.source: Billed champion by "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999), where he retains in a ladder match against Seth Blitzspear.

lost.source: Loses to Mordecai Winchester at "War!Report 4.1" (13 September 1999) — see note.

reigns.note: The wrestler who lost this match, billed and announced as Jeff Westfall, is unmasked afterward as a stand-in, Freak O' Nature; Westfall's own reign is recorded as ending here on the promotion's own in-story ruling, which did not reverse the title change.

reigns.title: war-1995-national-war-championship
reigns.label: Tommy Walks-With-Thunder

won.source: "War!Zone - Loud & Proud" (24 Aug 1997): Tommy Walks-With-Thunder is counted in after the Southern Man (unminted this pass), the pre-designated champion, is counted out attacking him at ringside, becoming the first-ever National WAR! Champion.

reigns.how: Won the title's inaugural match by countout.
reigns.note: The title itself is created for the fed's own August 1997 relaunch in Manhattan under new ownership (see the digest's own Old War!/New War! ruling); its first two challengers were the finalists of a 14-man battle royale on "War!Zone - All But One". Loses the title to Nomad on "War!Zone - OverKill" (8 Sep 1997).

reigns.title: war-1995-national-war-championship
reigns.label: Nomad

won.source: "War!Zone - OverKill" (8 Sep 1997): Nomad pins Tommy Walks-With-Thunder with a Caravan Suplex after stablemate Juggernaut (unminted this pass) attacks Thunder's injured brother at ringside as a distraction, becoming the second National WAR! Champion.

reigns.how: Won by pinfall with stablemate interference.
reigns.note: Retains against Tommy Walks-With-Thunder by disqualification-style stoppage (Juggernaut interferes again, unmasking is threatened but not completed) on "War!Zone - Bloody Allies"; also billed defending against Kevin Slater on "THIS IS WAR!"

reigns.title: war-1995-national-war-championship
reigns.label: Jerry "Goon" Gordon

won.source: Billed the reigning Manhattan Champion (the title's own on-air new name; 3-2-1) in the promotion's own 14 March 1999 rankings bulletin; no originating title-change or rename document survives in the held record.

reigns.how: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing; the title-winning match itself is not attested.
reigns.note: Retains against "The American" Butch Williams by pinfall on "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999); still champion at the close of the held record's 1999 pull. The title is carried on the same record as the National WAR! Championship (war-1995-national-war-championship), on-air renamed the Manhattan Championship per the promotion's own 5 November 1999 Players Guide.

reigns.title: war-1995-original-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: XL-9 & "Trailboss" Mike Dallas

won.source: "WarZone 1" (5 May 1995): wins a "Partners of War" tag tournament, WAR!'s own first-ever championship.

reigns.how: Won the fed's own debut tag tournament.
reigns.note: Declared defunct by General Andropov eleven days later on "WAR!REPORT 3" (16 May 1995) after Trailboss Mike Dallas beat XL-9 for it outright in what had been billed a tag defense; Andropov awarded Trailboss the newly-created singles Freedom Championship instead rather than resolve the ownership. Never contested again.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: CrocMaster

won.source: No title-change document survives; already champion by "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (6 May 1996). Big Duke's own ringside words there ("I held that crappy WAR!Lord belt for long enough") place an earlier Duke reign before this one, off-page.

reigns.how: Title change not recovered in the held record.
reigns.note: Retains against Big Duke in a bloody no-DQ, no-countout rematch on "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (6 May 1996). No document in the held record records the loss of the title; American Patriot holds it by Dec 1996.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: Lord Byron

won.source: "Casualties of War III" (24 May 1996): pins CrocMaster at 13:13 in a loser-leaves-town match; CrocMaster departs WAR!, and Byron becomes "the third War!Lord since its inception."

reigns.how: Won a loser-leaves-town match by pinfall.
reigns.note: CrocMaster's own departure is independently corroborated ("WAR!REPORT — The Story So Far," 3 Jun 1996, lists him among "recent departures"). Byron's own WarLord reign becomes vacant at an unrecovered date between 11-23 Jun 1996: he is a double titleholder (WarLord + International) as of 11 Jun 1996 but the WarLord belt is billed vacant on "WAR! IN WINNIPEG `96" (23 Jun 1996).

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: Robski

won.source: Not itself narrated as a full match in the held record: referenced only in EXTINCTION `96's own opening-credits montage ("Robski winning the Battle Royale", 28 Jun 1996) and confirmed as Robski's own first televised WarLord defense the same card (vs. Jerry "Goon" Gordon).

reigns.how: Won a 20-man battle royale for the vacant title (off-page).
reigns.note: Robski's own first reign; distinct from his later "regained" reign. Retains repeatedly through Oct 1996 (countout/DQ losses do not cost the WarLord title per the fed's own stated rule that it changes hands only on pinfall or submission). Loses the title via a loser-leaves-town stipulation match against Big Duke, by DQ, c.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: American Patriot

won.source: Acts of War! — The Brawl Before the Brawl (27 Nov 1996): the vacant title awarded on air after the previous holder's retirement — served on this wing

reigns.how: Title change not recovered in the held record.
reigns.note: Loses the title in a cage match to Robski, reinstated to the roster on a contract technicality after a dispute with Big Duke.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: Robski

won.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996): "Robski has just superplexed American Patriot... IT IS OFFICIAL! ROBSKI HAS REGAINED THE [title]."

reigns.how: Won a cage match against American Patriot.
reigns.note: The broadcast's own word "regained" implies an earlier Robski reign not otherwise documented in the held record.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: American Patriot

won.source: No title-change document recovered: the holder is last seen champion-less on 7 Dec 1996 and is billed the reigning WarLord champion by MEGAWAR 2 (28 Jan 1997, collected), so the reign began between those dates; lanes L60, L64 and L71 swept Nov 1996–Apr 1997 without finding the card

reigns.how: Already champion; the win back from Robski (war-1995-warlord-r003) is not recovered.
reigns.note: Loses the WarLord Championship to T.J. Independently billed "the former WAR!Lord Champion" entering "SKIRMISH REPORT!" (24 Feb 1997, collected, not served) thirteen days later.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: T.J. "Thunder" Decan

won.source: WAR!ZONE, Boston (11 Feb 1997), the card's own result: Decan pins the reigning WarLord champion after manager interference, 'the second title change of the evening' — served on this wing

reigns.how: Already champion; originating win from Robski not recovered.
reigns.note: Loses the title off-page after "hitting the bottle," per in-character dialogue on "War!Zone - Death of Innocence": "Decan hit the bottle and he lost the War!Lord title." No title-match text is recovered for either the win or this loss; "Jamaican Superstar" Arron Iron is billed the new WarLord Champion hours later on the same broadcast.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: "Jamaican Superstar" Arron Iron

won.source: Billed "current War!Lord" within hours of T.J. Decan's own forfeiture, on the same "War!Zone - Death of Innocence" broadcast (22 Apr 1997, served); no title-match text is recovered.

reigns.how: Became champion off-page after Decan's forfeiture; no match recovered.
reigns.note: Loses the WarLord Championship to Nomad by submission on "War!Zone" (5 May 1997, already served) — see the existing reign war-1995-warlord-r004.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: Nomad

won.source: "War!Zone" (5 May 1997, Madrid): Nomad submits "Jamaican Superstar" Arron Iron (unminted this pass) with a sleeperhold to win the WarLord Championship.

reigns.how: Won by submission.
reigns.note: Retains against T.J. "Thunder" Decan by disqualification on "War!Zone - Renegade Warriors". The title is vacant by the time of the Helmroy Cup tournament at "Extinction '97 - The Oblivion" (13 Jun 1997) -- no document in the held record records how or when Nomad lost or relinquished it; flagged as an open gap.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: Survival

won.source: "Extinction '97 - The Oblivion" (13 Jun 1997): Survival wins the eight-man Helmroy Cup tournament, pinning Ryan "The Intrepid" Howard (unminted this pass) in the final, to claim the vacant WarLord Championship.

reigns.how: Won a tournament final by pinfall.
reigns.note: continuity alongside the National WAR! and unified World WAR!

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: Frank Addams

won.source: "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999): pins Arron Iron in a cage match to win the War!Lord Championship.

reigns.how: Won a cage match by pinfall.
reigns.note: Stripped of the title minutes later, the same show, by President 'Lucky' Jim Howard, who announces a failed steroid test taken earlier in 1999; the vacated title is awarded that same night at the Brooklyn Brawl.

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: "Heavy Weapons" Max Doom

won.source: "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999): wins the vacated War!Lord Championship in the Brooklyn Brawl, an over-the-top-rope battle royal also carrying a $1,000,000 prize, eliminating Ronnie Severn and Dr. Melancholy last.

reigns.how: Won a battle royal for the vacated title.
reigns.note: Still champion at the close of the held record's 1999 pull.

lost.source: No surviving document records how the title passed from Max Doom to Ronny Ramirez; Ramirez is the billed champion by "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999).

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: Arron Iron

won.source: Billed the reigning War!Lord Champion (17-8-2) in the promotion's own 14 March 1999 rankings bulletin; no originating title-change document survives in the held record.

reigns.how: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing; the title-winning match itself is not attested.
reigns.note: Loses the title to Frank Addams by pinfall in a cage match on "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999).

reigns.title: war-1995-warlord-championship
reigns.label: Ronny Ramirez

won.source: Billed champion by "Extinction '99" (22 June 1999), where he retains in a steel cage match against "Heavy Weapons" Max Doom; the win itself is not attested by any document this collection holds.

lost.source: Fights Butch Williams to a double count-out at "War!Report 4.2" (21 September 1999) under a loser-leaves-WAR! stipulation; both men are suspended six months and the title is declared vacant.

reigns.note: Recorded as champion from billing; the promotion's own record does not show how the title passed from Max Doom. No further document in the held record names a new champion.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Brotherhood

won.source: WARATHON I (26 Apr 1996), the show's own result — served on this wing

reigns.how: Won via a surprise contractual title match sprung on the Ghetto Boyz immediately after the latter unified the tag belts.
reigns.note: Retains against the Ghetto Boyz by double disqualification in a "loser leaves town" match on "Tuesday Night WAR!fare" (6 May 1996). No document in the held record records the loss of the title; the Star Smashers hold it a week later.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Star Smashers

won.source: Superstars At War VII — The Dark Legacy (6 May 1996), the card's own review: the challengers submit a Brotherhood member — served on this wing

reigns.how: Title change not recovered in the held record.
reigns.note: Lose the World WAR! Tag Team titles to the Aderondac Brothers on "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996).

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Aderondac Brothers

won.source: "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996): "WE HAVE NEW TAG TEAM CHAMPIONS! THE ADERONDAC BROTHERS WIN THE BELTS!"

reigns.how: Won by pinfall over the Star Smashers.
reigns.note: No document in the held record records the loss of the title; Industrial Revolution holds it by Dec 1996.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Lost Boys

won.source: "Casualties of War III" (24 May 1996), a Street Fight: Lost Boy 2 pins Bombsquad (an Aderondac Brother) after a crowbar shot.

reigns.how: Won a Street Fight by pinfall.
reigns.note: Ends the existing Aderondac Brothers reign. Lost Boys's own first tag reign.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Theatre of Pain

won.source: "Superstars At War XI / Countdown to Extinction `96 Stage 2" (21 Jun 1996): Conquer pins Lost Boy 1 with a second moonsault after an initial false finish (the wrong Lost Boy was the legal man).

reigns.how: Won by pinfall.
reigns.note: Also billed "Total Destruction" on the era's arena-card results (e.g. "WAR! IN WINNIPEG `96", 23 Jun 1996, retaining by DQ). Loses the title back to the Lost Boys at an unrecovered date.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Lost Boys

won.source: No title-change document survives; Theatre of Pain (as "Total Destruction") are still champions as late as 23 Jun 1996, and the Lost Boys are confirmed champions again by 11 Oct 1996 ("WAR!Time", retaining by double count-out against The Agonizers).

reigns.how: Title change not recovered in the held record.
reigns.note: Lost Boys's own second tag reign. Retains through 22 Oct 1996 (Wendy Addams's own interference against Industrial Revolution).

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Industrial Revolution

won.source: Arena Card (29 Oct 1996): the tag titles change hands after a powerbomb — served on this wing

reigns.how: Title change not recovered in the held record.
reigns.note: Loses the World WAR! Tag Team titles to the Annihilators on "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996).

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Annihilators

won.source: "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996): Venom moonsaults Mega Daddy Kewl off the roof of a parked van in the WARena parking lot for the pin, a falls-count-anywhere match.

reigns.how: Won a falls-count-anywhere match against Industrial Revolution.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Lost Boys

won.source: "MEGAWAR 2 — Championship Tuesday" (masthead-dated 28 Jan 1997, collected/served as war-megawar-2-1997-01-28.html): Frank executes a top rope powerbomb on Shinjiro Kanemoto for the pin, winning the World WAR! Tag Team titles.

reigns.how: Won by pinfall, ending the Annihilators' own reign (war-1995-worldtag-r005). The Lost Boys' own third World WAR! Tag Team reign, following war-1995-worldtag-r006 (1996-05-24) and war-1995-worldtag-r008 (1996-08).
reigns.note: This reign's own end is not recovered.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Tyler Stevens & Ricky Deathwish

won.source: "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999): pin Sid Starr and Nomad after guest referee Jeff Westfall, a friend of Deathwish's, counts a fast pinfall following a chair shot the champions did not see coming.

reigns.how: Won by pinfall, aided by a corrupted guest referee.
reigns.note: Still champions at the close of the held record's 1999 pull.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Sid Starr & Nomad

won.source: Recapped on the promotion's own broadcast ("War!Zone: Beyond Hell," 31 March 1999) as having won the titles from Tyler Stevens and Ricky Deathwish's own prior partners "by using their professionalism"; no originating document survives in the held record.

reigns.how: Recorded from the promotion's own on-air recap; the title-winning match itself is not attested.
reigns.note: Loses the titles to Tyler Stevens and Ricky Deathwish on "War!Zone: Beyond Hell" (31 March 1999) after guest referee Jeff Westfall (a wrestler from another held promotion, officiating only) counts a fast, illegal pinfall favoring the challengers.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Seth Blitzspear

won.source: "A Week at WAR!" (28 May 1995), recapping the NuclearWar 1 supercard: Blitzspear wins the "BattleBlitz 1" gauntlet, then pins Trailboss Mike Dallas (the "BattleBlitz 2" winner) at 5:45 to claim the vacant World Championship.

reigns.how: Won the vacant title by winning a BattleBlitz gauntlet tournament, then defeating the other bracket's own winner.
reigns.note: Retains against Trailboss Mike Dallas in a double-disqualification finish on "WAR!REPORT 5" (29 May 1995). No document in the held record records how or when the title passed to Brewster Cogburn (unminted), who was already holding it when Randy Blake defeated him at "Casualties of WAR!" per the existing reign record's own citation.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Brutus "Sidewinder" Noir

won.source: "WarZone 2" (Season 1, 12 May 1995): wins a 16-man "Champion of War" tournament final over Inner City Firmer with the Marseilles Strangler submission at 17:55 -- WAR!'s first-ever singles champion.

reigns.how: Won a no-rules, no-time-limit tournament final over Inner City Firmer.
reigns.note: Retains against Seth Blitzspear on "WAR!REPORT 3" (16 May 1995) despite the bout itself falling to Blitzspear on a disqualification.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Inner City Firmer

won.source: "WarZone 3" (Season 1, 19 May 1995), part 2: wins a 2-out-of-3-falls, falls-count-anywhere match over Brutus Noir, pinning him after both men fall from a 30-foot arena balcony, at 45:02.

reigns.how: Won 2 falls to 1 in a falls-count-anywhere match.
reigns.note: Stripped of the title after being hospitalized (alongside Noir) in a real-injury angle following the same show, per the news recap in "A Week at WAR!" (28 May 1995): "ICF stripped of belt...champion to be decided at Nuclear War 1."

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: "The Economist" Randy Blake

won.source: Masters of War! 1 (12 Oct 1995), the show's own result — served on this wing

reigns.how: Won at "Casualties of WAR!" (not in the held record) by defeating Brewster Cogburn.
reigns.note: Confirmed still champion, resting from action, on "Masters of War 3" (22 Oct 1995): "There is no world war title match, quite simply because there were no good enough contenders, so Randy Blake gets a break." No document in the held record records the loss of the title to J.R. Death.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Brutus "Sidewinder" Noir

won.source: "WarZone 5 — The Bonfire Bash" (8 Nov 1995): pins Randy Blake with the Marseille Strangler after Ms. Paula's own interference is headbutted away.

reigns.how: Won by pinfall, explicitly billed the first wrestler ever to win the title three times.
reigns.note: Slots between the existing Randy Blake reign and the existing J.R. Death reign.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: "The Reverend" J.R. Death

won.source: Casualties of War 2 (23 Nov 1995), the show's own result — served on this wing

reigns.how: Title change not recovered in the held record.
reigns.note: Retains against Seth Blitzspear on "World WAR! III" (5 Feb 1996) after Vice-President Helmroy bars anyone from ringside. Lost the title to Stein "Ice" Berg at an unrecovered date before Apr 1996.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Stein "Ice" Berg

won.source: WarZone 3 (4 Mar 1996) reports the title awarded after the champion's suspension — served on this wing

reigns.how: Title change not recovered in the held record.
reigns.note: Lost the title to Tonnage at WARATHON 1 (a show not itself in the held record, recapped on "The WAR! Report"): "it was Tonnage who came out on top as he managed to execute the Gigaton Crush on the champion and get the three count."

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Tonnage

won.source: WARATHON I (26 Apr 1996), the show's own result — served on this wing

reigns.how: Won the title from Stein "Ice" Berg at WARATHON 1.
reigns.note: Retains against American Patriot in the main event of "Monday Night WAR!fare" (13 May 1996). By the Tournament of Champions round read here (30 Oct 1996) Tonnage is again pursuing the title rather than holding it — an off-page loss this pull does not otherwise document.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Seth Blitzspear

won.source: "Superstars At War X / Countdown to Extinction `96 Phase 2" (11 Jun 1996): pins Tonnage with a belly-to-back suplex after Brutus Noir's own on-screen attack on Tonnage's wife distracts the champion; Seth's own fourth World title.

reigns.how: Won by pinfall after an on-screen distraction of the champion.
reigns.note: Ends the existing Tonnage reign. Seth's own reign ends when he voluntarily relinquishes the title "over the summer of 96" (per "WAR! Player's Guide V1.2", 29 Oct 1996, and independently corroborated by "Tournament of Champions Semi-Final", 4 Nov 1996: "Decan was upset over Blitzspear's decision to relinquish the title"); the exact date of the relinquishment itself is not recovered. The title is confirmed vacant in-story on "WAR!Time" (11 Oct 1996).

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Jason Midnight

won.source: Domestic path: the previous champion relinquished the title in mid-1996, a Tournament of Champions final at War!Mongers crowned a new champion, Tonnage regained it on WAR!Time (13 Nov 1996), and Midnight followed — the exact transition is unrecovered; the earlier 'UWC interfed tournament' wording described a separate title Midnight held at the same time, per his own on-air words (War!Zone, 22 Apr 1997, collected)

reigns.how: Crowned via a separate interfed (UWC) tournament victory; the originating document is not in the held record.
reigns.note: Retains in a no-DQ, no-countout match against Tyler Stevens on "Nuclear WAR!fare" (7 Dec 1996), the last show read.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: T.J. "Thunder" Decan

won.source: Not itself recovered in the held record: won at "War!Mongers", beating Tonnage in the final of an in-house "Tournament of Champions" held to fill the vacancy; cited retrospectively on "WAR!Time" (13 Nov 1996, "a rematch of the War!Mongers match-up that saw Decan win the title for the first time") and in "A Week in War!" (18 Nov 1996, "Tonnage, who had lost the Tournament of Champions final to 'Thunder' Decan").

reigns.how: Won the vacant title by winning an in-house tournament final.
reigns.note: Decan's only WAR! World title reign; loses it on his first defense, the same night it is cited.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Tonnage

won.source: "WAR!Time" (13 Nov 1996): pins T.J. "Thunder" Decan with a vertical splash on Decan's first title defense, "for the second time, he has become the World War Champion."

reigns.how: Won by pinfall on the champion's first defense.
reigns.note: Tonnage's own second World title reign. Loses the title to Jason Midnight at an unrecovered date between 13 Nov and c.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: "Magnum" Biff McGriff

won.source: The champion's own on-air account (War!Zone, 1 Apr 1997, served) and the fed's retrospective house history; see reign war-1995-world-r009b

reigns.how: Won the World WAR! Championship from Bane, the same evening Bane took it from Lord Byron, at Casualties of War IV (circa mid-March 1997) — the card itself is unrecovered; the champion's own on-air account (1 Apr 1997) and the fed's house history corroborate it
reigns.note: Retains by double count-out in a triangle match against Lord Byron and Bane on "War!Zone - Death of Innocence" and again by double count-out against "Dirty" Doug Simpkins on "War!Zone - Wrath of the Bitter Damned" (29 Apr 1997, already served). Loses the title to Simpkins in a steel cage match on "War!Zone" (5 May 1997, already served) — Simpkins throws salt in his eyes and escapes the cage first.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Lord Byron

won.source: MEGAWAR 2 — Championship Tuesday (28 Jan 1997), the card's own result: Byron pins the reigning champion — served on this wing

reigns.how: Won the World WAR! Championship by pinfall at MEGAWAR 2 (28 Jan 1997)
reigns.note: Retains in a double count-out against Seth Blitzspear on the same 18 Feb 1997 card, and again in a 30-minute time-limit draw against "Dirty" Doug Simpkins on "WAR!!ZONE". Loses the title to "Magnum" Biff McGriff at an unrecovered date between 26 Feb and 9 Apr 1997 — no title-match text survives in either record; McGriff is already billed champion by "WAR!STARS 3" (9 Apr 1997, collected) and Byron himself appears only as a challenger, alongside Bane, in a triangle match against McGriff on "War!Zone - Death of Innocence". Byron loses the title not to McGriff directly but to Bane at Casualties of War IV, circa mid-March 1997; Bane loses it to McGriff the same evening — per the champion's own on-air account (1 Apr 1997) and the fed's retrospective house history.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Bane

won.source: The wing's own retrospective "War: Wrestling Federation Players Guide" (11 Aug 1997, collected -- outside this lane's own primary reading window but consulted to resolve this transition): "At Casualties of War IV, Lord Byron lost the World Title to Bane and then Bane to McGriff all in the same evening." Lord Byron's own on-air words on "[WAR!] Countdown to Extinction '97" (1 Apr 1997, served) independently corroborate a recent, hospitalizing loss of the World Title "following the loss to Bane" at "Casualties of WAR!," described as roughly two weeks before that broadcast -- bracketing the card to circa mid-March 1997. Neither corpus read by this or any prior lane carries "Casualties of War IV" itself; the month given is a retrospective approximation.

reigns.how: Won the World WAR! Championship from Lord Byron at "Casualties of War IV"; no primary-document text of the match itself is recovered.
reigns.note: Lost the title back the SAME EVENING to "Magnum" Biff McGriff, per the same retrospective source -- likely the shortest reign on this wing.

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: "Dirty" Doug Simpkins

won.source: "War!Zone" (5 May 1997, already served): Doug Simpkins throws salt in "Magnum" Biff McGriff's eyes and escapes a steel cage first to become the new World WAR! Champion.

reigns.how: Won a steel cage match by escaping first after throwing salt in the champion's eyes.
reigns.note: Not the same reign as Simpkins's own earlier Liberty Championship run. Retains across the reading window, billed "Old War! World Champion" by the fed's own August 1997 ownership-change storyline, before losing a title-unification match to the Southern Man (billed "New War!" World Champion) by countout after a masked man's interference on "THIS IS WAR!" (7 Oct 1997, already served).

reigns.title: war-1995-world-war-championship
reigns.label: Southern Man

won.source: "THIS IS WAR!" (7 Oct 1997, already served): billed the "New War!" World Champion, Southern Man defeats "Dirty" Doug Simpkins (billed "Old War! World Champion") by countout, after a masked man's interference, to become the Undisputed World WAR! Champion.

reigns.how: Won a title-unification match by countout after a masked man's interference.
reigns.note: Already billed "New War!" World Champion prior to this match, from an unrecovered parallel title lineage tied to the fed's own August 1997 ownership change (see the wing's own Old War!/New War! ruling). Stripped four days later after suffering an in-ring injury during a 30-man Royal Rumble on "WAR!Zone - AfterMath"; doctors advise the injury will keep him out for at least a month. won.source: Reigning champions entering Kaged II.

lost.source: Retained in a Four-Way Dance at Kaged II against the Hart-Breakers, the Mega-Powers and the Extreme Team; the note records the retention rather than a new reign.

reigns.note: This row records the confirmed retention at Kaged II; the reign's own start date is not established in the held record.

won.source: Champion entering Kaged II (31 August 1997).

lost.source: Lost to Shaolin Dynamite at Kaged II.

won.source: Champion entering March Madness, retaining against the Destroyer, 31 March 1997.

lost.source: Lost to the Crow at an unrecorded point between March Madness and Kaged II; the change itself is not in the held record.

won.source: Regained the title from the Crow in a Final Vengeance casket match at Kaged II, 31 August 1997.

lost.source: The 14 September broadcast still bills a match "for the WCWF Intercontinental Championship" involving the Undertaker; whether this is a title defense or a fresh challenge is not resolved by this pass's reading.

won.source: Champion entering Warzone III (23 February 1997), where he retains against Colonel Savard.

lost.source: Champion by the Giant as of 14 September 1997; the corpus shows Vader challenging for the title at Kaged II (31 August) but this pass's reading did not confirm that match's own result, so the exact change is an honest gap.

won.source: Confirmed champion, main-eventing against the Undertaker on the 14 September 1997 broadcast.

lost.source: No further change recorded in the held record.

reigns.title: wcwf-world-class-2000-cruiserweight

won.source: Already billed Cruiserweight Champion at the start of the promotion's own held run (Saturday Storm, 6 Jan 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

lost.source: Shawn is already billed 'current holder of the Cruiserweight title' by Meltdown (31 Jan 2001); no title-losing document survives in the surviving record.

reigns.how: Retained the title by submission over Psycho at Saturday Storm; how it passed to Shawn afterward is not narrated in the promotion's own surviving documents.
reigns.note: A missing-shows gap between Saturday Storm and Meltdown.

reigns.title: wcwf-world-class-2000-cruiserweight
reigns.label: Shawn

won.source: Already billed 'current holder of the Cruiserweight title' at Meltdown (31 Jan 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

reigns.how: Not narrated; the belt passed to Shawn off the held record between Saturday Storm and Meltdown.
reigns.note: Billed the Cruiserweight Champion at Meltdown and Wednesday Evening Confessions, and once, at Total Anarchy 2001, billed instead 'the current WCWF lightweight champion' -- almost certainly the same belt named inconsistently by the promotion's own broadcast rather than a second title, but recorded here as the documents state it rather than silently corrected. Still champion at the close of the promotion's own surviving documents.
