reigns.title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
reigns.label: The Crusher

won.source: The report's own intro: "The Crusher, managed by their arch-enemy Simon Bolendorf, took the Africa/Australia Belt."

reigns.how: Took the Africa/Australia Championship in turn 6, per the report's own intro; the specific title-deciding bout within the Continental Titles match block is not disambiguated by the report's own text.
reigns.note: The General is the Africa/Australia Champion in Report #8's own ranking table of 17 February 1991, where the report also credits him with a successful defense. The change falls inside the unheld Report #7; a gap, not a claim.

reigns.title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
reigns.label: The General

won.source: Not directly attested: the General is the Africa/Australia Champion in Report #8's own ranking table (17 February 1991), where the report also credits him with a successful defense. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost the belt to Mr. Roddy in the same turn in which he won the World Championship.
reigns.note: Won inside the unheld Report #7. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
reigns.label: Mr. Roddy

won.source: Report #9's own headline: “The General lost his Africa/Australia belt to Mr. Roddy.”

reigns.how: Lost to Tom “the Animal” Brown after outside interference by the Mexican Bandit.

reigns.title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
reigns.label: Tom “the Animal” Brown

won.source: Report #11's own headline: “Tom ‘the Animal’ Brown takes Africa/Australia Belt!”

reigns.how: Lost to DiMadMan.
reigns.note: The report credits the win to “outside interference by the Mexican Bandit”, and its own comments have Mr. Roddy working out that the Bandit’s initials are Mr. B’s.

reigns.title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
reigns.label: DiMadMan

won.source: Report #12's own ranking table: “Africa/Australia Champion: DiMadMan (9-0-1).”

reigns.how: Beat Tom “the Animal” Brown.
reigns.note: WindWarrior is champion by Report #15 (7 April 1991). A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
reigns.label: WindWarrior

won.source: Not directly attested: Report #15's own headline has him taking it — “One of their members, WindWarrior, took the Africa/Australia Championship this week” — in the same issue whose ranking table first carries him. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to DiMadMan.

reigns.title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
reigns.label: DiMadMan (second reign)

won.source: Report #16's own headline: “DiMadMan, after losing the Tag Team belts, came back to regain the Africa/Australia Championship!”

reigns.how: Vacated on winning the World Championship; a tournament was announced to fill it.

reigns.title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
reigns.label: Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel”

won.source: Report #20's own headline: “Bjorn ‘the Sweedish Pretzel’ Wins Tournament!”

reigns.how: Won the tournament for the vacant belt across three nights inside one turn — Virus on the Wednesday, Mr. Roddy on the Thursday, Frank Steel in Friday’s final.
reigns.note: The championship does not appear again: the Summer League that began a fortnight later ran three belts only.

reigns.title: wewf-americas-championship
reigns.label: The Feral Frog

won.source: The report's own intro: "The Leaping Lords were also successful this turn, taking two Continental Titles."

reigns.how: Took the Americas Championship in turn 6, per the report's own intro; the specific title-deciding bout within the Continental Titles match block is not disambiguated by the report's own text.
reigns.note: Photon Torpedo is the Americas Champion in Report #8's own ranking table of 17 February 1991, and Admiral Chekov's own line in Report #9 dates the change — “Photon Torpedo DID become the first wrestler in WeWF history to win a Continental title while ranked DEAD LAST in the ratings!” The change itself falls inside the unheld Report #7; a gap, not a claim.

reigns.title: wewf-americas-championship
reigns.label: Photon Torpedo

won.source: Not directly attested: Photon Torpedo is the Americas Champion in Report #8's own ranking table (17 February 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to Frank Steel.
reigns.note: Won inside the unheld Report #7. Admiral Chekov’s own line in Report #9 dates it: “Photon Torpedo DID become the first wrestler in WeWF history to win a Continental title while ranked DEAD LAST in the ratings!”

reigns.title: wewf-americas-championship
reigns.label: Frank Steel

won.source: Report #9's own ranking table: “Americas Champion: Frank Steel.”

reigns.how: Vacated: on winning the World Championship he held three belts at once, and the report declared the Americas Championship vacant with a tournament to fill it.

reigns.title: wewf-americas-championship
reigns.label: FireLord

won.source: Report #12's own headline: “FireLord wins Americas' Title!”

reigns.how: Won the eight-man tournament for the vacant belt — Incision in the first round, Mr. Roddy in the second, Juggernaut in the final.
reigns.note: The Re-Animator is champion by Report #15 (7 April 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Reports #13 and #14. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-americas-championship
reigns.label: The Re-Animator

won.source: Not directly attested: the Re-Animator is the Americas Champion in Report #15's own ranking table (7 April 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to the Big Kahuna in his second defense of that week.
reigns.note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-americas-championship
reigns.label: The Big Kahuna

won.source: Report #20's own headline: “The Big Kahuna Wins Americas' Title!”

reigns.how: Lost to the Re-Animator in a no-disqualification, no-time-limit main event, submitting to a Boston crab.

reigns.title: wewf-americas-championship
reigns.label: The Re-Animator (second reign)

won.source: Supercard #4's own ring announcement: “Here is your winner, and NEW Americas' Champion, the Re-Animator!”

reigns.how: Submitted the Big Kahuna to a Boston crab in the Supercard main event.
reigns.note: The championship does not appear again: the Summer League that began a fortnight later ran a World, a United States and a Tag Team Championship only. Whether it was retired or simply not defended is not stated anywhere in the surviving record.

reigns.title: wewf-battle-royal
reigns.label: RnR

won.source: the wing's own Supercard #4 of 29 May 1991, which introduces Mr. Roddy as “one half of the winning team in the Tag Team Battle Royal” (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-supercard-4-1991-05-29.html)

reigns.how: Won the sixteen-team Tag Team Battle Royal, and were attacked by the Four Corners the moment the match ended — the run-in that turned the 007 Special against them.

reigns.title: wewf-battle-royal
reigns.label: The Unknown Masked Wrestler

won.source: the wing's own Report #9 of 24 February 1991 (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-report-9-1991-02-24.html)

reigns.how: Won the league's first battle royal and took $100,000 from Mr. Fujikuchi's Akira Foundation; refused to give the interviewer his name, and shoved her when she reached for the mask.

reigns.title: wewf-battle-royal
reigns.label: Bjorn "The Sweedish Pretzel"

won.source: the wing's own Report #17 of 21 April 1991 (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-report-17-1991-04-21.html)

reigns.how: Won the Team Challenge Series battle royal, eliminating both of Flint and Steel at the end — “although he had some help.”

reigns.title: wewf-eurasia-championship
reigns.label: The Lethal Lemming

won.source: The report's own intro: "The Leaping Lords were also successful this turn, taking two Continental Titles."

reigns.how: Took the Eurasia Championship in turn 6, per the report's own intro; the specific title-deciding bout within the Continental Titles match block is not disambiguated by the report's own text.
reigns.note: “Irish” Mike Flint is the Eurasia Champion in Report #8's own ranking table of 17 February 1991. The change falls inside the unheld Report #7; a gap, not a claim.

reigns.title: wewf-eurasia-championship
reigns.label: “Irish” Mike Flint

won.source: Not directly attested: “Irish” Mike Flint is the Eurasia Champion in Report #8's own ranking table (17 February 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to Destruction.
reigns.note: Won inside the unheld Report #7. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-eurasia-championship
reigns.label: Destruction

won.source: Report #9's own ranking table: “Eurasia Champion: Destruction.”

reigns.how: Lost to AquaDemon.

reigns.title: wewf-eurasia-championship
reigns.label: AquaDemon

won.source: Report #12's own headline: “FireLord's partner, AquaDemon, won the Eurasia Title.”

reigns.how: Beat Destruction, one of two Elementals to take a Continental belt in the same turn.
reigns.note: “Irish” Mike Flint is champion again by Report #15 (7 April 1991). A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-eurasia-championship
reigns.label: “Irish” Mike Flint (second reign)

won.source: Not directly attested: “Irish” Mike Flint is the Eurasia Champion in Report #15's own ranking table (7 April 1991) and holds it through Report #20 (12 May 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.note: BudMan is champion by the week of Report #22, which has the Millionaire taking the belt from him. The change falls inside the unheld Report #21. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-eurasia-championship
reigns.label: BudMan

won.source: Not directly attested: Report #22 records the Millionaire winning the Eurasia Title “from BudMan”, which is the whole of the evidence for BudMan’s own reign. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to the Millionaire.
reigns.note: Won and lost inside eight days, one end of it in an unheld report. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-eurasia-championship
reigns.label: The Millionaire

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “the Millionaire won the Eurasia Title from BudMan!”

reigns.how: Beat BudMan.
reigns.note: The championship does not appear again: the Summer League that began a fortnight later ran three belts only.

reigns.title: wewf-iron-man-trophy
reigns.label: The Big Kahuna

won.source: the wing's own Supercard 5 of 31 July 1991, whose commentary calls him the winner of the previous Supercard's Iron Man Tournament (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-supercard-5-1991-07-31.html)

reigns.how: Won the first Iron Man Tournament, at the Supercard of 30 April 1991, beating the Romulan Mauler in the final round.
reigns.note: Retained the trophy in a four-man round robin against the Executioner, the Plaid Powerhouse and Photon Torpedo, finishing unbeaten at 3-0; he carried the cup onto Malibu's Bikini Shop a fortnight later. Source: the wing's own August Supercard (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-august-supercard-1991-08-31.html).

reigns.title: wewf-six-man-championship
reigns.label: Apocalypse Now

won.source: Report #15's own headline: “Apocalypse Now Take Six Man Belts! The three masked men calling themselves Apocalypse Now beat the Superstars to take the Six Man Titles.”

reigns.how: Lost to the Down-Under Decking Crew.
reigns.note: The championship appears for the first time in the same report that records this reign; whether it existed before is not stated.

reigns.title: wewf-six-man-championship
reigns.label: The Down-Under Decking Crew

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “The Down-Under Decking Crew beat Apocalypse Now for the Six-Man Titles.”

reigns.how: Beat Apocalypse Now.
reigns.note: The last word on the belts is the newsdesk’s own, in Report #38 of 10 November 1991: “Devastation, Inc. still have the WeWF 6-man belts … even though those titles have been retired,” and “they only hold two-thirds. No way would Mr. B give them his third of the title.” The championship was retired with its holders split up.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Dynamic Machine

won.source: The report's own headline: "The Dynamic Machine Regains Tag-Team Belts!"

reigns.how: Regained the Tag Team Championship in turn 6 with 145 points — the league's points-based tag standings, not a single decisive title bout.
reigns.note: The Leaping Lords are the Tag Team Champions in Report #8's own ranking table of 17 February 1991, and its own headline calls that reign a regain. The change falls inside the unheld Report #7; a gap, not a claim.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Leaping Lords

won.source: Not directly attested: the Leaping Lords are the Tag Team Champions in Report #8's own ranking table, and its own headline calls the reign a regain — “The Leaping Lords Regain Tag Belts!” The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to the Maniacs at the league’s own first Supercard.
reigns.note: A regain, so an intervening reign exists that this collection does not hold. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Maniacs

won.source: Report #10's own headline: “The Maniacs beat the Leaping Lords at the Supercard, and then successfully defended the belts this week!”

reigns.how: Lost to Flint and Steel in a very close match.
reigns.note: Won at the league’s own first Supercard, held on Thursday 28 February 1991; the Supercard itself does not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Flint and Steel

won.source: Report #11's own headline: “Flint and Steel Take Tag Titles!”

reigns.how: Beat the Maniacs, then made two more defenses the same turn.
reigns.note: The Intoxicators are champions by Report #15 (7 April 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Reports #13 and #14. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Intoxicators

won.source: Not directly attested: Report #15's own headline has them taking it — “Intoxicators Take Tag Belts! DiMadMan and BudMan beat RnR after the Highlanders had beaten RnR by DQ”. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to Flint and Steel.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Flint and Steel (second held reign)

won.source: Report #16's own headline: “Flint and Steel defeated the Intoxicators to win the Tag Team Titles for the third time!”

reigns.how: Lost to the Law in the Law’s own first defense as a full-time team.
reigns.note: The report calls it their third reign; this collection holds the second and the third but not the first.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Law

won.source: Report #19's own headline: “The Law Takes Tag Titles!”

reigns.how: Lost to the Highlanders.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Highlanders

won.source: Report #20's own headline: “Highlanders Take Tag Belts!”

reigns.how: Lost the belts back to the Law.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Law (second reign)

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “the Law regained the Tag Team Titles from the Highlanders”.

reigns.how: Lost to the Hoosiers in the Hoosiers’ own seventh match as a team.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Hoosiers

won.source: Summer Report #2's own call: “The Hoosiers win the match! We have new champions!”

reigns.how: Lost to Flint and Steel after more than twenty minutes.
reigns.note: The Four Corners laid the new champions and their manager out with the belts themselves minutes after the title change — the ambush that starts the summer’s central feud.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: Flint and Steel (third held reign)

won.source: Summer Report #4's own call: “Flint and Steel win the tag team titles!”

reigns.how: Lost to RnR in the August Supercard main event.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: RnR

won.source: The August Supercard's own call: “RnR are the new WeWF Tag Team Champions!”

reigns.how: Won when both legal men were unconscious and the Millionaire happened to be lying on top of Frank Steel.
reigns.note: The Klingons are champions by Report #37 (28 October 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Reports #33–#36. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Klingons

won.source: Not directly attested: the Klingons are the Tag Team Champions in Report #37's own standings (28 October 1991), and defend the belts in Reports #37 and #38. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Defended against the Maniacs on the Klinshai Bombing, and kept the belts by disqualification against the Hoosiers when their own manager shook the ropes.
reigns.note: The Hoosiers are champions by the newsdesk’s own standings of 30 January 1992. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Hoosiers (second reign)

won.source: Not directly attested: the Hoosiers are the Tag Team Champions in the newsdesk's own WeWF standings of 30 January 1992. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to the Law.
reigns.note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Law (third reign)

won.source: The newsdesk's own call, 15 February 1992: “The winners, and for the third time WeWF Tag Team Champions: The Law!” — a count this ledger's own three reigns for them match exactly.

reigns.how: Judge Dredd cradled Erik while Machiavelli distracted the referee and Judge Anderson shook the top rope to drop Daemon off it.
reigns.note: Still champions at the held record's end, having defended against the Hoosiers and the Cochon Brothers.

reigns.title: wewf-twiw-tv-championship
reigns.label: Mr. B

won.source: Not directly attested: Mr. B is the TWIW TV Champion on the newsdesk's own broadcast of 30 January 1992, and the broadcast of 15 February says he had held it “for the better part of a month.” The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to the Hangman on a flying powerslam off the top turnbuckle, after being hung over the top rope with the Hangman’s own noose while the referee was down.
reigns.note: On 30 January he kept the belt on a disqualification he was himself the subject of, when the guest announcer left the booth to attack the challenger.

reigns.title: wewf-twiw-tv-championship
reigns.label: Hangman

won.source: Now dated from the newsdesk's own broadcast of 15 February 1992: the Hangman hung Mr. B over the top rope with his own noose while the referee was down, then hit a flying powerslam off the top turnbuckle for the three.

reigns.how: Beat Mr. B on the newsdesk's own broadcast of 15 February 1992, and retained against Mr. B again, against Lancelot by countout, against Freddie “Fair Play” Fitness and against Uncle Nasty.
reigns.note: Still champion at the held record's end. THE REIGN'S OWN START WAS UNRECOVERED AND IS NOW DATED from the newsdesk's own broadcast of 15 February 1992; the reigns on this belt were renumbered into date order in the same pass.

reigns.title: wewf-twiw-tv-tag-team-championship
reigns.label: The Annihilation Alliance

won.source: Now dated from the tournament's own final, 31 March 1992: “A quick pin, and we have the first TWIW tag team champions!”

reigns.how: Won the four-round, eight-team TWIW TV Tag Team Title Tournament, beating the WeWF's own tag champions Flint and Steel in the final; retained against Carnage in a steel cage rematch on 13 April.
reigns.note: Still champions at the held record's end. THE REIGN'S OWN START WAS UNRECOVERED AND IS NOW DATED to the tournament final that the 13 April broadcast calls “a rematch of what I call the finals.”

reigns.title: wewf-united-states-championship
reigns.label: Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel”

won.source: Summer Report #1's own call: “Your winner, and new US Champion, Bjorn ‘the Sweedish Pretzel’!”

reigns.how: Won the sixteen-man tournament that created the championship, beating BudMan in the final on his own leglock.
reigns.note: Mr. B is champion by Summer Report #9 (25 August 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Summer Reports #6–#8. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-united-states-championship
reigns.label: Mr. B

won.source: Not directly attested: Mr. B is the United States Champion in Summer Report #9's own standings (25 August 1991), and defends the belt there and at the August Supercard. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” on a sleeper, with Victor Rivera Jr. pulling the ropes out of reach.
reigns.note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-united-states-championship
reigns.label: Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” (second reign)

won.source: Report #32's own call: “Bjorn ‘The Swedish Pretzel’ regains the US Title!”

reigns.how: Lost to the General, who wrestled with his head bandaged from an ambush an hour earlier.

reigns.title: wewf-united-states-championship
reigns.label: The General

won.source: Report #37's own ring call: “Here is your winner, and NEW US CHAMPION, The General!”

reigns.how: Beat Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” on a brainbuster after rolling away from a fistdrop off the top rope.
reigns.note: Black Tiger is champion by the newsdesk’s own standings of 30 January 1992, undefeated at 6-0. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-united-states-championship
reigns.label: Black Tiger

won.source: Not directly attested: Black Tiger is the United States Champion in the newsdesk's own WeWF standings of 30 January 1992, at 6-0. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Defended against “Gentleman” Jim Gilette on a backslide and against Zangief the Terrible on a cradle suplex, and challenged the whole federation to a caged battle royal for the belt.
reigns.note: Still champion at the held record's end, and still unbeaten.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: Volcano

won.source: The report's own words: Volcano "defeated the former champ Joe 'Brick' Wall."

reigns.how: Beat Joe "Brick" Wall for the vacated-by-loss title, defended it against Irving Forbush, "Irish" Mike Flint and Mr. Roddy, then lost it the same turn.
reigns.note: Predecessor reign (Joe "Brick" Wall's own) is not attested in the held record beyond the report's own "the former champ" phrase — a gap, not a claim of a vacant title.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: Juggernaut

won.source: The report's own words: Juggernaut "barely pinned Volcano" to become "the 8th WeWF World Champion."

reigns.how: Barely pinned Volcano.
reigns.note: Held the belt for almost a month, through the unheld Report #7 and a five-defense week in Report #8, before the General beat him by five points in Report #9. The reign's own end is now dated from the wing's own weekly record.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: The General

won.source: Report #9's own headline: “The General beat Juggernaut to become the 10th WeWF World Champion!”

reigns.how: Beat Juggernaut by five points after Photon Torpedo had beaten him by disqualification and “Irish” Mike Flint had taken him to three.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: Frank Steel

won.source: Report #11's own headline: “The Americas Champion, Frank Steel beat the General to win the WeWF World Title!”

reigns.how: Beat the General while holding the Americas Championship, and won the Tag Team Championship with his own partner in the same turn — three belts at once, which is why the Americas Championship was declared vacant.
reigns.note: The report calls it his second reign; the first is not attested in the held record.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: The General (second reign)

won.source: Report #18's own headline: “The General beat Frank Steel to regain the WeWF World Championship!”

reigns.how: Beat an exhausted Frank Steel, who had won only two of his five title matches that week.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: DiMadMan

won.source: Report #19's own headline: “DiMadMan Wins World Title!”

reigns.how: Beat the General, and vacated his own Africa/Australia Championship on winning it.
reigns.note: Still champion in Report #20 (12 May 1991); the General is champion again at the start of Report #22’s own week. The change falls inside the unheld Report #21. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: The General (third reign)

won.source: Not directly attested: the General is the reigning champion at the start of Report #22's own week (26 May 1991), having regained the belt inside the unheld Report #21. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to the Big Kahuna in the first of three title changes inside one week.
reigns.note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: The Big Kahuna

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “The Big Kahuna defeated the General to win the title, but then lost it to Bjorn ‘the Sweedish Pretzel’.”

reigns.how: Beat the General, then lost to Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” the same week.
reigns.note: One of three World Championship changes inside a single week — the only such week in the surviving record.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel”

won.source: Report #22's own headline.

reigns.how: Beat the Big Kahuna, then lost to “Irish” Mike Flint the same week.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: “Irish” Mike Flint

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “‘Irish’ Mike Flint then beat Bjorn to win the WeWF World Championship! This is the second time he has held the belt.”

reigns.how: Beat Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel”, and carried the belt into the Summer League as its own standing champion.
reigns.note: The report calls it his second reign; the first is not attested in the held record.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: The Big Kahuna (second reign)

won.source: Summer Report #4's own call: “The Big Kahuna wins the World Championship back from the man who took it from him right before the Summer League started!”

reigns.how: Beat “Irish” Mike Flint on a big splash, in Flint’s second title match of the same night.
reigns.note: Still champion in Summer Report #5 (28 July 1991); Mr. Roddy is champion by Summer Report #9 (25 August). The change falls inside the unheld Summer Reports #6–#8. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: Mr. Roddy

won.source: Not directly attested: Mr. Roddy is the reigning champion in Summer Report #9's own standings (25 August 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to the General on a bulldog off the top rope.
reigns.note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: The General (fourth reign)

won.source: Report #32's own call: “The General regains the WeWF World Title for an unprecedented fourth time!”

reigns.how: Beat Mr. Roddy on a bulldog off the top rope — the first man to hold the belt four times, ahead of Volcano and “Irish” Mike Flint on three.
reigns.note: Steelgrave is champion by Report #37 (28 October 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Reports #33–#36. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: Steelgrave

won.source: Not directly attested: Steelgrave is the reigning champion in Report #37's own standings (28 October 1991), and defends the belt in Reports #37 and #38. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Defended against the Sandman (by disqualification) and the Millionaire (a power bomb) in the two held reports of his own reign.
reigns.note: Mr. Roddy is champion again by the newsdesk’s own standings of 30 January 1992. The change falls inside the unheld Reports #39–#49. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: Mr. Roddy (second reign)

won.source: Not directly attested: Mr. Roddy is the reigning champion in the newsdesk's own WeWF standings of 30 January 1992. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.note: The Sandman is champion by the newsdesk’s own standings of 15 February 1992. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: The Sandman

won.source: Not directly attested: the Sandman is the reigning champion in the newsdesk's own WeWF standings of 15 February 1992, and Report #50 says he “held that belt for almost a month.” The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

reigns.how: Lost to Metal on a powerslam, with nobody in his corner.
reigns.note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

reigns.title: wewf-world-championship
reigns.label: Metal

won.source: Report #50's own call: “Metal defeats The Sandman to win the WeWF World Title!”

reigns.how: Picked the Sandman up over his shoulder and powerslammed him.
reigns.note: Still champion at the held record's end; no later WeWF report survives.

reigns.title: wfsw-1996-united-states
reigns.label: Mark "The Crippler" Baker

won.source: First attested as champion, already holding the title, in the fed's own 17 April 1996 broadcast (retaining over Gatekeeper); how or when he won it is not captured in the held record.

reigns.note: Booked to defend the title against Harlequin Chaos at a show never recapped in the held record.

reigns.title: wfsw-1996-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Harlequin Tragedy

won.source: The fed's own debut pay-per-view: won a twenty-man battle royal main event, his first-ever match.

reigns.how: Won a twenty-man battle royal main event, 29 January 1996.
reigns.note: No document in the held record records the loss of this title. Outside posts call him a former champion by October 1996, all after the held record ends.

reigns.title: wfsw-1996-world-tag-team
reigns.label: The Returners

won.source: First attested as champions, already holding the belts, in the fed's own 30 April 1996 broadcast (retaining over The Harlequins); how or when they won the belts is not captured in the held record.

reigns.note: A different federation's own later broadcast billed a separate team as holding this same title; that document belongs to the other federation's own record and is not asserted here as a title change.

reigns.title: wfw-1995-usenet-intercontinental
reigns.label: Inferno

won.source: The fed's own 'Summernight Powerslam' supercard: won a battle-royal-qualified final by count-out over Lenny Rose.

reigns.how: Won a twelve-man Battle Royal and its count-out final to become the WFW's first-ever Intercontinental Champion.
reigns.note: Still recognized as champion two days later, successfully defending in a non-title match on the fed's own 'Power Zone' broadcast.

reigns.title: wfw-1995-usenet-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: The Ultimate Fighting Machine

won.source: The fed's own 'Summernight Powerslam' supercard: pinned champion Johnny Banger.

reigns.how: Pinned champion Johnny "the rebel" Banger for the WFW World Championship.
reigns.note: Still champion two days later, successfully defending (non-title) on the fed's own 'Power Zone' broadcast.

reigns.title: wfw-1995-usenet-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Johnny "the rebel" Banger

won.source: Billed the reigning WFW World Champion coming into the fed's own 'Summernight Powerslam' supercard; no title-change document for his own win survives in the held record.

reigns.how: Not recovered — held the title coming into the held record.
reigns.note: Lost the title to the Ultimate Fighting Machine on 5 July 1995.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Diablo

won.source: Handed the title by Shawn Hart on the microphone after Hart won both world titles at the Spirit of NGEN.

lost.source: Lost the title to Rat Fink at NYC Unplugged.

reigns.how: Handed the belt by Shawn Hart, who said Diablo had proved himself worthy of defending it by beating Andre Eian in the flaming-tables match.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Rat Fink

won.source: Won the title from Diablo in a falls-count-anywhere match in Central Park.

lost.source: Lost the title to Felix Red at Turkey Day Terror.

reigns.how: Pinned Diablo with Falcon's Arrow after The American and Fink Bot joined in; he kept the title against Psycho at Almost Live. He kept the title against Pulsar in a Coal Miner's Glove match at Ghoulish Games.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Felix Red

won.source: Won the title from Rat Fink at Turkey Day Terror.

lost.source: Lost the title to Minion at Great Expectations.

reigns.how: Pinned Rat Fink with Ecstasy Through Agony through a table, nineteen minutes in, after two fans, Toxick White and Krist Blue, ran in against Fink's men; he teamed with Richard Gideon as BAD World Heavyweight Champion at Merrython. He kept it against Psycho at Mind Over Matter, when Psycho passed out in his sleeper, and lost it to Minion in a falls-count-anywhere match at Great Expectations.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Minion

won.source: Won the title from Felix Red at Great Expectations.

lost.source: The title was announced vacated at Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux.

reigns.how: Pinned Felix Red with the Fall From Grace in a falls-count-anywhere match at Edison Field, after running through an outfield wall and being cut by Felix Red; the line-up announced at Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux says he vacated the title with a torn ligament in his leg.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jared Wells

won.source: Won the vacant title in a four-man falls count anywhere elimination match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

lost.source: Lost the title to Steve Johnson on 17 April 2007, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

reigns.how: Pinned Rat Fink with the Alabama Jam from the Heavens, after he had pinned Pulsar and Rat Fink had pinned Felix Red; he kept the title against Mike Lane at BOMB Voyage by pulling him overboard. He kept the title against Iron Lion at Cherry Blossom Chaos II with a Rage Bomb off the second rope after chop-blocking the challenger's knee. He lost it to Steve Johnson on 17 April 2007, with DC Statton refereeing, ending a reign of almost three years, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Steve Johnson

won.source: Won the title from Jared Wells on 17 April 2007, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

lost.source: Lost the title to Jared Wells at Unplugged on 31 December 2009, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

reigns.how: Won the title from Jared Wells on 17 April 2007, with DC Statton refereeing, ending Wells's near three-year reign; the fed's own history of the belt gives no finish. He lost it to Wells at Unplugged on 31 December 2009.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Jared Wells

won.source: Won the title from Steve Johnson at Unplugged, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

reigns.how: Beat Steve Johnson at Unplugged on 31 December 2009; the fed's list of 20 January 2010 carried the title and its champion into NGEN.

end.source: The fed's list of its champions of 20 January 2010, served in the NGEN 2010 wing, names Jared Wells the BAD World Heavyweight Champion and says the title would be kept under its name in the fed's relaunch as NGEN, where Wells's reign carries on; this fed's own history of the belt, last edited in May 2010, lists no change after his win at Unplugged.

reigns.note: This wing's record of the title ends on 20 January 2010 with Wells still champion; the title and his reign continue in the NGEN 2010 wing.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american
reigns.label: Michael Manson

won.source: Won the vacant title as the man not pinned in the three-way final at Vox Hiberionacum.

lost.source: Lost the title to Scotty Michaels in a steel cage at the Spirit of NGEN, after Luster's interference.

reigns.how: Left unpinned when Doc Silver pinned Shawn Hart in the three-way final; he kept the title through Rat Fink's theft of the belt at Shock & Awe and a three-way ladder match at Cherry Blossom Chaos.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american
reigns.label: Scotty Michaels

won.source: Won the title from Michael Manson in a steel cage at the Spirit of NGEN.

lost.source: Lost the title to Richard Gideon in a three-way with Felix Red at Ghoulish Games, passing out in Gideon's figure-four leglock.

reigns.how: Pinned Michael Manson with the Viewer's Delight brainbuster after the lights went out and Luster struck Manson with a pipe; he kept the title against Copycat at Almost Live with Luster's brass knuckles.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american
reigns.label: Richard Gideon

won.source: Won the title from Scotty Michaels, with Felix Red also in the match, at Ghoulish Games.

lost.source: Lost the title to Psycho in a two out of three falls match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

reigns.how: Made Scotty Michaels pass out in the figure-four leglock after Michaels' cousin Shawn Matthews hit his injured leg with a chair; he kept the title against Psycho at Turkey Day Terror when Psycho was disqualified for using a fork. He kept the title in a three-way against Copycat and Psycho at Great Expectations, pinning Psycho with the Buffalo Bomb. He lost the title to Psycho at the Superbowl of Wrestling, two falls to one in a match of submissions only, the Four Corners of Hell and a Texas Death Match.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american
reigns.label: Psycho

won.source: Won the title from Richard Gideon in a two out of three falls match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

reigns.how: Won two falls to one in a match of submissions only, the Four Corners of Hell and a Texas Death Match, taking the deciding fall when Gideon could not get up at the ten count; Gideon handed him the belt. He kept the title in the Falls Count Anywhere on the Mall II four-way against Rat Fink, Pulsar and El Arco Iris at Cherry Blossom Chaos II and against Golem at Paradise Lost, where he had cut the first referee open with a fork.
reigns.note: The fed's own list of its North American champions dates this change to 26 April 2004, the day the post telling the deciding fall went up; the first post of the broadcast is dated 18 April 2004, which this record uses.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Doc Silver

won.source: Won the vacant title in the three-way final at Vox Hiberionacum, pinning Shawn Hart.

lost.source: Eliminated from the four-way main event of Cherry Blossom Chaos, in which Psycho won the title.

reigns.how: Pinned Shawn Hart in the three-way final after Rat Fink held Michael Manson's legs from under the ring.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Psycho

won.source: Won the title by pinning Shawn Hart in the final fall of the four-way main event of Cherry Blossom Chaos.

lost.source: Lost the title to Doc Silver in the steel cage of Rage in the Cage.

reigns.how: Pinned Shawn Hart with the Tiger Driver after Doc Silver struck Hart with a steel chair at the Lincoln Memorial.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Doc Silver

won.source: Won the title back from Psycho in the steel cage of Rage in the Cage.

lost.source: Lost the title to Shawn Hart in the Last Man Standing third fall of their best-of-three match at the Spirit of NGEN.

reigns.how: Escaped the razor-wire cage, crawling from under the ring after he and Psycho fell through it.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Shawn Hart

won.source: Won the title from Doc Silver, two falls to one, at the Spirit of NGEN.

lost.source: Lost the title to Scotty Michaels in a Winter Wonderland match in Central Park at Merrython.

reigns.how: Won the third fall, a Last Man Standing match, on Alex Wylde's ten count after Doc Silver's knee buckled; he had taken the first fall in a lumberjack match after Diablo's fireball blinded Silver. He kept the title against Luster at New World Madness and Michael Manson in a Chicago street fight at Ghoulish Games. He lost it to Scotty Michaels in a Winter Wonderland match in Central Park at Merrython, when Luster, in disguise as Michaels' wheelchair-using brother, laid Michaels across Hart for the pin.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Scotty Michaels

won.source: Won the title from Shawn Hart in a Winter Wonderland match in Central Park at Merrython.

lost.source: Lost the title to Sean Edmunds in the Ironman match at Great Expectations, five falls to four.

reigns.how: Pinned Shawn Hart after Minion had hit him with a chair, the wheelchair-using 'Steve Matthews' had jumped up, hit Hart with the wheelchair and laid Michaels across Hart, the man in the movie mask proving to be Luster; Michaels said the brother and his drunken act were a set-up. The Great Expectations commentary says he also defended the title against Minion and Shawn Hart on a GXW card, Battleground Britain, of which this fed's pages carry no account.
reigns.note: The fed's own list of its World Heavyweight champions dates this change to 31 December 2003 and the Edmunds change to 25 February 2004; the first posts of the two broadcasts are dated 30 December 2003 and 18 February 2004, which this record uses.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Sean Edmunds

won.source: Won the title from Scotty Michaels in the Ironman match at Great Expectations, five falls to four.

lost.source: Lost the title to Alex Wylde at Road to Glory.

reigns.how: Won the sixty-minute Ironman match five falls to four, the last fall a Northern Lights suplex with seconds left after Luster hit Michaels with a chair and the special referee, Copycat, kicked Michaels; the fed's roleplay pages later have him taken to hospital with a heart arrhythmia.
reigns.note: The fed's own list of its World Heavyweight champions dates this change to 25 February 2004 and the Wylde change to 21 March 2004; the first posts of the two broadcasts are dated 18 February 2004 and 10 March 2004, which this record uses.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Alex Wylde

won.source: Won the title from Sean Edmunds at Road to Glory.

lost.source: Lost the title to Michael Manson in a ladder match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

reigns.how: Pinned Sean Edmunds with the Gatecrasher superkick after Edmunds, bleeding from the nose, lost his grip on a Northern Lights suplex, the fed's President winning, by the commentary, the first world title of his career; with Pulsar he beat Michael Manson and Rat Fink in a street fight at Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux. He lost it to Michael Manson in a ladder match at the Superbowl of Wrestling, with Joey Melton the special referee.

reigns.title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: Michael Manson

won.source: Won the title from Alex Wylde in a ladder match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

reigns.how: Pulled Alex Wylde off the ladder and took the belt off its hook fifteen feet above the ring, with Joey Melton the special referee; he kept the title against Richard Gideon at BOMB Voyage, the referee calling for the bell at 59 minutes 59 seconds with Gideon in the Tourniquet. He kept the title against Felix Red at Cherry Blossom Chaos II with a clothesline after Red's spinning back kick missed, the referee slow to count in the rain. He kept the title against El Arco Iris at Guerra Interminable, two falls to one under Lucha rules, taking the third fall when Iris tapped to the Tourniquet.
reigns.note: The fed's own list of its World Heavyweight champions dates this change to 29 April 2004, the day the post telling the ladder match went up; the first post of the broadcast is dated 18 April 2004, which this record uses.

won.source: Not attested in this record.

lost.note: Commentary on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast states Speed Racer beat Dragon for the title, without giving a date.

reigns.title: whcw-1996-cruiserweight
reigns.label: Speed Racer

won.source: Won the title from Dragon, per the promotion's own commentary; the date of the win is not given.

reigns.note: Successfully defended the title against “Gimmickless” Gary Garvin at Rumble in the Bronx 2 with a top-rope Flatliner, in 9 minutes 56 seconds.

won.source: Won a five-man steel cage elimination match for the vacant title, outlasting Sennaga Cortez, the Inferno Kid, Guy LaChance and Hooligan.

reigns.title: whcw-1996-extreme
reigns.label: Doomsday

won.source: Referenced only in passing on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast, as the standard the new champion was compared against.

lost.note: Not attested in this record; the title was vacant by the time of this broadcast.

reigns.note: Commentary calls this new champion unlikely to 'live up to Doomsday's reign,' the only evidence for it in this record.

reigns.title: whcw-1996-north-american
reigns.label: “Casanova” Chris Tyler

won.source: Reached the vacant title first during an unsanctioned construction-site brawl and had the win confirmed by the promotion's own president over the phone, on the same broadcast.

reigns.note: No stipulation had named a formal winner for the title inside the brawl itself; the promotion's own president ruled on it afterward.

reigns.title: whcw-1996-north-american
reigns.label: Kensai Akira

won.source: Billed on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast as a former WHCW North American Champion.

lost.note: Not attested in this record.

reigns.note: How and when the reign ended is not given; the title was vacant by the time of this broadcast.

won.source: Won the WHCW North American Tag Team Championship from the Sociopaths after revealing themselves from beneath a disguise.
Billed on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast as the reigning WHCW North American Tag Team Champions entering the card.

lost.source: Pinned by the returning Ultranationalists after a backstage beatdown left them battered before the bell.

reigns.title: whcw-1996-world
reigns.label: Adonis Mercury

won.source: Billed on the promotion's own Rumble in the Bronx 2 broadcast as a five-time former WHCW World Champion, with individual reign dates not given.

lost.note: Mercury's own on-air account blames a contract dispute engineered by the promotion's president for costing him the title, rather than a match.

reigns.note: The promotion's own broadcast does not name a wrestler holding the title after Mercury; its status is not attested in this record.

reigns.title: whw-united-states
reigns.label: "Wildchild" Ryan Decker

won.source: Held entering the fed's own February Massacre card; the held record does not show when or how he won it.

reigns.note: Retained the title over Pitbull in a ladder match at February Massacre; the held record does not trace the reign further.

reigns.title: whw-world-heavyweight
reigns.label: "Iron" Mike Austin

won.source: /promotions/whw/archive/whw-february-massacre-1997-03-03.html

reigns.note: Won a steel-cage main event over Curt X; the held record does not trace the reign further.
reigns.notes: End of reign unrecorded (unrecorded). Event: WHW February Massacre

reigns.title: wia97-heavyweight
reigns.label: Spangler

won.source: Dated only as reigning champion as of his own 21 September 1997 promo; no title-change document survives.

reigns.note: Gap-registered: the reign's start is not attested in the held record.

reigns.how: Won a 10-man over-the-top-rope battle royal to become the fed's own first WICeW Cruiserweight Champion.
reigns.label: Gangsta New Jack
reigns.title: wicew-cruiserweight

won.source: promotions/wicew/archive/results-1998-10-04.html

reigns.note: First-ever holder of this title. How and when he lost the title to the next attested holder, Blizzard (circa 10 December 1998), does not survive in this capture.

reigns.how: Held as of the fed's own 10 December 1998 championship snapshot.
reigns.label: Blizzard
reigns.title: wicew-cruiserweight

won.source: promotions/wicew/archive/champions.html

reigns.how: Defeated the champion, Sean "Iceman" Stevens, in a time of 19:45, to become new champion.
reigns.label: Volcano
reigns.title: wicew-european

won.source: promotions/wicew/archive/results-1998-11-08.html

reigns.note: The fed's own first-ever European Title match was billed for an unheld Thursday Night House Show following the 4 October 1998 card, between Arch Angel and "Superstar" Steve Taylor (both now minted; see characters.json) -- not itself captured in this holding, and its own winner is not recorded. Sean "Iceman" Stevens is independently minted (sean-iceman-stevens-wicew) and billed as champion here, but his own path to the title between that Thursday match and this 8 November defense is unrecorded -- he is NOT asserted to be the title's first champion. How and when Volcano lost the title to the next attested holder, Kyle Barrows (circa 10 December 1998), does not survive in this capture.

reigns.how: Held as of the fed's own 10 December 1998 championship snapshot.
reigns.label: Kyle Barrows

reigns.how: John Grant made WWA history when he tigerbombed RJ Stone in the middle of the ring to pick up the United States title. He became the youngest champion in the storied tenure of the WWA. reigns.note: Sources disagree on the pairing. WWA's own title history names the first champions as the Outlaw and The Executive. WWA's own served card of 9 January 1998 (wwa-1997-01-09, promotions/wwa/archive/1997-01-09.html) bills the belt as the CWC Northeast Tag Team Championship and has The Executive and Mr. Business win it: the pair come through a four-corners first round, then pin Triple Threat in the tournament's final, and the commentary calls them "the new and first Northeast Tag Champions"; the Outlaw hosts the night's Saloon segment and does not wrestle in the tournament. The cards of 14 January and 6 February 1998 also bring The Executive and Mr. Business out as the champions, and the card of 6 February 1998 (wwa-1998-02-06) has them lose the belts to the Commandant's Own. Both readings are recorded. The pair is filed as its own tag team, The Executive and Mr. Business (the-executive-and-mr-business-wwa), the Executive's Club being the stable they belong to (the-executives-club-wwa): the card of 9 January 1998 bills them "the Executive and Mr. Business of the Executive's Club" and the card of 14 January 1998, where they retain the belts over Matt Sanders and Canuck (Mr. Business pins Canuck with the Claw), brings them out "with their tag belts strung over their shoulders"; WWA's own title history carries the reign under the club's name.

reigns.note: CORRECTS the ledger's compiled note. The primary broadcast, read cover to cover, shows Studd was a no-show for the announced IP title match; the WWO's on-air president character declares Massacre "the official winner of this match" and hands him the newly-restored IP belt by decree — not by pinning or submitting Studd, who never appears in the segment at all. In the SAME ring segment, Massacre separately relinquishes his own WWO Extreme Championship, framed in his own words as personal ("I need to get rid of something, not only as a conscience..."), immediately after signing a new WWO contract — no narration ties the vacating of the Extreme title to the awarding of the IP belt as one "unification" transaction; they are two adjacent beats in the same segment, not one bout deciding both belts. This leaves the WWO Extreme Championship VACANT as of this date, a fact not reflected anywhere in the currently-held Extreme title reigns — NOT corrected here.

reigns.note: The ledger gives no location. This reign (Andros over King $$$ Perfect) cannot be the same reign a 26 May 1997 broadcast (msg_id ylIv784kiMwJ) reports Andros reclaiming. This note narrows r003's own window. It does not change r003's won.date, which stays year-precision. The tournament's own semifinals and final were held the same night, at Battle of the Titans IV (18 Apr 1997). Underground Kingpin beat "Terrible" Travis Lee in one semifinal, Andros beat Jack "Tower of Terror" Harper in the other (msg_id dcyEFh4s03UJ, read cover to cover), and Kingpin then beat Andros in the final for the vacant title itself (r020). This means r003's own 'Andros defeated King $$$ Perfect' bout, whatever its date, is very likely an EARLIER round of this SAME tournament, not a genuine championship reign. Andros never held the belt as champion at all under this reading. He reached the final and lost it there. r003's won.date can honestly be stated only as 'sometime in the Jan-Apr 1997 tournament window,' and its status as a 'reign' (rather than a bracket-advancement record inherited uncritically from the fed's own imprecise title-history ledger) is now in real doubt. Flagged as a structural question for the dedicated WWO reconciliation pass, not resolved by this patch.

reigns.note: A primary-source discrepancy: the fed's own title-history ledger credits Natalya Neidhart with defeating all six other women in one elimination match, but the served Genesis show text instead depicts Madusa Miceli winning that six-way elimination outright, only to be jumped afterward by Victoria & Natalya Neidhart and forced to submit to a Camel Clutch — after which GM Eric Bischoff simply presented the belt to Natalya. Both primary sources are on record; the ledger's own holder (Natalya) is kept as the reign of record since that is how the belt was actually presented in-fiction, with this note carrying the served show's own contrary blow-by-blow rather than silently picking a side.
